concepts.name: Newton's Second Law (F = ma)
concepts.explanation: The net force on an object equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration; allows calculation of acceleration or force for linear motion.

concepts.name: Newton's First Law (Inertia)
concepts.explanation: An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a resultant external force; defines the concept of inertia.

concepts.name: Newton's Third Law (Action–Reaction)
concepts.explanation: For every force exerted by object A on object B there is an equal and opposite force exerted by B on A; forces occur in pairs.

concepts.name: Velocity (average and instantaneous)
concepts.explanation: Displacement per unit time (vector); average velocity over an interval and instantaneous velocity at a moment, distinct from speed.

concepts.name: Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of velocity with time; can be constant (uniformly accelerated motion) or variable.

concepts.name: Kinematic equations for constant acceleration
concepts.explanation: Equations relating displacement, initial/final velocity, acceleration and time for uniformly accelerated linear motion (e.g., v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2).

concepts.name: Electric current (I)
concepts.explanation: Rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes; direction convention and measurement with ammeters.

concepts.name: Potential difference (Voltage)
concepts.explanation: Work done per unit charge in moving a charge between two points; measured in volts and produced by sources like cells and batteries.

concepts.name: Resistance and Ohm's Law (V = IR)
concepts.explanation: Electrical resistance opposes current; for ohmic conductors voltage across a resistor is proportional to current with constant R.

concepts.name: Series and parallel circuits
concepts.explanation: Arrangement of circuit elements that determines how current and voltage divide; series add resistances, parallel provides alternative paths.

concepts.name: Domestic electricity and safety (fuses, earthing, circuit breakers)
concepts.explanation: Principles of household wiring, protective devices and safety practices to prevent overloads, shocks and fires.

concepts.name: Wave properties and the wave equation (v = fλ)
concepts.explanation: Fundamental properties of waves: wavelength, frequency, amplitude, period, and the relation linking wave speed, frequency and wavelength.

concepts.name: Sound: pitch, loudness and speed of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave; pitch relates to frequency, loudness to amplitude, and speed depends on medium and temperature.

concepts.name: Reflection of light (laws of reflection and plane mirror images)
concepts.explanation: Incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in one plane; angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; image formation in plane mirrors.

concepts.name: Refraction and Snell's Law
concepts.explanation: Bending of light when passing between media with different refractive indices; n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2 and concept of critical angle/total internal reflection.

concepts.name: Lenses and image formation (lens equation 1/f = 1/v + 1/u)
concepts.explanation: Converging/diverging lenses form real or virtual images; lens formula and magnification relate object distance, image distance and focal length.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Amount of thermal energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one degree; used in heat capacity calculations.

concepts.name: Modes of heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation
concepts.explanation: Three mechanisms by which thermal energy moves: conduction through solids, convection in fluids, and thermal radiation via electromagnetic waves.

concepts.name: Atomic model and energy levels (basic)
concepts.explanation: Basic atomic structure concepts including discrete energy levels and electron transitions that explain line spectra and simple atomic behavior.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.explanation: Vector measure of change of position; includes magnitude and direction, with SI unit metre (m).

concepts.name: Velocity
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of displacement (vector); distinguishes average and instantaneous velocity; units m s^-1 and represented on distance–time and velocity–time graphs.

concepts.name: Equations of motion (constant acceleration)
concepts.explanation: Kinematic relations connecting displacement, initial/final velocity, acceleration and time for constant acceleration (used to solve linear motion problems).

concepts.name: Vector vs Scalar quantities in mechanics
concepts.explanation: Distinction between vector quantities (magnitude and direction; e.g., displacement, velocity, acceleration, force) and scalar quantities (magnitude only; e.g., speed, mass).

concepts.name: Measurement of velocity and acceleration (graphs and timers)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedures and interpretation of distance–time and velocity–time graphs using apparatus such as ticker-tape, air track, or timers to determine velocity and acceleration.

concepts.name: Newton's First Law (law of inertia)
concepts.explanation: A body remains at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted on by a net external force; foundation for understanding equilibrium and forces.

concepts.name: Newton's Third Law (action and reaction)
concepts.explanation: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction; forces between two interacting bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

concepts.name: Force (definition and vector nature)
concepts.explanation: An interaction that can change the motion of an object; a vector quantity with SI unit newton (N); includes contact and non-contact forces.

concepts.name: Momentum (p = mv)
concepts.explanation: Product of mass and velocity; vector quantity conserved in isolated systems; units kg m s^-1.

concepts.name: Conservation of momentum
concepts.explanation: Total momentum of an isolated system remains constant; applied to collisions and recoil problems (vector addition of momenta).

concepts.name: Friction
concepts.explanation: Force opposing relative motion between surfaces; includes static and kinetic friction and has practical implications (walking, lubrication).

concepts.name: Newton's law of universal gravitation
concepts.explanation: Gravitational force between two masses: F = G m1 m2 / r^2; explains attraction between masses and orbital effects.

concepts.name: Weight and gravitational acceleration (W = mg; g on other bodies)
concepts.explanation: Weight is the force due to gravity on a mass (W = mg); gravitational acceleration g varies for different celestial bodies and affects weight calculations.

concepts.name: Measurement of g (experimental methods)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedures to determine local g (e.g., pendulum period, free-fall timing, ticker-tape/air track methods) and calculations from kinematic data.

concepts.name: Density
concepts.explanation: Mass per unit volume (ρ = m/V); distinguishes materials and is used in buoyancy and pressure calculations; SI unit kg m^-3.

concepts.name: Pressure in liquids and gases
concepts.explanation: Force per unit area in fluids; includes hydrostatic pressure variation with depth, atmospheric pressure and related measurements (Pa).

concepts.name: Boyle's Law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of ideal gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (P ∝ 1/V); used in gas pressure problems.

concepts.name: Archimedes' Principle
concepts.explanation: A body immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of fluid displaced; basis for flotation and buoyancy calculations.

concepts.name: Law of flotation
concepts.explanation: Floating bodies displace a weight of fluid equal to their own weight; determines how and why objects float at particular depths.

concepts.name: Hydrometer (use to measure fluid density)
concepts.explanation: Instrument that floats at a depth depending on fluid density; practical procedure for determining specific gravity of liquids.

concepts.name: Moment (torque), lever and couple
concepts.explanation: Moment is turning effect of a force about a pivot (moment = force × perpendicular distance); includes concepts of levers and couples in equilibrium problems.

concepts.name: Conditions for equilibrium
concepts.explanation: Static equilibrium conditions: vector sum of forces equals zero and sum of moments about any point equals zero; applied to rigid bodies in balance.

concepts.name: Work
concepts.explanation: Work done by a force is the product of the component of force along displacement and the displacement (W = F·s); measured in joules (J).

concepts.name: Energy (mechanical)
concepts.explanation: Forms include kinetic and potential energy; energy can be transformed between forms and conserved in isolated systems (basic conservation concepts).

concepts.name: Power
concepts.explanation: Rate at which work is done or energy is transferred (P = W/t); practical calculations for devices and efficiency considerations.

concepts.name: Demonstration of atmospheric pressure (collapsing-can experiment)
concepts.explanation: Practical demonstration showing effects of external atmospheric pressure when internal pressure is reduced, illustrating existence and magnitude of atmospheric pressure.

concepts.name: Use of air track or ticker-tape to demonstrate Newton's laws
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedures using low-friction tracks or timers to observe uniform motion, acceleration under known forces and collisions to illustrate Newtonian dynamics and conservation laws.

concepts.name: Energy (definition and unit)
concepts.explanation: Energy defined as the capacity to do work; SI unit is the joule (J).

concepts.name: Work done by a constant force (force and displacement in same direction)
concepts.explanation: Work W equals the product of a constant force and the displacement in the same direction: W = F s (special case of W = F s cosθ when θ = 0).

concepts.name: Gravitational potential energy (Ep = mgh)
concepts.explanation: Gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface given by Ep = m g h, where m is mass, g is gravitational acceleration, h is height.

concepts.name: Kinetic energy (Ek = 1/2 mv^2)
concepts.explanation: Translational kinetic energy of a mass m moving at speed v: Ek = 1/2 m v^2.

concepts.name: Principle of conservation of energy
concepts.explanation: In an isolated system, the total energy remains constant — energy can be converted between forms but not created or destroyed.

concepts.name: Forms of energy
concepts.explanation: Identification of different energy forms (e.g., kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, thermal, electrical, radiant) and their distinguishing characteristics.

concepts.name: Energy conversion (demonstrations and analysis)
concepts.explanation: Understanding and demonstrating conversion between energy forms (e.g., chemical → electrical → light, electrical → mechanical) and identifying input/output forms in simple devices.

concepts.name: Experiments with bulbs and motors to show energy conversion
concepts.explanation: Simple laboratory demonstrations using bulbs and motors to illustrate electrical-to-light and electrical-to-mechanical energy conversions and associated measurements.

concepts.name: Power (definition, formula and unit)
concepts.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work or the rate of energy transfer: P = W/t or P = ΔE/Δt; SI unit is the watt (W) = J/s.

concepts.name: Estimating average power in everyday activities
concepts.explanation: Procedure to estimate average power output for tasks (e.g., a person running upstairs or repeatedly lifting weights) by computing work (ΔEp = m g Δh) and dividing by time: Pavg = ΔE/Δt.

concepts.name: Percentage efficiency (η = (power output / power input) × 100%)
concepts.explanation: Definition and calculation of efficiency as the percentage of input power converted to useful output power: η = (Pout / Pin) × 100%.

concepts.name: Mass–energy equivalence (E = mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Concept from modern physics that mass and energy are equivalent, related by E = m c^2, where c is the speed of light.

concepts.name: Newton's Second Law (a ∝ F, F = ma)
concepts.explanation: The relationship between net force, mass, and acceleration; experimentally shows acceleration is proportional to applied force and inversely proportional to mass (F = ma).

concepts.name: Conservation of Linear Momentum
concepts.explanation: The principle that the total linear momentum of an isolated system remains constant in the absence of external forces; verified through collision experiments (elastic and inelastic).

concepts.name: Equilibrium of Coplanar Forces
concepts.explanation: Conditions for static equilibrium for a set of forces acting in a single plane: vector sum of forces equals zero (and moments balanced) for a body at rest.

concepts.name: Measurement of Velocity
concepts.explanation: Experimental methods to determine linear velocity (average and, where applicable, instantaneous) from measurements of displacement and time using timers, photogates, or motion sensors.

concepts.name: Measurement of Acceleration
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of linear acceleration from changes in velocity over time, including methods for constant-acceleration motion and data analysis to extract acceleration values.

concepts.name: Measurement of Gravitational Acceleration (g)
concepts.explanation: Procedures to determine the local acceleration due to gravity (g) using free-fall timing, simple pendulum period, or other experimental setups and data analysis.

concepts.name: Boyle's Law (Pressure-Volume Relationship)
concepts.explanation: The inverse relationship between pressure and volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature (PV = constant); experimentally verified by measuring pressure and volume changes.

concepts.name: Concept of temperature
concepts.explanation: Temperature as a quantitative measure of how hot or cold a body is, related to the average kinetic energy of particles and the direction of heat flow.

concepts.name: Zeroth law of thermodynamics (thermal equilibrium)
concepts.explanation: If two bodies are each in thermal equilibrium with a third body, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other; this principle defines temperature and allows use of thermometers.

concepts.name: Temperature scales and conversion (Celsius and Kelvin)
concepts.explanation: Definitions of Celsius and Kelvin scales and conversion between them (T(K) = T(°C) + 273.15); understanding of scale zero points and units.

concepts.name: Difference between heat and temperature
concepts.explanation: Distinguishing heat (energy transferred due to temperature difference, measured in joules) from temperature (intensive property indicating thermal state), including examples.

concepts.name: Thermometry: liquid-in-glass thermometer
concepts.explanation: Operation and use of a liquid-in-glass thermometer: thermal expansion of a contained liquid in a capillary indicates temperature on a calibrated scale; reading technique and common errors.

concepts.name: Thermometric property
concepts.explanation: A physical property that changes with temperature (e.g., length, volume, electrical resistance) used as the basis of a thermometer.

concepts.name: Fixed points and calibration of thermometers
concepts.explanation: Use of reproducible fixed points (e.g., ice point, steam point) to calibrate thermometers and define scale markings; procedure for marking and linear interpolation.

concepts.name: Absolute zero and significance
concepts.explanation: Concept of absolute zero (0 K) as the lower limit of thermodynamic temperature where particle kinetic energy is minimal; its place on the Kelvin scale and implications.

concepts.name: Accuracy, precision and uncertainty in temperature measurement
concepts.explanation: Understanding sources of error in temperature measurement (parallax, calibration, response time), reporting uncertainty and distinguishing accuracy from precision.

concepts.name: Temperature (measure of hotness)
concepts.explanation: Macroscopic quantity that indicates how hot or cold a body is; in kinetic theory it is proportional to the average kinetic energy of particles and is measured on an absolute scale (Kelvin) or practical scales (Celsius).

concepts.name: Graduation (calibration) of thermometers using ice and steam points
concepts.explanation: Procedure to calibrate thermometers by fixing two reproducible reference points (ice point and steam point of water) and assigning temperatures, then linearly interpolating between them to create a scale (practical Celsius calibration).

concepts.name: Liquid-in-glass thermometer (mercury column length)
concepts.explanation: Thermometer that uses thermal expansion of a liquid in a capillary: temperature change causes a measurable change in the length (height) of the liquid column which is related to temperature via calibration.

concepts.name: Thermocouple (EMF as thermometric property)
concepts.explanation: Thermocouple operation based on the Seebeck effect: a junction of two different metals produces an electromotive force proportional to the temperature difference between junctions, used to measure temperature.

concepts.name: Resistance thermometry (thermistors and RTDs)
concepts.explanation: Temperature measurement method using materials whose electrical resistance changes with temperature; resistance is measured and converted to temperature using calibration curves or known R(T) relationships.

concepts.name: Constant-volume gas thermometer (pressure vs temperature)
concepts.explanation: Gas thermometer where the gas volume is held constant so that the pressure is proportional to absolute temperature (ideal gas relation p ∝ T); used as a primary standard for temperature measurement.

concepts.name: Constant-pressure gas thermometer (volume vs temperature)
concepts.explanation: Gas thermometer operated at constant pressure so that the gas volume varies proportionally with absolute temperature (V ∝ T), providing a thermometric method based on gas expansion.

concepts.name: Colour (optical/radiation thermometry)
concepts.explanation: Use of emitted radiation colour or intensity (principles of blackbody radiation and pyrometry) as a thermometric property to infer temperature of hot objects without contact.

concepts.name: Comparison and intercalibration of thermometers
concepts.explanation: Experimental skill of comparing readings from two or more thermometers for the same unknown temperature to assess agreement, systematic differences, precision, and accuracy.

concepts.name: Temperature
concepts.explanation: A thermodynamic quantity that measures the hotness or coldness of a body; the macroscopic parameter that determines heat flow direction between systems.

concepts.name: Kelvin (SI unit of temperature)
concepts.explanation: The SI base unit for temperature; an absolute temperature scale where 0 K is absolute zero and increments are the same size as Celsius degrees.

concepts.name: Temperature scale (linear scale between reference points)
concepts.explanation: A method of assigning numerical temperature values by drawing a straight-line (linear) relationship between established reference (fixed) points and interpolating values between them (e.g., Celsius scale).

concepts.name: Fixed points for thermometer calibration (ice and steam points)
concepts.explanation: Standard reference states (commonly the ice point and steam point of water) used to calibrate thermometers and define temperature scales by assigning agreed numerical values to those points.

concepts.name: Kelvin (unit of temperature)
concepts.explanation: The SI base unit of temperature; an absolute scale where 0 K corresponds to absolute zero and intervals equal those of the Celsius degree.

concepts.name: Celsius scale
concepts.explanation: A practical temperature scale defined by the size of the degree equal to the kelvin and historically anchored so that 0°C is the freezing point and 100°C the boiling point of water at standard pressure.

concepts.name: Triple point of water
concepts.explanation: The unique temperature and pressure at which water's solid, liquid, and vapor phases coexist in equilibrium; historically used as a fixed point in defining the kelvin.

concepts.name: Temperature scale (Celsius and Kelvin)
concepts.explanation: Systems for quantifying temperature: Celsius (°C) uses the freezing and boiling points of water as references, while Kelvin (K) is an absolute scale with 0 K at absolute zero.

concepts.name: Celsius–Kelvin conversion
concepts.explanation: The relation between Celsius and Kelvin: t(°C) = T(K) − 273.15 (equivalently T(K) = t(°C) + 273.15), used to convert temperatures between the two scales.

concepts.name: Temperature measurement (Thermometry)
concepts.explanation: The procedures and principles for determining temperature, including concepts of calibration, accuracy, resolution, and use of different temperature scales (e.g., Celsius, Kelvin).

concepts.name: Thermometer
concepts.explanation: An instrument used to measure temperature, such as liquid-in-glass thermometers, digital thermometers (thermistors, thermocouples), with operation based on thermal expansion or temperature-dependent electrical properties.

concepts.name: Thermometer calibration and comparison
concepts.explanation: Procedures for comparing and calibrating thermometers, including use of fixed points (e.g., ice point, steam point), adjustment for systematic offsets, and establishing a common scale so different devices give comparable readings.

concepts.name: Thermal contact and equilibration time
concepts.explanation: Concept and practice that thermometers must be placed in good thermal contact with the measured system and allowed sufficient time to reach thermal equilibrium; influenced by thermal conductivity, heat capacity, and probe design.

concepts.name: Temperature (definition and measurable quantity)
concepts.explanation: The physical quantity that indicates how hot or cold an object is, related to the average kinetic energy of particles and measurable with a thermometer.

concepts.name: Thermometer (device and reading)
concepts.explanation: A device for measuring temperature; includes understanding types (mercury, alcohol, digital), how to read scales, and proper use in experiments.

concepts.name: Standard thermometer (school reference instrument)
concepts.explanation: The practice of designating a single, reliable commercial laboratory thermometer as the reference instrument for a school to ensure consistent temperature measurements across experiments.

concepts.name: Calibration and standardization of thermometers
concepts.explanation: Procedures to check and adjust thermometers against known fixed points or a chosen school standard to ensure accuracy and inter-comparability of temperature readings.

concepts.name: Heat (thermal energy)
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred between systems or objects because of a temperature difference; flows from hotter to colder bodies and changes a body's internal energy or does work.

concepts.name: Thermal equilibrium
concepts.explanation: Condition in which two or more objects in thermal contact exchange no net heat because they are at the same temperature (basis of the zeroth law of thermodynamics).

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one kelvin; used in Q = mcΔT for calculating heat transfer during temperature changes.

concepts.name: Latent heat (fusion and vaporisation)
concepts.explanation: Heat energy absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature; quantified by Q = mL where L is latent heat of fusion or vaporisation.

concepts.name: Conduction
concepts.explanation: Mode of heat transfer through a material due to microscopic collisions and energy exchange between particles or free electrons; depends on material, cross-sectional area, thickness and temperature difference.

concepts.name: Thermal conductivity and steady-state heat flow
concepts.explanation: Quantitative description of conduction: material property k that relates steady-state heat flow to area, temperature difference and thickness, often expressed as Q/t = kA(ΔT)/L.

concepts.name: Convection
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer in fluids by the bulk movement of the fluid: natural (buoyancy-driven) or forced (external means like a pump or fan), important in heat transport in liquids and gases.

concepts.name: Radiation
concepts.explanation: Transfer of energy by electromagnetic waves emitted by all bodies; can transfer heat through a vacuum; qualitative links to emissivity and the Stefan–Boltzmann concept at more advanced level.

concepts.name: Calorimetry (mixing and measurement of heat)
concepts.explanation: Experimental techniques using calorimeters to measure heat transfer, specific heat capacities or latent heats by applying conservation of energy: heat lost = heat gained (accounting for calorimeter).

concepts.name: Thermal expansion (linear)
concepts.explanation: Increase in linear dimensions of solids with temperature change, characterized by the linear expansion coefficient α and relation ΔL = αLΔT; explains practical effects like gaps in rails.

concepts.name: Quantity of heat (Q)
concepts.explanation: The amount of thermal energy transferred between systems as a result of a temperature difference; typically denoted Q and measured in joules (or calories); a path-dependent scalar that quantifies heat transfer.

concepts.name: Units and conversion of heat (joule, calorie)
concepts.explanation: Standard units used to express quantity of heat (joule in SI, calorie in older conventions) and the conversion factor between them (1 cal = 4.184 J); includes use of unit consistency in heat calculations.

concepts.name: Heat capacity (C)
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of an object by one degree (C = Q/ΔT); an extensive property depending on mass and material.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity (c) and formula Q = mcΔT
concepts.explanation: Material property giving heat required per unit mass per degree change (c = Q/(mΔT)); used in calculations of heat exchanged for homogeneous substances via Q = m c ΔT.

concepts.name: Calorimetry (measurement of heat)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to measure heat transfer using a calorimeter (e.g., mixing method, measuring temperature change and applying Q conservation) to determine specific heats or heat of reactions.

concepts.name: Heat (thermal energy transfer)
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred between systems or objects due to a temperature difference, measured in joules and distinct from internal energy and temperature.

concepts.name: Temperature (measure of thermal state)
concepts.explanation: A scalar quantity that indicates the average kinetic energy of particles in a substance and determines direction of heat flow; measured in °C, K or °F.

concepts.name: Internal energy
concepts.explanation: Total microscopic energy of a system including kinetic and potential energies of particles, which changes when heat is added or work is done.

concepts.name: Thermal equilibrium (zeroth law concept)
concepts.explanation: State in which two objects in contact exchange no net heat and thus have the same temperature; basis for thermometers and temperature scales.

concepts.name: Heat capacity
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of an object or system by one degree (extensive), measured in J/K.

concepts.name: Calorimetry (experimental heat measurement)
concepts.explanation: Procedures and apparatus (e.g., calorimeter) used to measure heat transfer and specific heats by monitoring temperature changes and applying energy conservation.

concepts.name: Latent heat (fusion and vaporization)
concepts.explanation: Heat absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature per unit mass, described by Q = mL_f (fusion) or Q = mL_v (vaporization).

concepts.name: Conduction (heat transfer by contact)
concepts.explanation: Transfer of thermal energy through a material via microscopic collisions and vibrations of particles; described macroscopically by Fourier's law (heat flux ∝ temperature gradient).

concepts.name: Convection (heat transfer by fluid motion)
concepts.explanation: Transfer of heat by the bulk movement of fluid (liquid or gas), including natural (buoyancy-driven) and forced convection mechanisms.

concepts.name: Thermal radiation (electromagnetic emission)
concepts.explanation: Emission of electromagnetic waves due to the thermal motion of charges in matter; described for ideal bodies by the Stefan–Boltzmann law and wavelength distribution by Planck's law.

concepts.name: Thermal expansion
concepts.explanation: Increase in dimensions or volume of materials with temperature; characterized by linear and volumetric expansion coefficients and useful in explaining structural effects of heating.

concepts.name: First law of thermodynamics (energy conservation for thermal systems)
concepts.explanation: Statement that the change in internal energy of a system equals heat added to the system minus work done by the system: ΔU = Q − W, applied to closed and open processes.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity (specific heat)
concepts.explanation: The amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one degree; c = Q / (m ΔT), units J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹. Used to compare thermal inertia of materials and in calorimetry calculations.

concepts.name: Heat
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred between systems or bodies due to a temperature difference; relates macroscopic thermal interactions and transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, radiation).

concepts.name: Latent heat
concepts.explanation: Heat absorbed or released during a phase change at constant temperature (e.g., fusion, vaporization) without changing temperature; typically expressed per unit mass (J/kg).

concepts.name: Specific latent heat
concepts.explanation: The amount of energy required to change the phase of 1 kilogram of a substance at constant temperature (e.g., melting or vaporization); given by L = Q/m and expressed in J/kg.

concepts.name: Temperature versus Heat
concepts.explanation: Distinction between temperature (a measure of average kinetic energy of particles) and heat (energy transfer); includes concepts of thermal equilibrium and thermometer-based measurement.

concepts.name: Heat transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, radiation)
concepts.explanation: The three fundamental processes by which heat is transferred: conduction (through material contact), convection (via fluid motion), and radiation (electromagnetic emission), with qualitative descriptions and basic governing factors.

concepts.name: Heat Transfer
concepts.explanation: The study of how thermal energy moves between systems or within a body by conduction, convection, and radiation; includes quantitative description and energy balance approaches.

concepts.name: Thermal Radiation
concepts.explanation: Emission and transfer of energy through electromagnetic radiation from bodies due to their temperature; described by laws such as Stefan–Boltzmann (P = εσAT^4) and concepts of emissivity and absorptivity.

concepts.name: Thermal Energy Storage
concepts.explanation: Methods and principles for storing thermal energy, including sensible heat storage (changing temperature) and latent heat storage (phase change materials), important for managing heat supply and demand.

concepts.name: Specific heat capacity and heat calculations (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Material-specific quantity relating heat added or removed to mass and temperature change; use Q = m c ΔT to compute thermal energy change.

concepts.name: Conduction (mode of heat transfer)
concepts.explanation: Transfer of heat through a material or between materials in direct contact via microscopic collisions and energy transfer between particles.

concepts.name: Convection (mode of heat transfer)
concepts.explanation: Bulk movement of fluid (liquid or gas) carrying thermal energy, including natural (buoyancy-driven) and forced convection.

concepts.name: Thermal radiation (infrared emission)
concepts.explanation: Emission of electromagnetic radiation due to the temperature of a body; radiative heat transfer that does not require a medium.

concepts.name: Rate of heat transfer / thermal power (P = Q/t)
concepts.explanation: Rate at which thermal energy is transferred or delivered; P = Q/t relates energy transfer Q to time t; relevant for heater performance and transient problems.

concepts.name: Resistive (Joule) heating — electrical to thermal energy conversion
concepts.explanation: Conversion of electrical energy into heat through electrical resistance; power dissipated as heat given by P = I^2R = VI.

concepts.name: Heater power rating and energy consumption (kW, kWh)
concepts.explanation: Specification of a heater's instantaneous power (kW) and the energy consumed over time (kWh); used for sizing and cost calculations.

concepts.name: Thermal insulation and heat loss reduction
concepts.explanation: Materials and design principles that reduce heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) to limit unwanted energy loss.

concepts.name: U-value (thermal transmittance)
concepts.explanation: Rate of heat transfer through a building element per unit area per unit temperature difference (units W·m⁻²·K⁻¹); measures insulation quality.

concepts.name: Calculating heat loss using U-values (domestic situations)
concepts.explanation: Procedure for estimating steady-state heat loss through walls, roofs, windows or whole buildings using area × U-value × temperature difference to inform insulation/energy decisions.

concepts.name: Refrigeration cycle (vapour-compression)
concepts.explanation: The thermodynamic cycle used in common refrigerators and heat pumps involving evaporation, compression, condensation and expansion to transfer heat from cold to hot reservoirs.

concepts.name: Heat pump (principle and applications, e.g., refrigerator)
concepts.explanation: A device that moves heat from a colder region to a warmer one by doing work (practical example: refrigerator); used for heating or cooling by reversing heat flow.

concepts.name: Coefficient of performance (COP) of heat pumps
concepts.explanation: Ratio of heat delivered (or removed) to the work input for a heat pump or refrigerator; a measure of efficiency (COP = Q/W).
concepts.broader_concept: Heat pump (principle and applications, e.g., refrigerator)

concepts.name: Latent heat of vaporization
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat energy required to convert a unit mass of liquid into vapor at constant temperature and pressure; key to phase-change cooling processes.

concepts.name: Evaporative cooling (perspiration)
concepts.explanation: Cooling mechanism where liquid sweat evaporates from skin, absorbing latent heat and lowering body temperature; links biology and heat transfer concepts.

concepts.name: Heat loss from domestic hot-water storage
concepts.explanation: Estimating thermal losses from hot-water cylinders and distribution pipes (through insulation and surface area) and their impact on energy use.

concepts.name: Modes of Heat Transfer
concepts.explanation: Classification of the fundamental processes by which heat is transferred: conduction, convection, and thermal radiation, with different governing mechanisms and laws.

concepts.name: Solar Heating Systems
concepts.explanation: Systems that collect solar radiation and convert it to usable heat for space heating or domestic hot water, typically involving solar thermal collectors, storage elements, and heat distribution components.

concepts.name: Heat calculation using Q = mcΔT
concepts.explanation: Compute the thermal energy required to change the temperature of a substance using mass (m), specific heat capacity (c), and temperature change (ΔT).

concepts.name: Calorimetry experiment to determine specific heat capacity
concepts.explanation: A simple laboratory procedure measuring temperature change of a known mass when heated or cooled to calculate the material's specific heat capacity using energy balance.

concepts.name: Latent heat calculation using Q = mL
concepts.explanation: Calculate the heat absorbed or released during a phase change (melting, boiling) using mass (m) and the material's latent heat (L), with no temperature change during the process.

concepts.name: Measuring temperature change with thermometers and sensors
concepts.explanation: Procedures and skills for accurately measuring temperature (reading liquid-in-glass thermometers, using thermocouples/thermistors, handling calibration and uncertainties) during heating experiments.

concepts.name: Simple heat transfer experiment (conduction demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Hands-on experiments demonstrating conduction (e.g., heating one end of rods of different materials, observing temperature distribution or time to warm) and exploring insulating effects.

concepts.name: Heat (energy transfer)
concepts.explanation: Heat is energy transferred between systems or objects because of a temperature difference; this transfer can increase the internal energy and often causes a rise in temperature of the receiving body.

concepts.name: Temperature (response to heat)
concepts.explanation: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of particles in a substance; when heat is added to a system its temperature typically rises unless the energy goes into a phase change or other internal processes.

concepts.name: Temperature change due to heat transfer
concepts.explanation: The rise or fall of an object's temperature when heat is added or removed; the magnitude of the change depends on the amount of heat transferred, the object's mass and specific heat capacity, and whether a phase change occurs.

concepts.name: Distinction between heat and temperature
concepts.explanation: Heat is energy transferred between systems because of a temperature difference (measured in joules), whereas temperature is a measure of the thermal state or average kinetic energy of particles (measured in °C, K); they are related but conceptually different.

concepts.name: Thermal conduction in solids
concepts.explanation: Qualitative comparison of rates of heat conduction through different solids, emphasizing how material properties (thermal conductivity), cross-sectional area, thickness and temperature difference affect the rate.

concepts.name: Solar radiation
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by the Sun that reaches the Earth, including its spectrum (visible, infrared, ultraviolet) and its role in heating and energy transfer to the Earth's surface.

concepts.name: Solar constant (solar irradiance)
concepts.explanation: The average solar power received per unit area at the top of Earth's atmosphere at mean Earth–Sun distance (~1361 W/m²); definition, units (W/m²) and significance for Earth's energy budget.

concepts.name: Measurement of specific heat capacity (calorimetry)
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of a material's specific heat capacity using calorimetric methods (e.g., method of mixtures), applying energy conservation (heat lost = heat gained) and the relation Q = mcΔT to compute specific heat.

concepts.name: Calibration curve of a thermometer using a laboratory mercury standard
concepts.explanation: Procedure to calibrate a thermometer by comparing its readings to a laboratory mercury thermometer (standard) across known temperature points, plotting measured versus true temperatures to obtain a calibration curve and determine systematic offsets and scale factors.

concepts.name: Interpreting and applying a thermometer calibration curve
concepts.explanation: Using the calibration curve to correct raw thermometer readings, assess linearity and accuracy, estimate measurement uncertainty, and apply corrections to experimental temperature data.

concepts.name: Calorimetry (simple calorimeter)
concepts.explanation: Experimental technique and apparatus for measuring heat transfer and determining specific heat capacities or latent heats by thermal equilibrium methods.

concepts.name: Electrical method for measuring specific heat capacity
concepts.explanation: Determining specific heat by supplying known electrical energy (Q = V I t) to a sample or calorimeter and measuring the resulting temperature change.

concepts.name: Mechanical method for measuring specific heat capacity
concepts.explanation: Using mechanical work (e.g., frictional heating or paddle-wheel apparatus) converted into heat to raise a sample's temperature and determine specific heat.

concepts.name: Mechanical equivalent of heat (Joule's experiment)
concepts.explanation: The quantitative relation between mechanical work and heat energy (establishing the conversion factor J), demonstrated by experiments converting work into heat.
concepts.broader_concept: Energy conservation between work and heat

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat (experimental determination)
concepts.explanation: Procedures using calorimetry to determine latent heat by supplying/removing heat during phase change and measuring mass and heat exchanged (e.g., melting or boiling experiments).

concepts.name: Heat of fusion of ice
concepts.explanation: The specific latent heat for the fusion (melting) of ice: the energy required to convert 1 kg of ice at 0°C to 1 kg of water at 0°C (≈ 3.34×10^5 J/kg).

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat (calorimetry experiment)
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to determine a substance's specific latent heat using calorimetry and energy balance (e.g., melting ice in warm water, measuring temperature changes, applying Q_lost = Q_gained to solve for L), including consideration of heat losses and systematic errors.

concepts.name: Specific latent heat of vaporisation of water (value and units)
concepts.explanation: The specific latent heat for water, typically given as approximately 2260 kJ/kg (at 100°C), representing the energy needed to vaporize 1 kg of water at its boiling point; units J/kg (or J/g).

concepts.name: Calculation of heat required for vaporisation (Q = m L_v)
concepts.explanation: Use Q = m L_v to compute the thermal energy Q needed to convert mass m of a liquid to vapor, where L_v is the specific latent heat of vaporization.

concepts.name: Experimental measurement of latent heat of vaporization (calorimetry)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory methods to determine latent heat by supplying a known amount of heat to vaporize a measured mass of liquid (or measuring heat removal during condensation) and using energy balance to calculate L_v.

concepts.name: Evaporative cooling
concepts.explanation: Cooling effect produced when higher-energy (hotter) molecules escape from a liquid by vaporization, lowering the average kinetic energy and thus the temperature of the remaining liquid or surface.

concepts.name: Boiling versus evaporation
concepts.explanation: Distinction between evaporation (surface phenomenon occurring at any temperature) and boiling (bulk vaporization occurring when vapor pressure equals external pressure, typically at the boiling point).

concepts.name: Enthalpy of vaporization and its temperature dependence (Clausius–Clapeyron relation)
concepts.explanation: Thermodynamic concept relating the latent enthalpy of vaporization to the variation of vapor pressure with temperature; Clausius–Clapeyron equation gives d(ln p)/dT = L/(R T^2) for phase equilibrium.

concepts.name: Wave (mechanical wave)
concepts.explanation: A disturbance that transfers energy and momentum through a medium without net transport of matter; characterized by oscillations of particles of the medium.

concepts.name: Wavelength (λ)
concepts.explanation: The spatial period of a wave; the distance between successive points in phase (e.g., crest to crest or compression to compression).

concepts.name: Frequency (f)
concepts.explanation: The number of complete oscillations or cycles of a wave that pass a point per unit time, measured in hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Period (T)
concepts.explanation: The time taken for one complete cycle of a wave; the reciprocal of frequency (T = 1/f).

concepts.name: Amplitude
concepts.explanation: The maximum displacement of particles in the medium from their equilibrium position; indicates the wave's energy or intensity.

concepts.name: Wave speed and the relation v = fλ
concepts.explanation: The speed at which a wave disturbance travels through a medium (v), related to frequency and wavelength by v = f·λ.

concepts.name: Transverse wave
concepts.explanation: A wave in which particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (e.g., waves on a string).

concepts.name: Longitudinal wave
concepts.explanation: A wave in which particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation (e.g., sound waves in air with compressions and rarefactions).

concepts.name: Phase and phase difference
concepts.explanation: Phase specifies the state of oscillation at a point in a cycle; phase difference measures the relative offset between two points or waves (expressed in degrees or radians).

concepts.name: Principle of superposition and interference
concepts.explanation: When two or more waves meet, the resultant displacement is the algebraic sum of individual displacements; constructive and destructive interference patterns follow from phase relationships.

concepts.name: Standing waves; nodes and antinodes
concepts.explanation: A standing wave is formed by the superposition of two waves of same frequency traveling in opposite directions, producing stationary nodes (zero amplitude) and antinodes (maximum amplitude).

concepts.name: Reflection of waves (law of reflection)
concepts.explanation: The change in direction of a wave at a boundary such that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection measured from the normal.

concepts.name: Refraction of waves
concepts.explanation: The change in direction and speed of a wave when it passes obliquely from one medium into another, governed by wavelength change and Snell's law for wavefronts.

concepts.name: Diffraction
concepts.explanation: The spreading of waves when they encounter an obstacle or pass through an aperture comparable in size to their wavelength, producing characteristic interference patterns.

concepts.name: Ripple tank experiments (visualizing waves)
concepts.explanation: Use of a ripple tank to produce and observe wave phenomena such as reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference and to measure wavelength and wave speed visually.

concepts.name: Resonance in strings and air columns (fundamental and harmonics)
concepts.explanation: Formation of standing waves at specific frequencies (fundamental and harmonics) in stretched strings or air columns; used to determine wave speed and relationships between length, frequency and wavelength.

concepts.name: Doppler effect
concepts.explanation: Change in observed frequency (or wavelength) of a wave due to relative motion between source and observer; includes formulae for moving source/observer for sound and waves in a medium.

concepts.name: Red shift (Doppler shift of light)
concepts.explanation: Increase in wavelength (shift toward red) of electromagnetic radiation from receding astronomical objects; observational consequence of Doppler effect for light used in astronomy.

concepts.name: Doppler radar speed measurement (speed traps)
concepts.explanation: Application of the Doppler effect using reflected waves (e.g., radar) to calculate object speed from frequency shift; includes appropriate calculation procedures.

concepts.name: Radio waves (electromagnetic waves)
concepts.explanation: Long-wavelength portion of the electromagnetic spectrum used for communication; basic properties include wavelength, frequency, speed and examples of sources/detection.

concepts.name: Surface water waves (waves at sea)
concepts.explanation: Mechanical waves on the interface between water and air characterized by wavelength, period, amplitude, and propagation; includes qualitative behavior in sea conditions.

concepts.name: Seismic waves
concepts.explanation: Mechanical waves that travel through Earth's interior and along its surface (e.g., P-waves and S-waves); properties used to infer Earth's structure and in earthquake analysis.

concepts.name: Ripple tank and slinky demonstrations of wave properties
concepts.explanation: Hands-on experimental demonstrations using ripple tanks and slinkies to illustrate reflection, refraction, interference, wavelength, frequency and wave speed qualitatively and quantitatively.

concepts.name: Longitudinal waves
concepts.explanation: Waves in which particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation; characterised by compressions and rarefactions (e.g., sound in air).

concepts.name: Transverse waves
concepts.explanation: Waves in which particle displacement is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation; characterised by crests and troughs (e.g., waves on a string, electromagnetic waves).

concepts.name: Doppler effect (sound from a moving source)
concepts.explanation: Change in observed frequency or wavelength of sound when the source and/or observer are in relative motion, including formulas relating observed frequency to source frequency, speed of sound, and relative velocity.

concepts.name: Frequency
concepts.explanation: Number of complete wave cycles passing a point per unit time; measured in hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Wavelength
concepts.explanation: Distance between successive corresponding points on a wave (e.g., crest to crest); typically measured in metres.

concepts.name: Wave speed and the relation v = f · λ
concepts.explanation: The propagation speed v of a wave equals its frequency f multiplied by its wavelength λ; for light in vacuum this is c = f·λ.

concepts.name: Stationary (Standing) Waves
concepts.explanation: Wave patterns formed by the superposition of two waves of the same frequency traveling in opposite directions, producing nodes and antinodes.

concepts.name: Interference
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where two or more waves superpose to produce regions of constructive and destructive interference, affecting amplitude and intensity.

concepts.name: Reflection (of waves)
concepts.explanation: Change in direction of a wavefront when it bounces off a boundary, with angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection for ideal planar boundaries.

concepts.name: Refraction
concepts.explanation: Change in direction and speed of a wave as it passes from one medium into another due to a change in wave speed, described by Snell's law for light.

concepts.name: Polarisation
concepts.explanation: Orientation property of transverse waves (notably light) describing the direction of oscillation; includes linear, circular, and elliptical polarisation and methods to produce/analyze it.

concepts.name: Dependence of diffraction on wavelength and aperture/obstacle size
concepts.explanation: Qualitative principle that the amount of diffraction (spreading) of a wave depends on the relationship between the wavelength and the size of the aperture or obstacle; greatest spreading occurs when the wavelength is comparable to or larger than the feature size.

concepts.name: Single-slit diffraction (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative treatment of how a wave passing through a single narrow slit spreads out and produces a diffraction pattern, with the amount of spreading related to slit width relative to wavelength.

concepts.name: Diffraction around an obstacle (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative description of how waves bend around obstacles, reducing sharp shadows and causing wave energy to appear in regions geometrical optics would predict to be dark; effect depends on obstacle size vs wavelength.

concepts.name: Inter-node distance in standing waves
concepts.explanation: Relationship in standing waves between the distance between adjacent nodes (inter-node distance) and the wavelength; adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength (λ/2).

concepts.name: Wave nature of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound as a mechanical longitudinal wave that propagates via oscillations of particles in a medium, with properties such as wavelength, frequency and speed.

concepts.name: Frequency and pitch
concepts.explanation: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second of a sound wave; pitch is the perceptual sensation corresponding to frequency.

concepts.name: Amplitude and loudness
concepts.explanation: Amplitude is the size of the oscillation of a sound wave; loudness is the perceived intensity related to amplitude and frequency.

concepts.name: Quality (timbre) and overtones
concepts.explanation: Timbre (sound quality) arises from the spectrum of overtones/harmonics present in a sound beyond its fundamental frequency.

concepts.name: Resonance
concepts.explanation: Resonance is the large amplitude response of a system when driven at one of its natural frequencies; includes examples in musical instruments and vocal folds.

concepts.name: Natural frequency and fundamental frequency
concepts.explanation: Natural frequency is an oscillator's intrinsic frequency of free vibration; the fundamental frequency is the lowest natural mode in a resonator.

concepts.name: Nodes and antinodes
concepts.explanation: Nodes are points of zero displacement and antinodes are points of maximum displacement in standing waves; crucial for mode patterns on strings and in pipes.
concepts.broader_concept: Standing Waves in Strings and Pipes

concepts.name: Open and closed pipe boundary conditions
concepts.explanation: Boundary conditions for pipes (open or closed ends) determine allowed standing-wave patterns and harmonic series (which harmonics are present).
concepts.broader_concept: Standing Waves in Strings and Pipes

concepts.name: Sound intensity level (decibels)
concepts.explanation: Sound intensity level quantified on a logarithmic decibel scale, relating physical intensity to perceived loudness and threshold values.

concepts.name: Measurement of sound level (sound-level meter)
concepts.explanation: Use and interpretation of a sound-level meter to measure sound intensity levels in decibels for experiments and safety assessments.

concepts.name: Interference of sound (constructive and destructive)
concepts.explanation: Superposition of sound waves producing constructive (amplifying) or destructive (reducing) interference; basis for beats and noise cancellation.

concepts.name: Noise reduction using destructive interference
concepts.explanation: Application of destructive interference principles to reduce unwanted sound (active noise control) and demonstrations using multiple sources.

concepts.name: Reflection of sound (echo)
concepts.explanation: Reflection occurs when sound waves bounce off surfaces producing echoes and affecting room acoustics; depends on surface geometry and absorption.

concepts.name: Diffraction of sound
concepts.explanation: Diffraction is the bending and spreading of sound waves around obstacles and through openings, significant when obstacle size is comparable to wavelength.

concepts.name: Refraction of sound
concepts.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction and speed of sound waves when passing between media or gradients in temperature/density.

concepts.name: Speed of sound in various media
concepts.explanation: The speed at which sound travels depends on the medium's mechanical properties (e.g., faster in solids than in gases) and temperature.

concepts.name: Frequency limits of audibility
concepts.explanation: Human hearing has practical frequency limits (~20 Hz to 20 kHz); concept used to discuss ultrasound, infrasound, and hearing tests.

concepts.name: Ultrasound and dog whistle (inaudible high frequencies)
concepts.explanation: Sounds with frequencies above human hearing (ultrasound) used in devices like dog whistles and applications such as medical imaging.

concepts.name: Hearing impairment and ear protection
concepts.explanation: Relationship between exposure to high sound levels and hearing damage; principles and use of ear protection in industrial and musical contexts.

concepts.name: Demonstration that sound requires a medium
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure showing that sound cannot propagate in a vacuum (e.g., bell jar experiment), illustrating mechanical-wave nature of sound.

concepts.name: Using tuning forks and instruments to demonstrate vibration and resonance
concepts.explanation: Procedures using tuning forks, strings or wind instruments to show resonance, beats, standing waves and overtone series.

concepts.name: Demonstrating interference with loudspeakers and signal generators
concepts.explanation: Controlled experiments using multiple loudspeakers and signal generators to show constructive and destructive interference patterns.

concepts.name: Vocal folds (vocal cords) as a sound source
concepts.explanation: Anatomical and physical description of vocal folds producing voiced sounds by vibrating at resonant frequencies, affecting pitch and timbre.

concepts.name: Standing waves on stretched strings
concepts.explanation: Formation of stationary wave patterns on a stretched string with fixed boundary conditions, characterized by nodes and antinodes and a series of harmonics (modes).

concepts.name: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string
concepts.explanation: Lowest natural frequency of a stretched string: f1 = (1/2L) * sqrt(T/μ). Depends inversely on length L, and directly on tension T and inversely on linear mass density μ.

concepts.name: Standing waves in pipes (open and closed)
concepts.explanation: Resonant longitudinal standing waves in air columns with boundary conditions: open-open pipes have harmonics f_n = n v/(2L); open-closed pipes support odd harmonics f_n = n v/(4L) (odd n).

concepts.name: Relationship between frequency and length for vibrating systems
concepts.explanation: General dependence of resonant frequency on the effective length of the vibrating medium: frequency typically varies inversely with length for strings and pipes (e.g., f ∝ 1/L for fixed tension or fixed wave speed).

concepts.name: Speed of sound in air
concepts.explanation: Propagation speed of longitudinal sound waves in air; depends chiefly on temperature (approx. v ≈ 331 + 0.6 T°C) and medium properties; used to relate frequency and wavelength via v = fλ.

concepts.name: Measurement of the speed of sound in air (experimental methods)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedures to determine sound speed, e.g., time-of-flight measurements, resonance in pipes or tubes (standing-wave methods), and Kundt's tube; involves measuring distances, frequencies or resonance positions.

concepts.name: A-weighting (dB(A))
concepts.explanation: Frequency weighting applied to sound measurements (dB(A)) that approximates the human ear's sensitivity by attenuating low and very high frequencies, used for assessing perceived loudness and occupational noise.
concepts.broader_concept: Sound level weighting and human perception

concepts.name: Threshold of hearing (minimum audible intensity)
concepts.explanation: Lowest sound intensity or pressure perceivable by a young average human ear, reference intensity about 1×10^-12 W·m^-2 (≈20 µPa at 1 kHz); threshold varies strongly with frequency.

concepts.name: Frequency response of the ear and equal-loudness contours
concepts.explanation: Variation of human ear sensitivity with frequency, commonly represented by equal-loudness (Fletcher–Munson) curves showing how perceived loudness depends on frequency and sound level.

concepts.name: Investigation of variation of fundamental frequency of a stretched string with length (experimental procedure)
concepts.explanation: Classroom experiment measuring how the fundamental frequency changes as string length is varied while keeping tension and linear density constant; involves measuring frequency, plotting f vs 1/L or f^2 vs 1/L to verify theoretical relation.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental investigation of standing waves on strings

concepts.name: Laws of reflection
concepts.explanation: Two rules governing reflection at a plane surface: (1) the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection; (2) incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

concepts.name: Laws of refraction (Snell's law)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between angles of incidence and refraction at an interface: n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2, governing how rays bend when passing between media.

concepts.name: Refractive index
concepts.explanation: Measure of how much a medium reduces light speed and bends rays; defined by n = c/v (optical speed ratio) and, for an interface, by the ratio of sines in Snell's law.

concepts.name: Mirror and lens equation (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Gaussian formula relating focal length (f), object distance (u) and image distance (v) for thin spherical mirrors and thin lenses (with appropriate sign convention).
concepts.broader_concept: Geometric Optics: Mirror and Lens Equations

concepts.name: Image magnification (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Lateral magnification defined as the ratio of image distance to object distance (m = v/u); relates image size to object size (sign conventions affect sign of m).

concepts.name: Sign conventions for mirrors and lenses (real-is-positive)
concepts.explanation: System for assigning positive/negative values to object/image/focal distances (syllabus uses 'real-is-positive') to apply lens/mirror equations consistently.

concepts.name: Ray tracing technique for mirrors and lenses
concepts.explanation: Procedural skill of drawing principal rays (e.g., parallel→focus, through center, through focal point→parallel) to locate image position and nature for plane, concave, convex mirrors and thin lenses.

concepts.name: Plane mirror image formation
concepts.explanation: Formation of a virtual, erect image behind a plane mirror with image distance equal to object distance and lateral inversion.

concepts.name: Spherical mirror imaging (concave and convex)
concepts.explanation: How concave and convex spherical mirrors form real or virtual images depending on object position relative to focal point — predictable via ray diagrams and mirror equation.

concepts.name: Critical angle and total internal reflection
concepts.explanation: Critical angle is the angle of incidence in the denser medium above which refraction into the rarer medium ceases and total internal reflection occurs; used to trap light within a medium.

concepts.name: Relationship between critical angle and refractive index
concepts.explanation: Mathematical link: for boundary from medium n1 to n2 (n1>n2), sin(c) = n2/n1; for interface to air, n = 1/sin(c) (with stated assumptions).

concepts.name: Apparent and real depth (refraction at a horizontal surface)
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where objects submerged appear shallower due to refraction; for near-normal viewing the ratio real depth/apparent depth ≈ refractive index of the liquid.

concepts.name: Optical fibres and guided transmission
concepts.explanation: Use of total internal reflection to confine and transmit light through flexible fibres for communications and medical imaging (endoscopes).

concepts.name: Thin lens equation (1/f = 1/v + 1/u)
concepts.explanation: Relation between focal length (f), image distance (v) and object distance (u) for a thin lens, used to calculate image position.

concepts.name: Image formation by single thin lenses (ray diagrams)
concepts.explanation: Use of principal rays to determine whether a single thin convex or concave lens forms real or virtual, erect or inverted, magnified or diminished images.

concepts.name: Lens magnification (m = v/u = image height/object height)
concepts.explanation: Quantifies the linear magnification produced by a thin lens as the ratio of image distance to object distance or image height to object height.

concepts.name: Power of a lens (P = 1/f)
concepts.explanation: Optical power is the reciprocal of focal length (in metres) measured in dioptres; indicates how strongly a lens converges or diverges light.
concepts.broader_concept: Lens optical power and focal length

concepts.name: Combination of thin lenses in contact (P = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: When two thin lenses are in contact, the combined power equals the sum of their individual powers; used to find equivalent focal length.

concepts.name: Optical fibres and total internal reflection
concepts.explanation: Transmission of light through optical fibres relies on total internal reflection within a core of higher refractive index than the cladding; includes concept of critical angle and acceptance cone.
concepts.broader_concept: Total internal reflection and light guidance

concepts.name: Optical structure of the human eye
concepts.explanation: Key optical parts of the eye (cornea, crystalline lens, retina) and their roles in forming images on the retina.
concepts.broader_concept: Human eye as an optical instrument

concepts.name: Vision defects (myopia and hyperopia) and optical corrections
concepts.explanation: Causes of short sight (myopia) and long sight (hyperopia) and their corrections using appropriate diverging (concave) or converging (convex) lenses respectively.
concepts.broader_concept: Human eye as an optical instrument

concepts.name: Young's double-slit experiment
concepts.explanation: Demonstration of interference using two narrow, closely spaced slits producing a pattern of bright and dark fringes; fringe positions given by d sinθ = mλ for maxima.

concepts.name: Single-slit diffraction
concepts.explanation: Diffraction of light by a single narrow aperture producing a central maximum and subsidiary minima; minima approximately satisfy a sinθ = mλ (m ≠ 0) in the Fraunhofer limit.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating and grating equation
concepts.explanation: Multiple-slit (grating) interference producing sharp principal maxima with angular positions given by d sinθ = mλ and used for spectral dispersion and wavelength measurement.

concepts.name: Path difference and phase difference
concepts.explanation: Relation between extra distance traveled by two waves (path difference) and the corresponding phase difference (ϕ = 2π·(path difference)/λ) determining constructive or destructive interference.

concepts.name: Constructive and destructive interference
concepts.explanation: Conditions where superposed waves add to give enhanced amplitude (constructive, phase difference 2πm) or cancel/reduce amplitude (destructive, phase difference π(2m+1)).

concepts.name: Coherence of light sources
concepts.explanation: Temporal and spatial coherence properties of sources required for stable interference patterns; coherence length/time and coherence area concepts.

concepts.name: Principle of superposition for waves
concepts.explanation: Linear addition of wave amplitudes at a point to determine resultant amplitude and intensity used to analyze interference and diffraction.

concepts.name: Huygens–Fresnel principle
concepts.explanation: Wave-front construction method treating each point on a wavefront as a source of secondary wavelets to predict diffraction and interference patterns.

concepts.name: Fraunhofer and Fresnel diffraction (far-field vs near-field)
concepts.explanation: Classification of diffraction into far-field (Fraunhofer) where patterns are Fourier transforms of apertures and near-field (Fresnel) where geometry-dependent phase variations matter.

concepts.name: Fringe visibility and intensity distribution
concepts.explanation: Quantitative description of intensity across interference/diffraction patterns (including contrast/visibility metrics) and formulas for intensity variation for double-slit and single-slit arrangements.

concepts.name: Polarization of light (transverse wave nature)
concepts.explanation: Light behaves as a transverse electromagnetic wave whose oscillations have direction; polarization describes the orientation of the electric field and includes linear, circular, and unpolarized states.

concepts.name: Dispersion of light
concepts.explanation: Wavelength-dependent variation of a material's refractive index causing white light to separate into its component colours (e.g., through prisms or raindrops).

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum and visible region
concepts.explanation: The full range of electromagnetic radiation by wavelength or frequency, with the visible region being the narrow band detectable by the human eye and responsible for perceived colours.

concepts.name: Rainbow formation (dispersion and internal reflection in droplets)
concepts.explanation: Formation of rainbows by refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight in spherical water droplets, producing angularly separated colours.

concepts.name: Thin-film interference (interference colours)
concepts.explanation: Colour patterns produced by constructive and destructive interference between light waves reflected from the boundaries of a thin film; examples include soap bubbles and oil films.

concepts.name: Diffraction gratings and structural (iridescent) colours
concepts.explanation: Separation of light into colours by diffraction from periodic structures (e.g., compact disc tracks) producing angle-dependent iridescence and spectral patterns.

concepts.name: Using a spectrometer (measuring spectra)
concepts.explanation: Techniques and procedures for measuring the spectral composition of light with a spectrometer or spectroscope, including calibration and interpretation of spectral lines or bands.

concepts.name: Stress-induced birefringence (photoelasticity / stress polarisation)
concepts.explanation: Mechanical stress in certain transparent materials produces temporary birefringence that polarizes transmitted light; used diagnostically in photoelastic experiments to visualize stress patterns.

concepts.name: Linear polarizers and Polaroid sunglasses (application of polarization)
concepts.explanation: Devices (Polaroid filters) that transmit one plane of polarization and block orthogonal components, commonly used to reduce glare from reflected light and in polarization experiments.

concepts.name: Dispersion in gemstones (optical 'fire')
concepts.explanation: Separation of white light into coloured components within faceted gemstones due to material dispersion and multiple internal reflections, producing perceived 'fire'.

concepts.name: Double-slit interference (demonstration of wave nature of light)
concepts.explanation: Experimental demonstration that light exhibits interference and diffraction (e.g., Young's double-slit, single-slit diffraction), showing superposition and wavefront behavior and enabling measurement of wavelength.

concepts.name: Infrared imaging (thermal cameras)
concepts.explanation: Principles of infrared radiation detection and imaging: blackbody emission, IR detectors (thermal and photon), image formation, and applications such as medical thermography and night vision.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet radiation absorption by the ozone layer
concepts.explanation: How UV radiation (UV-A, UV-B, UV-C) interacts with atmospheric ozone, the role of ozone in absorbing harmful UV wavelengths, and implications for surface UV flux and biological effects.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect (radiative heat trapping in the atmosphere)
concepts.explanation: Mechanism by which greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, altering Earth's energy balance and surface temperature; basic radiative transfer and concepts of emissivity/absorption.

concepts.name: Television signal transmission and image formation
concepts.explanation: Physical principles behind electronic capture, encoding and transmission of images (scanning, modulation, carrier waves) and reconstruction on display devices; relation to electromagnetic waves and electronics.

concepts.name: Electric lighting (principles of lamps and illumination)
concepts.explanation: Physical principles of common light sources (incandescent, fluorescent, LED): mechanisms of light generation, spectra, luminous efficacy, and basics of illumination and lighting design.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating equation (nλ = d sinθ)
concepts.explanation: Relation between wavelength λ, grating spacing d, diffraction order n and angle θ used to calculate spectral wavelengths from grating measurements.

concepts.name: Spectrometer: parts and function
concepts.explanation: Identification and purpose of spectrometer components (collimator, prism/grating mount, telescope, scale) and how the instrument is used to measure spectral angles and wavelengths.

concepts.name: Polarisation of light
concepts.explanation: Orientation of the electric field vector of transverse light waves; includes linear polarisation and experimental demonstration using polaroid filters to analyze and produce polarised light.

concepts.name: Dispersion by a prism
concepts.explanation: Separation of white light into its constituent wavelengths due to wavelength-dependent refractive index of glass, producing a continuous spectrum.

concepts.name: Dispersion by a diffraction grating
concepts.explanation: Wavelength-dependent angular separation of light created by interference from multiple slits or grooves; distinct spectral lines and order-dependent dispersion described by the grating equation.

concepts.name: Recombination of dispersed light by a prism
concepts.explanation: Reversing the dispersion process by passing a spectrum back through a prism (or sequence of prisms) to recombine different wavelengths into white light.

concepts.name: Additive colour mixing (primary, secondary and complementary colours)
concepts.explanation: Combination of coloured lights: primary additive colours (red, green, blue), formation of secondary colours by addition, and concept of complementary colours that combine to produce white light.

concepts.name: Ordering of electromagnetic radiations by wavelength and frequency
concepts.explanation: Relative positions of ultraviolet, visible and infrared regions (and other bands) along the electromagnetic spectrum, noting inverse relation between wavelength and frequency.

concepts.name: Detection of ultraviolet (UV) and infrared (IR) radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods and devices for detecting UV and IR radiation (e.g., photodiodes, thermopiles, photographic/chemical indicators, thermal detectors) and basic experimental tests distinguishing these bands from visible light.

concepts.name: Snell's Law of Refraction (verification experiment)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative relationship between angles of incidence and refraction when light passes between two media, typically verified by measuring angles and showing n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2.

concepts.name: Refractive Index (measurement of a liquid or solid)
concepts.explanation: Determination of a medium's refractive index (absolute or relative) using experimental methods such as Snell's law, apparent depth, or critical angle measurements; includes n = c/v and n = sinθ1/sinθ2.

concepts.name: Focal Length of a Concave Mirror (measurement)
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of a concave mirror's focal length using object-image distances and the mirror equation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di or by focusing parallel rays (distant object) to the focus.

concepts.name: Focal Length of a Converging Lens (measurement)
concepts.explanation: Experimental methods to measure the focal length of a converging (convex) lens using lens formula 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, displacement method, or by focusing parallel rays.

concepts.name: Wavelength of Monochromatic Light (measurement)
concepts.explanation: Measurement of the wavelength of a single-frequency light source using interference or diffraction techniques (e.g., diffraction grating, double-slit interference) and related formulas (d sinθ = mλ).

concepts.name: Wavelength-frequency-speed relation (c = λ·f)
concepts.explanation: Mathematical relationship connecting a light wave's wavelength (λ), frequency (f), and its speed (c): c = λ·f; used to relate color, energy, and propagation.

concepts.name: Snell's law (Refraction)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative law describing refraction at a boundary: n1·sinθ1 = n2·sinθ2, relating incidence and refraction angles via refractive indices.

concepts.name: Law of reflection
concepts.explanation: Geometric rule for reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection measured relative to the normal; basis for ray optics.

concepts.name: Speed of light in vacuum
concepts.explanation: The constant speed at which light propagates in vacuum (commonly denoted c ≈ 3.00×10^8 m/s), fundamental in wave and relativity contexts.

concepts.name: Dispersion (wavelength dependence of refractive index)
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where refractive index varies with wavelength, causing different colors to refract by different amounts (prisms, chromatic aberration).

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum (visible, UV, IR)
concepts.explanation: Classification of electromagnetic radiation by wavelength/frequency, including visible light, ultraviolet, and infrared regions and their properties.

concepts.name: Photon energy and quantization (E = h·f)
concepts.explanation: Quantum description of light energy: individual quanta (photons) carry energy E = h·f, underlying phenomena like the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: Electric fields
concepts.explanation: The vector field around electric charges that describes the force per unit positive test charge (E = F/q), represented by field lines and used to calculate forces and potential.

concepts.name: Force between charges (Coulomb's law)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative law giving the electrostatic force between two point charges: F = k q1 q2 / r^2 (with vector direction), including principles of superposition.

concepts.name: Potential difference
concepts.explanation: The work done per unit charge in moving a test charge between two points in an electric field (V = W/q), related to electric field by V(b)-V(a) = -∫E·dl and measured in volts.

concepts.name: Electrification by induction
concepts.explanation: Method of charging an object without direct contact by redistributing charges using a nearby charged body and often grounding to separate charges.

concepts.name: Electrification by contact (charging by conduction)
concepts.explanation: Charging process in which charge is transferred between objects through direct physical contact, resulting in redistribution of charge.

concepts.name: Distribution of charge on conductors
concepts.explanation: Principles governing how excess charge resides on conducting bodies at electrostatic equilibrium (charges on the outer surface, higher density at sharp points, electrostatic shielding in cavities).

concepts.name: Electroscope (detection of charge)
concepts.explanation: A device used to detect and give a qualitative measure of electric charge; demonstrates charging by contact and induction and shows sign and relative magnitude of charge.

concepts.name: Everyday electrostatic phenomena (dust on television screens; static on clothes)
