concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure to determine the heat capacity (or specific heat) of a substance by supplying known energy via mechanical work (e.g., paddle-wheel) or electrical heating (Q = V I t) and measuring the temperature change, accounting for heat losses.

concepts.name: Mechanical equivalent of heat (Joule's principle)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between mechanical work and heat energy (work converted into heat); experimentally established by Joule. Provides conversion factor between mechanical energy units and heat (often implied in calorimetry with mechanical heating).

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the specific latent heat of a substance by supplying known heat (commonly via electrical heating) to cause a phase change for a measured mass and recording energy input and mass/temperature data while accounting for heat losses.

concepts.name: Measurement of specific latent heat (heat of fusion of ice)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to determine the specific latent heat of fusion by mixing melting ice with water in a calorimeter, applying energy conservation (heat lost = heat gained), using L = Q/m and correcting for calorimeter heat capacity and heat losses to environment.

concepts.name: Latent heat of vaporisation
concepts.explanation: The energy required to convert a unit mass of a substance from liquid to gaseous phase at constant temperature and pressure; for a mass m the heat required is Q = m L_v (units J/kg), and for water L_v ≈ 2.26×10^6 J/kg at 100°C (value varies with temperature and pressure).

concepts.name: Phase change: evaporation versus boiling
concepts.explanation: Distinction between evaporation (surface phenomenon occurring at temperatures below boiling point) and boiling (bulk vaporisation at a specific boiling temperature where vapor pressure equals ambient pressure); both require latent heat of vaporisation supplied to the liquid.

concepts.name: Experimental determination of latent heat of vaporisation (calorimetry)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedures to measure L_v, typically by supplying known heat to vaporise a measured mass (or by condensing steam into cooler water and using energy balance), using Q = m L_v and accounting for heat losses and calibration of thermometer and calorimeter.

concepts.name: Wave (definition)
concepts.explanation: A disturbance that transfers energy (and information) through a medium or space without net transport of matter; characterized by regularly repeating variation in a physical quantity.

concepts.name: Period
concepts.explanation: The time taken for one complete cycle of the wave; the reciprocal of frequency (T = 1/f).

concepts.name: Transverse and longitudinal waves
concepts.explanation: Classification of waves by particle motion: transverse waves have particle displacement perpendicular to propagation, longitudinal waves have displacement parallel to propagation.

concepts.name: Principle of superposition
concepts.explanation: When two or more waves overlap, the resultant displacement at each point is the algebraic sum of the displacements due to each wave separately.

concepts.name: Interference (constructive and destructive)
concepts.explanation: The pattern produced when two coherent waves superpose: constructive interference where waves are in phase (amplitudes add), destructive where out of phase (amplitudes subtract or cancel).

concepts.name: Reflection and refraction of waves
concepts.explanation: Reflection is the change in direction when a wave bounces off a boundary; refraction is the change in direction and speed as a wave passes between media with different wave speeds, described by Snell's law for many waves.

concepts.name: Standing waves (nodes and antinodes)
concepts.explanation: A stationary wave pattern formed by the superposition of two equal-amplitude waves travelling in opposite directions, characterized by nodes (zero displacement) and antinodes (maximum displacement).

concepts.name: Resonance in wave systems
concepts.explanation: The condition where a system oscillates with maximum amplitude at particular natural frequencies when driven by a periodic force matching a natural frequency, often demonstrated with standing waves.

concepts.name: Harmonic travelling wave equation (y(x,t)=A sin(kx - ωt))
concepts.explanation: Mathematical description of a sinusoidal travelling wave using amplitude A, wave number k, angular frequency ω, showing spatial and temporal variation and allowing derivation of v = ω/k and v = fλ.

concepts.name: Wave speed relation (v = fλ)
concepts.explanation: Relationship between wave speed (v), frequency (f) and wavelength (λ): v = f × λ; used in calculations of wave behavior across media.

concepts.name: Astronomical redshift
concepts.explanation: Observed increase in wavelength (redshift) of light from distant stars and galaxies interpreted as a Doppler shift due to recessional motion or cosmic expansion.

concepts.name: Radio waves (as example of electromagnetic waves)
concepts.explanation: Long-wavelength electromagnetic waves used in communication and radar systems; often cited as everyday examples of wave phenomena.

concepts.name: Ripple tank demonstration of wave properties
concepts.explanation: Laboratory demonstration using a ripple tank to visualize wave phenomena such as reflection, refraction, interference and diffraction on a water surface.

concepts.name: Slinky demonstration of longitudinal and transverse waves
concepts.explanation: Classroom experiment using a slinky to show differences between longitudinal (compression) and transverse waves and to illustrate concepts like wavelength and wave speed.

concepts.name: Microphone and speaker demonstration of sound waves
concepts.explanation: Simple experimental setup using a speaker to generate sound and a microphone to detect variations, demonstrating properties of sound waves and Doppler effects for audible frequencies.

concepts.name: Wave speed relation (v = fλ / c = fλ)
concepts.explanation: Mathematical relationship linking wave speed (v or c for light), frequency (f), and wavelength (λ): v = fλ (for electromagnetic waves commonly written c = fλ).

concepts.name: Reflection of waves
concepts.explanation: Process by which a wave bounces back from a boundary between two media, with angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection for planar waves.

concepts.name: Relationship between inter-node distance and wavelength (standing waves)
concepts.explanation: In standing waves, nodes are points of zero amplitude and adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength; the distance between successive nodes equals λ/2, allowing wavelength determination from node spacing.

concepts.name: Diffraction at an obstacle and single slit — dependence on wavelength
concepts.explanation: Qualitative understanding that waves spread (diffract) when encountering an obstacle or aperture of size comparable to their wavelength; diffraction is significant when the obstacle or slit width is on the order of the wavelength, producing characteristic spreading and interference patterns (single-slit central maximum width scales with wavelength/aperture size).

concepts.name: Doppler effect for a moving source and stationary observer (simple quantitative treatment)
concepts.explanation: When a source moves relative to a stationary observer, the observed frequency shifts because successive wavefronts are compressed or stretched; for a source moving at speed v_s in a medium with wave speed v, f' = f * v/(v ± v_s) (use sign convention: minus for source moving toward observer), presented at a simple non-relativistic quantitative level.

concepts.name: Sound as longitudinal mechanical waves
concepts.explanation: Sound is a mechanical disturbance that propagates through a material medium as longitudinal pressure waves consisting of compressions and rarefactions.

concepts.name: Sound intensity level (decibel)
concepts.explanation: Sound intensity level L (in decibels) is defined by L = 10 log10(I/I0), where I is sound intensity and I0 is a reference intensity (typically 10^-12 W m^-2); used to quantify perceived loudness on a logarithmic scale.

concepts.name: Stationary (standing) waves in strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: Standing waves arise from superposition of waves traveling in opposite directions, producing nodes and antinodes; boundary conditions on strings and pipes determine allowed standing-mode patterns.

concepts.name: Fundamental frequency and harmonics (overtones)
concepts.explanation: The fundamental is the lowest-frequency standing wave mode (f1); harmonics are integer multiples of the fundamental for strings and open pipes (fn = n·v/2L for a string/open-open pipe), producing overtone series that determine pitch and timbre.

concepts.name: Natural frequency and resonance
concepts.explanation: A system's natural frequency is the frequency at which it oscillates freely; resonance occurs when a driving frequency matches a natural frequency, producing large amplitude response and practical examples (e.g., vocal cords, bridges, musical instruments).

concepts.name: Reflection, refraction and diffraction of sound
concepts.explanation: Sound waves reflect from surfaces, refract when entering media with different wave speed, and diffract around obstacles and through openings; these wave phenomena affect acoustics and sound propagation.

concepts.name: Frequency limits of audibility and ultrasonic devices
concepts.explanation: Human hearing typically ranges from about 20 Hz to 20 kHz; frequencies above this range are ultrasonic (e.g., dog whistle) and may be used by animals or for technical applications.

concepts.name: Timbre (quality) and overtone content
concepts.explanation: Timbre is the perceptual quality that distinguishes sounds with the same pitch and loudness; it arises from the relative amplitudes and phases of fundamental and overtone (harmonic) components.

concepts.name: Sound requires a medium
concepts.explanation: Sound cannot propagate in a vacuum; demonstrations (e.g., vibrating source in evacuated chamber) show that a material medium is required for transmission of pressure waves.

concepts.name: Experimental demonstrations and measurements (tuning forks, signal generators, sound-level meters)
concepts.explanation: Practical methods for studying sound include using tuning forks to show interference and resonance, signal generators and loudspeakers for controlled waveforms, and sound-level meters to measure intensity levels in decibels.

concepts.name: Hearing impairment and ear protection (sound exposure limits)
concepts.explanation: Prolonged or intense sound exposure can cause hearing damage; understanding intensity levels and exposure limits underpins use of ear protection in industry and assessment of noise pollution.

concepts.name: Wave speed on a stretched string (v = sqrt(T/μ))
concepts.explanation: Speed of transverse waves on a stretched string given by v = sqrt(T/μ), where T is tension and μ is linear mass density; determines frequencies of standing waves.

concepts.name: Harmonics in strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: Discrete set of resonant modes (overtones) with frequencies that are integer multiples of the fundamental for strings and for pipes depending on boundary conditions (open/closed), determining allowed standing-wave patterns.

concepts.name: Frequency–period relationship (f = 1/T)
concepts.explanation: Definition linking frequency f and period T of periodic motion: frequency is the reciprocal of the period.

concepts.name: Frequency dependence on length for strings and pipes
concepts.explanation: How the fundamental frequency varies inversely with length (for a given wave speed): longer strings/pipes give lower fundamental frequencies; specific relations depend on boundary conditions.

concepts.name: Sound intensity (I)
concepts.explanation: Sound intensity is the sound power transmitted per unit area (I = P/A), with SI unit watts per square metre (W·m⁻²); a physical measure of sound energy flux.

concepts.name: Threshold of hearing and ear frequency response (dB(A) weighting)
concepts.explanation: Reference threshold I0 (~10⁻¹² W·m⁻²) for hearing and the ear's varying sensitivity across frequencies; dB(A) weighting applies a frequency-dependent filter to dB measurements to reflect perceived loudness.

concepts.name: Experiment: variation of fundamental frequency with string length
concepts.explanation: Practical investigation where the fundamental frequency of a stretched string is measured as length is changed, demonstrating inverse relationship between frequency and length for fixed tension and mass per unit length.
concepts.broader_concept: Practical investigations of standing waves on strings

concepts.name: Experiment: variation of fundamental frequency with string tension
concepts.explanation: Practical investigation measuring how the fundamental frequency changes with tension, illustrating that frequency increases with the square root of tension for a fixed string length and mass per unit length.
concepts.broader_concept: Practical investigations of standing waves on strings

concepts.name: Concave mirror image formation
concepts.explanation: Rules for image formation by a concave (converging) spherical mirror depend on object position relative to focal point and centre; images can be real/inverted or virtual/upright and magnified or diminished.

concepts.name: Convex mirror image formation
concepts.explanation: A convex (diverging) spherical mirror always produces a virtual, upright, diminished image located behind the mirror.

concepts.name: Lens and mirror equation and magnification
concepts.explanation: Relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v) and focal length (f) given by 1/u + 1/v = 1/f; linear magnification m = v/u (with sign convention) links image size to object size.

concepts.name: Sign convention for mirrors and lenses (real-is-positive)
concepts.explanation: A prescribed sign convention (real distances positive or 'real-is-positive') for object/image/focal distances and magnification used when applying lens/mirror equations.

concepts.name: Law of refraction (Snell's law)
concepts.explanation: The ratio of the sines of the angles of incidence and refraction is constant for an interface between two media: n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2.

concepts.name: Refractive index (definition and speed relation)
concepts.explanation: Refractive index quantifies how much light slows in a medium; n = c/v (or ratio of sines via Snell's law) and relative refractive index between two media is the ratio of their light speeds.

concepts.name: Critical angle and relationship to refractive index
concepts.explanation: The critical angle is the angle of incidence in the denser medium above which total internal reflection occurs; related by sin θc = n2/n1 for light from medium 1 into medium 2 (n1>n2).

concepts.name: Total internal reflection
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where light incident from a denser to a rarer medium at angles greater than the critical angle is completely reflected back into the denser medium, with no transmitted refracted ray.

concepts.name: Ray tracing for mirrors and lenses
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure using principal rays (parallel to axis, through centre, through focal point) and instruments (ray box, laser) to construct image position and size for mirrors and lenses.

concepts.name: Optical fibres and total internal reflection applications
concepts.explanation: Use of optical fibres that guide light by repeated total internal reflection for telecommunications and medical endoscopy; requires core/cladding refractive index differences.

concepts.name: Real and apparent depth (refraction at surface)
concepts.explanation: Apparent depth phenomenon where an object submerged in a medium appears at a shallower depth when viewed from above due to refraction at the interface; can be related to refractive indices.

concepts.name: Mirages (refraction in gradient atmospheres)
concepts.explanation: Optical phenomenon caused by continuous refraction (bending) of light in layers of air with varying refractive index (temperature gradients), producing displaced or inverted images.

concepts.name: Prism reflectors and retroreflection (corner-cube prisms)
concepts.explanation: Devices that return incident light toward the source using multiple internal reflections (corner-cube retroreflectors), used in reflective road signs and safety devices.

concepts.name: Spectacles and lens correction of vision
concepts.explanation: Application of lenses to correct refractive errors of the eye (myopia, hyperopia) by forming an image on the retina using appropriate converging or diverging lenses.

concepts.name: Image formation by a single thin lens (real and virtual images)
concepts.explanation: How a single thin lens produces real or virtual images depending on object position relative to the focal length; ray-diagram construction rules (parallel ray through focus, ray through centre undeviated, ray through focus emerges parallel).

concepts.name: Lens magnification (m = v/u = hi/ho)
concepts.explanation: The lateral magnification of a thin lens: ratio of image height to object height (hi/ho) which equals the ratio of image distance to object distance (v/u) under the thin-lens approximation.

concepts.name: Power of a lens (P = 1/f, in dioptres)
concepts.explanation: Definition of lens power P as the reciprocal of focal length f (in metres); positive for converging lenses and negative for diverging lenses; measured in dioptres (D).

concepts.name: Power of two thin lenses in contact (P = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: For two thin lenses in close contact, the combined optical power equals the algebraic sum of their individual powers; used to find equivalent focal length of lens systems.

concepts.name: Total internal reflection and critical angle
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon occurring when light attempts to pass from a denser to a rarer medium at angles greater than the critical angle, causing complete reflection; critical angle given by sin θc = n2/n1 (n1>n2).
concepts.broader_concept: Optical fibres and total internal reflection

concepts.name: Light transmission in optical fibres (guided by total internal reflection)
concepts.explanation: Principle of optical fibre operation: light is confined to the core and propagated long distances by repeated total internal reflection at the core–cladding interface; includes concepts of core/cladding refractive indices and acceptance angle.
concepts.broader_concept: Optical fibres and total internal reflection

concepts.name: Myopia (short-sightedness) and optical correction
concepts.explanation: Vision defect where the eye focuses images in front of the retina (distant objects blurred); corrected using a diverging (concave) lens to move the image back onto the retina.

concepts.name: Hyperopia (long-sightedness) and optical correction
concepts.explanation: Vision defect where the eye focuses images behind the retina (near objects blurred); corrected using a converging (convex) lens to move the image forward onto the retina.

concepts.name: Interference of light
concepts.explanation: Superposition of coherent light waves that produces spatial variations in intensity (fringes) due to phase differences between waves; basis for experiments like double-slit and for understanding diffraction patterns.

concepts.name: Diffraction of light
concepts.explanation: The bending and spreading of light waves when they encounter apertures or obstacles, producing characteristic intensity patterns that result from interference of secondary wavelets (Huygens principle).

concepts.name: Constructive and destructive interference (phase and path difference)
concepts.explanation: Conditions determining whether interfering waves reinforce (constructive: phase difference = 2πn or path difference = nλ) or cancel (destructive: phase difference = π(2n+1) or path difference = (n+1/2)λ), producing maxima and minima in intensity.

concepts.name: Coherence and monochromatic light
concepts.explanation: Requirements for stable interference: temporal coherence (consistent phase over time, related to monochromaticity) and spatial coherence (fixed phase relationship across sources or wavefronts).

concepts.name: Fringe spacing (double-slit) formula
concepts.explanation: Relation x = λL/d (for small angles) giving fringe separation x on the screen in terms of wavelength λ, slit separation d, and distance to screen L; derived from path difference and small-angle approximation.

concepts.name: Single-slit diffraction and minima condition
concepts.explanation: Diffraction pattern from a single slit characterized by a central maximum and subsidiary minima; minima occur at angles satisfying a sinθ = mλ (m = ±1, ±2,...), where a is slit width.

concepts.name: Light as a transverse wave
concepts.explanation: The concept that light is an electromagnetic wave whose oscillations of the electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to the direction of propagation; basis for polarization phenomena.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
concepts.explanation: The full range of electromagnetic radiation ordered by wavelength or frequency, including the visible band; relates wavelength, frequency and photon energy.

concepts.name: Visible spectrum and colour perception
concepts.explanation: How different wavelengths within the visible portion of the electromagnetic spectrum correspond to perceived colours and how white light decomposes into spectral colours.

concepts.name: Dispersion (wavelength-dependent refraction)
concepts.explanation: The dependence of a material's refractive index on wavelength, causing different wavelengths to refract by different amounts and leading to separation of white light into colours (e.g., rainbows, gemstone 'fire').

concepts.name: Rainbow formation
concepts.explanation: The specific optical process by which raindrops produce a spectrum: dispersion by refraction on entering and leaving the drop combined with internal reflection and geometric angles for each wavelength.

concepts.name: Spectrometer and spectral measurement
concepts.explanation: Use and principles of a spectrometer (prism- or grating-based) to separate and measure wavelengths of light and record spectra for analysis.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating and structural colours (compact discs)
concepts.explanation: Diffraction from regularly spaced grooves or microstructures separates light into constituent wavelengths, producing spectral colours on surfaces such as compact discs and CDs.

concepts.name: Linear polarization and polarizing filters (Polaroid sunglasses)
concepts.explanation: Polarization describes the orientation of transverse light oscillations; polarizing filters (Polaroid) transmit light of a given polarization and can reduce glare by blocking reflected polarized light.

concepts.name: Stress-induced birefringence (stress polarisation)
concepts.explanation: Mechanical stress in certain transparent materials produces anisotropic refractive indices (birefringence) so that polarized light experiences different phase shifts, producing characteristic coloured patterns when viewed with polarizers.

concepts.name: Wave nature of light
concepts.explanation: The concept that light exhibits wave phenomena such as interference, diffraction and polarization, described by wavelength, frequency and phase.

concepts.name: Infrared radiation (IR) — properties and detection
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than visible light; characterized by thermal emission, absorption bands, and detection methods (photodiodes, bolometers).

concepts.name: Infrared thermal imaging (infrared camera principles and applications)
concepts.explanation: Principles of converting IR emission to temperature maps (thermal imaging), including detector arrays and calibration; applications include medical thermography and night vision.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet radiation and ozone layer interaction
concepts.explanation: How ultraviolet (UV) radiation is absorbed by stratospheric ozone (O3), the role of ozone in shielding biological systems from harmful UV, and the photochemical reactions involved.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect (radiative trapping by atmospheric gases)
concepts.explanation: The process by which greenhouse gases absorb and re‑emit longwave infrared radiation, trapping heat in the atmosphere and affecting Earth's energy balance and surface temperature.

concepts.name: Diffraction grating formula (nλ = d sinθ)
concepts.explanation: The relationship between diffraction order n, wavelength λ, grating spacing d and diffraction angle θ used to predict or calculate spectral line positions.

concepts.name: Derivation of the diffraction grating formula
concepts.explanation: Geometric derivation of nλ = d sinθ from path difference and constructive interference conditions for multiple slits or grooves.

concepts.name: Using a diffraction grating to measure wavelength
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure and calculations to determine unknown wavelengths from measured diffraction angles and known grating spacing or order.

concepts.name: Spectrometer components and function
concepts.explanation: Identification and role of spectrometer parts (entrance slit/collimator, dispersing element—prism or grating, telescope, scale) and how the instrument is used to measure spectral angles and wavelengths.

concepts.name: Polarisation of light (demonstration with polaroids)
concepts.explanation: Concept of linear polarization, use of polarizing filters (polaroids) to produce and analyze polarized light and classroom demonstrations of polarization effects.

concepts.name: Malus's law (I = I0 cos^2θ)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative law giving transmitted intensity through an analyzer as I = I0 cos^2θ where θ is the angle between transmission axes of polarizer and analyzer.

concepts.name: Additive colour mixing and primary/secondary/complementary colours
concepts.explanation: Principles of additive mixing of light (primary colours red, green, blue), formation of secondary colours (cyan, magenta, yellow), and complementary colour pairs used in spectral and display contexts.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum ordering and wavelength–frequency relations
concepts.explanation: Relative ordering of ultraviolet, visible and infrared radiation by wavelength and frequency and the relationship c = λf linking wavelength and frequency.

concepts.name: Detection methods for UV and IR radiation
concepts.explanation: Techniques and detectors used to observe or measure ultraviolet and infrared radiation (e.g., photodetectors, thermal detectors, photographic/fluorescent indicators) and basic operating principles.

concepts.name: Snell's Law of Refraction
concepts.explanation: Mathematical relation n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2 that quantifies how a light ray changes direction when crossing an interface between two media with refractive indices n1 and n2.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Snell's Law
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to measure incident and refracted angles at an interface and show the proportionality of sinθ1 to sinθ2 (or determine ratio n2/n1), using apparatus such as a semicircular block, protractor, and laser or ray box.

concepts.name: Measurement of Refractive Index of a Liquid or Solid
concepts.explanation: Experimental methods to determine the refractive index of a medium (liquid or solid) using Snell's law, critical angle measurements, or apparent depth techniques and calculation of n = sinθ1/sinθ2 or related formulas.

concepts.name: Measurement of the Focal Length of a Converging Lens
concepts.explanation: Procedures to determine a converging lens's focal length using the lens formula 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, methods with an optical bench, distant object method, or conjugate f method and ray tracing to locate image and object distances.

concepts.name: Measurement of the Focal Length of a Concave Mirror
concepts.explanation: Techniques to find a concave mirror's focal length using the mirror equation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, methods such as using a distant object, measuring image and object distances on an optical bench, or using ray diagrams to locate the focus.

concepts.name: Wavelength Measurement of Monochromatic Light
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of the wavelength λ of monochromatic light using interference or diffraction methods (e.g., Young's double-slit, diffraction grating) and relations such as d sinθ = mλ or λ = xd / (mD) from measured fringe positions.
concepts.broader_concept: Wave Nature of Light / Wavelength Measurement

concepts.name: Wave–particle duality of light
concepts.explanation: Light exhibits both wave-like (interference, diffraction) and particle-like (photons, quantized energy exchange) behaviors; foundation for explaining phenomena across optics and quantum experiments.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum (visible light)
concepts.explanation: Classification of electromagnetic radiation by wavelength/frequency, including the visible band (~380–750 nm) with associated photon energies.

concepts.name: Index of refraction
concepts.explanation: Material property n = c/v giving the ratio of light speed in vacuum to speed in the medium; underpins refraction and dispersion.

concepts.name: Image formation by plane mirrors
concepts.explanation: Plane mirrors produce virtual, upright images the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front; lateral inversion and equal size apply.

concepts.name: Thin lens equation and magnification
concepts.explanation: Relation between object distance (do), image distance (di) and focal length (f): 1/f = 1/do + 1/di; lateral magnification m = -di/do describes image size and orientation.

concepts.name: Young's double-slit interference
concepts.explanation: Interference pattern produced by coherent light through two slits; fringe spacing given approximately by y = λD/d for small angles (λ = wavelength, D = screen distance, d = slit separation).

concepts.name: Polarization of light
concepts.explanation: Orientation property of transverse electromagnetic waves describing the direction of the electric field vector; can be analyzed/produced with polarizers and described by Malus' law.

concepts.name: Coulomb's law (force between charges)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative law giving the electrostatic force between two point charges: magnitude proportional to product of charges and inverse-square of separation, vector along line joining charges; basis for calculating pairwise forces and using superposition.

concepts.name: Electric field (definition and superposition)
concepts.explanation: Vector field defined as force per unit positive test charge (E = F/q); representation with field lines; field of point charges and construction of net field by vector superposition.

concepts.name: Electric potential and potential difference
concepts.explanation: Electric potential as potential energy per unit charge; potential difference (voltage) between two points equals work done per unit charge to move a test charge; relation to electric field (E = -dV/ds in one dimension).

concepts.name: Electrification by contact (charging by contact)
concepts.explanation: Process of transferring charge between bodies through physical contact, resulting in redistribution of electrons and net charge on objects that were initially neutral or charged.

concepts.name: Electrification by induction (charging by induction)
concepts.explanation: Charging process where a charged object brought near a conductor induces charge separation without direct contact; grounding can remove one sign of charge producing a net charge on the conductor.

concepts.name: Electroscope operation and use
concepts.explanation: Instrument and procedures for detecting and estimating charge: charging an electroscope, observing leaf divergence, determining sign of charge via induction or contact, and basic experimental precautions.

concepts.name: Electrostatic hazards and applications (static electricity effects)
concepts.explanation: Practical examples and safety concerns of static electricity: attraction of dust to TV screens, static cling on clothes, and industrial hazards such as ignition risks in flour mills and during aircraft refuelling due to electrostatic discharge.

concepts.name: Lightning (atmospheric electric discharge)
concepts.explanation: Rapid electrical discharge in the atmosphere between charged regions (within clouds, cloud-to-cloud, or cloud-to-ground) producing a bright flash and large current.

concepts.name: Dielectric breakdown of air
concepts.explanation: The ionization process in which the air becomes conductive when the local electric field exceeds a threshold, initiating an electrical discharge (breakdown voltage/field).

concepts.name: Step leader and return stroke mechanism
concepts.explanation: The staged formation of an ionized path (step leader) from cloud toward ground and the subsequent high-current return stroke that produces most light and energy release in a lightning flash.

concepts.name: Thunder (acoustic shock from lightning)
concepts.explanation: Loud sound produced by rapid heating and expansion of air along the lightning channel, forming a shock wave whose features depend on channel geometry and distance.
concepts.broader_concept: Acoustic waves from rapid thermal expansion

concepts.name: Lightning rods and grounding for protection
concepts.explanation: Design and function of conductors and grounding systems that provide a low-resistance path to safely divert lightning current to ground and protect structures.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic radiation from lightning
concepts.explanation: Broadband electromagnetic emission from lightning including visible flash, radio-frequency pulses, and X-ray/gamma bursts caused by rapid current changes and energetic electrons.

concepts.name: Estimating distance to lightning using flash and thunder
concepts.explanation: Procedure using the near-instantaneous arrival of light and the slower speed of sound: measure time delay between flash and thunder to estimate distance to strike.

concepts.name: Electric field (vector) and field strength
concepts.explanation: The electric field is a vector field defined as the force per unit positive test charge at a point: E = F/q, with direction showing force on a positive charge.

concepts.name: Electric potential difference (voltage) and definition of volt
concepts.explanation: Potential difference between two points is the work done per unit charge to move a charge between them; the volt is one joule per coulomb.

concepts.name: Charge distribution on conductors (surface charge)
concepts.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium excess charge on a conductor resides on its outer surface; there is no net electric field inside a conductor.

concepts.name: Charge concentration at sharp points
concepts.explanation: Electric charge tends to accumulate at regions of high curvature (points) on a conductor, producing stronger local fields at sharp points.

concepts.name: Point discharge and corona
concepts.explanation: Discharge phenomena from sharp points where strong local electric fields ionize air, leading to corona, sparking or point discharge.

concepts.name: Lines of force (field lines) concept
concepts.explanation: A qualitative representation of electric fields using lines that indicate field direction and relative strength; lines originate on positive charges and terminate on negative charges.

concepts.name: Forces between collinear charges (one-dimensional Coulomb calculations)
concepts.explanation: Calculation of net electrostatic forces when multiple point charges lie along a common line, using vector addition of Coulomb forces (collinear case).

concepts.name: Demonstration: forces between charges (pith balls/torsion balance)
concepts.explanation: Experimental demonstrations that show attraction and repulsion of charged objects and allow estimation/verification of Coulomb's law using pith balls or torsion balances.

concepts.name: Demonstration: insulated conductor and nearby charged object (induction)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration showing charge redistribution (induction) on an insulated conductor placed near a charged object, illustrating induced charges and grounding effects.

concepts.name: Van de Graaff generator demonstrations
concepts.explanation: Use of a Van de Graaff generator to produce high static voltages for demonstrations of charging, hair-raising effects, sparks and discharge phenomena.

concepts.name: Field mapping using oil and semolina (visualising electric field patterns)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory method to visualize electric field lines and equipotentials by dispersing particles (e.g., semolina) in oil between charged plates or electrodes.

concepts.name: Lightning conductors (lightning rods) and their uses
concepts.explanation: Devices that provide a low-resistance path to ground for lightning strikes, protecting structures by directing charge safely to earth.

concepts.name: Electrostatic precipitator principle
concepts.explanation: Industrial application using electric fields to charge and collect particulate pollutants from exhaust gases by attracting charged particles to collection plates.

concepts.name: Xerography (photocopying) principle
concepts.explanation: Copying process that uses electrostatic charge patterns on a photoconductor to attract toner particles, which are then transferred and fused to paper.

concepts.name: Hazards of strong electric fields to integrated circuits
concepts.explanation: Effects of static electric fields and electrostatic discharge (ESD) that can damage semiconductor devices and integrated circuits; importance of ESD precautions.

concepts.name: Capacitors and capacitance (common uses)
concepts.explanation: Capacitor stores electric charge and energy; capacitance is the ratio of charge to potential difference. Common uses include tuning circuits, flash guns, smoothing and filtering.

concepts.name: Electric current
concepts.explanation: Rate of flow of electric charge in a conductor, typically measured in amperes; direction conventionally taken as flow of positive charge.

concepts.name: Sources of emf (mains, cells, thermocouples)
concepts.explanation: Devices that provide electromotive force (emf) or voltage, including batteries (cells), mains supplies, accumulators and thermocouples; their basic characteristics as voltage sources.

concepts.name: Conduction in materials
concepts.explanation: Mechanisms by which different materials conduct electricity: free electrons in metals, ions in electrolytes, and band theory distinctions in semiconductors/insulators.

concepts.name: Capacitance (definition and unit)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative measure of a conductor's ability to store charge: C = Q/V; unit is the farad (F).

concepts.name: Parallel-plate capacitor and capacitance formula
concepts.explanation: Capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor and its dependence on plate area A, separation d, and dielectric: C = εA/d (including effect of dielectric constant).

concepts.name: Charging and discharging a capacitor through a load (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Procedure and analysis for charging a capacitor and discharging it through a lamp or low-voltage DC motor, including measurements and energy/charge calculations.

concepts.name: Capacitor behavior with AC and DC
concepts.explanation: How capacitors respond to alternating current versus direct current: they pass changing (AC) signals but block steady (DC) currents, and the concept of reactance.

concepts.name: Potential difference (voltage) and electromotive force (emf)
concepts.explanation: Concept of potential difference (voltage) measured in volts, and the distinction/use of emf as the energy per unit charge supplied by a source when applied to a circuit.

concepts.name: Rectification of AC
concepts.explanation: Conversion of alternating current to direct current using diodes or rectifier circuits; understanding half-wave and full-wave rectification principles.

concepts.name: Charge carriers
concepts.explanation: Identification of the mobile charges responsible for conduction in different media (electrons, holes, ions) and their role in current flow.

concepts.name: Conduction in ionic solutions (electrolytic conduction) and electrode activity
concepts.explanation: Ionic conduction in solutions via movement of positive and negative ions and the roles of active and inactive electrodes in electrolytic cells.

concepts.name: Conduction in vacuum (electron emission and vacuum tubes)
concepts.explanation: Current flow in vacuum by free electrons emitted from a source (thermionic or field emission) and principles behind vacuum tube conduction.

concepts.name: Conduction in semiconductors: intrinsic and extrinsic; p-type and n-type
concepts.explanation: Semiconductor conduction distinguishing intrinsic (pure) behavior and extrinsic conduction via dopants; formation and roles of p-type (acceptor, holes) and n-type (donor, electrons) materials.

concepts.name: Semiconductor devices and applications (LEDs, integrated circuits, computers)
concepts.explanation: Practical applications of semiconductor materials in LEDs, diodes, transistors and integrated circuits used in computers and electronic devices.

concepts.name: Wheatstone bridge
concepts.explanation: A four-resistor bridge circuit used to measure an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of the bridge; at balance the ratio of two known resistances equals the ratio of the other leg (R1/R2 = R3/Rx). Commonly used as an experimental procedure to determine resistance precisely.

concepts.name: Potentiometer (variable potential divider)
concepts.explanation: A three-terminal resistor with an adjustable contact (wiper) that divides an input voltage to provide a variable output voltage; used for voltage control, sensing, and as an adjustable bias in circuits. Output follows Vout = Vin * (R2/(R1+R2)) for the two resistances formed by the wiper.

concepts.name: Chemical effects of electric current (electrolysis and electroplating)
concepts.explanation: Electric current causes chemical changes in electrolytes (electrolysis); used to deposit metals (electroplating), refine metals (electrorefining), produce gases, and manufacture chemicals. Understanding includes electrode reactions, ions migration, and practical applications.

concepts.name: High-voltage (EHT) power transmission and reduction of I^2R losses
concepts.explanation: Transmitting electrical power at very high voltages (extra-high tension) reduces line current for a given power, thereby lowering resistive (I^2R) losses and allowing more efficient long-distance transmission and smaller conductor sizes.

concepts.name: Thermostat (temperature control device)
concepts.explanation: A control device that maintains a desired temperature by sensing temperature and switching heating or cooling elements on and off (feedback control); includes mechanical (bimetallic) and electronic types, and concepts of setpoint and hysteresis.

concepts.name: Thermal cut-out (fail-safe device)
concepts.explanation: A safety device that interrupts electrical power when temperature exceeds a safe limit (e.g., thermal fuse, thermal overload switch) to prevent overheating and fire; used in heaters, motors, and household appliances.

concepts.name: Definition of electrical resistance and unit
concepts.explanation: Resistance as a measure of opposition to current flow (ratio of voltage to current) and its SI unit, the ohm (Ω).

concepts.name: Measurement of resistance with an ohmmeter
concepts.explanation: Procedure and interpretation for using an ohmmeter to measure the resistance of components and conductors, including practical considerations (leads, zeroing).

concepts.name: Use of a metre bridge to determine resistance
concepts.explanation: Technique for measuring an unknown resistance using a metre bridge (Wheatstone bridge principle) and associated calculations.

concepts.name: p-n junction diode: forward and reverse bias behavior
concepts.explanation: Fundamental behavior of a semiconductor p-n junction under forward and reverse bias, including direction of current flow and demonstration using a lamp or indicator.

concepts.name: Thermistor behavior
concepts.explanation: Temperature-dependent resistor (NTC/PTC) and its characteristic change in resistance with temperature; demonstration and basic applications.

concepts.name: Simple fuse rating calculations
concepts.explanation: Calculation of appropriate fuse ratings for circuits by relating expected current draw to fuse selection to provide overcurrent protection.

concepts.name: Wiring a plug (live, neutral, earth connections)
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure and safety considerations for correctly wiring a mains plug, identifying live, neutral and earth conductors and secure connections.

concepts.name: Electricity at home: fuse box and meter
concepts.explanation: Common domestic electricity components (fuse box/consumer unit, electricity meter), their functions and basic operation within household supply systems.

concepts.name: Electrical safety practices
concepts.explanation: Key safety principles for working with and around electrical systems (insulation, earthing, isolation, safe handling) relevant to domestic and laboratory contexts.

concepts.name: Equivalent resistance of resistors in series and parallel
concepts.explanation: Calculation and derivation of the combined resistance for resistors connected in series (R_eq = ΣR_i) and in parallel (1/R_eq = Σ1/R_i), including using Ohm's law and circuit analysis to derive formulas and solve for currents and voltages in simple circuits.

concepts.name: Potential divider
concepts.explanation: A circuit of two or more resistors in series that produces an output voltage equal to a fixed fraction of the input voltage; for two resistors Vout = Vin * R2/(R1+R2). Used for voltage scaling, reference generation, and interfacing sensors.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday's law and Lenz's law)
concepts.explanation: Induction of an emf in a circuit due to changing magnetic flux; quantitative relation (Faraday's law) and direction of induced emf opposing flux change (Lenz's law).

concepts.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor (F = IℓB) and Lorentz force (F = qvB)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic force experienced by a conductor carrying current in a magnetic field (F = IℓB) and the equivalent force on a moving charge (Lorentz force F = qv × B); includes direction (right-hand rule) and dependence on current, length, and field strength.

concepts.name: Magnetic field due to current-carrying conductors (straight wire, loop, solenoid)
concepts.explanation: Patterns and qualitative description of magnetic fields produced by a long straight current, a current loop, and a solenoid; solenoid approximates a bar-magnet field inside.

concepts.name: Magnetic flux and magnetic flux density (Φ = BA, B)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux Φ as the product of magnetic flux density B and area A (for uniform fields) and the concept of magnetic flux density B (directional field strength, units tesla).

concepts.name: Definition of the ampere (force between currents)
concepts.explanation: Operational definition of the ampere in terms of the magnetic force between parallel currents; links current to magnetic interaction.

concepts.name: Forces between currents (parallel currents attraction/repulsion)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative behavior of forces between current-carrying conductors (parallel currents attract, antiparallel repel) and its role in defining magnetic interactions between circuits.

concepts.name: Joule heating (heating effect of electric current, W = I²Rt)
concepts.explanation: Conversion of electrical energy into heat in a resistor; energy dissipated W = I²Rt and implications for power and heating in circuits.

concepts.name: Electromagnets: construction and uses
concepts.explanation: Creating a magnetic field using coils of current around ferromagnetic cores and typical applications (lifting, relays, solenoids).

concepts.name: Electric motor principle
concepts.explanation: Conversion of electrical energy to mechanical work via magnetic forces on current-carrying conductors in fields (basic motor action).

concepts.name: Generator principle (mechanical to electrical energy)
concepts.explanation: Production of emf and electrical energy by changing magnetic flux through coils (electromagnetic induction applied to generators).

concepts.name: Mutual and self-induction
concepts.explanation: Self-induction: emf induced in a circuit by change in its own current (inductance); mutual induction: emf induced in one circuit due to changing current in a nearby circuit.

concepts.name: Transformers: operation and uses
concepts.explanation: Use of mutual induction to step voltage up or down in AC systems using primary and secondary coils and a magnetic core; role in power distribution.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) and the national grid
concepts.explanation: Characteristics of alternating current (periodic reversal), reasons for AC use in power transmission, and the structure/function of the national grid.

concepts.name: Overcurrent protection devices (fuses and MCBs)
concepts.explanation: Devices that protect circuits from excessive current: fuse (one-time thermal element) and miniature circuit breaker (resettable electromechanical/electronic breaker).

concepts.name: Earthing and bonding (protective earthing)
concepts.explanation: Connecting conductive parts to earth to prevent dangerous voltages and bonding to ensure equipotential among exposed conductive parts for safety.

concepts.name: Ring and radial domestic circuit topologies
concepts.explanation: Two common wiring layouts in buildings: ring circuits (looped supply providing two paths) and radial circuits (single path), with differences in load distribution and protection.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) as unit of electrical energy
concepts.explanation: Practical unit of electrical energy equal to one kilowatt of power used for one hour, used for energy billing and quantifying consumption.

concepts.name: Alternating current and voltage (AC)
concepts.explanation: Electric current and voltage that vary periodically with time (typically sinusoidally), characterised by amplitude, frequency and period; describes how voltage and current change with time in AC circuits.

concepts.name: Peak and RMS values of alternating voltages and currents
concepts.explanation: Definitions and relationships for the maximum (peak) value of an AC waveform and the root-mean-square (RMS) value which gives the effective DC-equivalent voltage or current (for a sinusoid Vrms = Vpeak/√2).

concepts.name: Using an oscilloscope to display and measure AC waveforms
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure to observe time-varying voltages and currents on an oscilloscope, including measuring peak, period/frequency and waveform shape of AC signals.

concepts.name: Structure and principle of operation of a transformer
concepts.explanation: Physical construction (primary and secondary windings on a magnetic core) and operating principle where alternating current in the primary produces a changing magnetic flux that induces a voltage in the secondary; turns ratio determines step-up or step-down behaviour.

concepts.name: Qualitative effects of inductors on AC circuits
concepts.explanation: How inductors respond to alternating currents (they oppose changes in current, store energy in magnetic fields, and alter amplitude and phase of AC signals) described qualitatively without requiring mathematical phase relations.

concepts.name: Applications of inductors in electrical circuits
concepts.explanation: Common uses of inductors such as chokes and filters, energy storage in magnetic fields, and use in transformers and tuning circuits.

concepts.name: Joule's law (electrical heating)
concepts.explanation: The relationship that the heat produced (or temperature rise) in a conductor is proportional to the square of the current (Δθ ∝ I^2) for a given resistance and time; used to predict and verify thermal effects of electric current.

concepts.name: Resistivity and its measurement for a wire
concepts.explanation: The property of a material that quantifies how strongly it opposes electric current (ρ), and the experimental procedure to determine ρ using measurements of a wire's resistance, length and cross-sectional area (ρ = R A / L).

concepts.name: Temperature dependence of resistance in metallic conductors
concepts.explanation: The characteristic variation of a metallic conductor's electrical resistance with temperature (typically increasing with temperature for metals), and experimental methods to investigate and quantify this relationship.

concepts.name: Thermistor resistance–temperature relationship
concepts.explanation: The specific dependence of a thermistor's electrical resistance on temperature, R(T), usually strongly non‑linear and characterized for sensors and circuits.

concepts.name: Measuring thermistor resistance vs temperature (experimental procedure)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to vary and control a thermistor's temperature, measure resistance at multiple temperatures, record data, and control systematic errors.

concepts.name: Using Ohm's law to determine resistance
concepts.explanation: Applying R = V/I (and related circuit methods such as potential dividers) to calculate an unknown resistance from measured voltage and current during experiments.

concepts.name: Calibration of a thermistor as a temperature sensor
concepts.explanation: Deriving a calibration curve or conversion equation (resistance or voltage to temperature), including methods to linearize or fit the non‑linear R(T) behavior for practical use.

concepts.name: Electrical resistance and resistivity
concepts.explanation: Resistance is the measure of how much a component opposes current (R = V/I); resistivity is a material property describing how strongly a material resists current flow and depends on material and temperature.

concepts.name: Potential difference (voltage, V)
concepts.explanation: The work done per unit charge to move a test charge between two points in an electric field; the driving force that causes current to flow, measured in volts (V).

concepts.name: Measuring I–V characteristics (experimental procedure)
concepts.explanation: A laboratory method for recording current at varying applied voltages across a component, including safe circuit setup, use of variable power supply, ammeter and voltmeter placement, and plotting I versus V.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic of a metallic (ohmic) conductor
concepts.explanation: The linear I–V behaviour of metals at approximately constant temperature where current is proportional to voltage and resistance is constant.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic of a filament bulb (temperature‑dependent resistance)
concepts.explanation: A non‑ohmic I–V curve where resistance increases with filament temperature as current rises, producing a curved I–V plot (current does not scale linearly with voltage).

concepts.name: Ionic conduction in electrolytes (copper sulphate solution with copper electrodes)
concepts.explanation: Conduction by movement of ions in an electrolyte; the I–V behaviour can show nonlinearity due to electrode processes, concentration polarization, and decomposition thresholds in a copper sulfate solution with copper electrodes.

concepts.name: I–V characteristic of a semiconductor diode
concepts.explanation: The rectifying I–V behaviour of a p–n junction device showing very low current in reverse bias and an exponential increase in forward current beyond a threshold (cut‑in) voltage.

concepts.name: Millikan oil drop experiment (measurement of elementary charge)
concepts.explanation: Experimental method to measure the quantized value of the electron charge by balancing gravitational, buoyant and electric forces on charged oil droplets.

concepts.name: X-ray production and properties
concepts.explanation: Generation of X-rays by high-energy electron interactions (e.g., braking radiation and characteristic X-rays) and their penetrating electromagnetic properties and uses.

concepts.name: Cathode ray tube (CRT) and television
concepts.explanation: Vacuum tube device in which thermionically emitted electrons are accelerated and deflected to form visual images; historical basis for television displays and other CRT applications.

concepts.name: Cathode ray oscilloscope (CRO) — operation and uses
concepts.explanation: Instrument using an electron beam deflected on a fluorescent screen to display electrical signals in time, including measurement and visualization of waveforms (applications: ECG, EEG).
concepts.broader_concept: Electron beam devices and signal visualization

concepts.name: Photoelectric effect (demonstration with zinc plate and electroscope)
concepts.explanation: Observation that light incident on certain metal surfaces (e.g., zinc) can eject electrons, demonstrated by discharge/change of charge on an electroscope; shows threshold frequency and particle nature of light.

concepts.name: Production of an electron beam using a cathode ray tube
concepts.explanation: Generation of a focused beam of electrons by thermionic emission and acceleration in a vacuum tube (CRT), used to demonstrate properties of electrons and to form images on screens.
concepts.broader_concept: The Electron / Cathode Ray Tube Experiments

concepts.name: Deflection of electron beams by electric and magnetic fields
concepts.explanation: The transverse acceleration (deflection) of moving electrons when subjected to external electric or magnetic fields, used to measure charge-to-mass ratio and demonstrate Lorentz force effects.
concepts.broader_concept: Electron motion in electric and magnetic fields

concepts.name: Uses and hazards of X-rays
concepts.explanation: Practical applications of X-rays in medicine (diagnostic radiography, CT) and industry (non-destructive testing), together with associated biological hazards and radiation safety principles.

concepts.name: Sound track in films (sound recording and reproduction)
concepts.explanation: Principles of recording, encoding, and reproducing sound for film, including conversion of mechanical vibrations to electrical signals and playback synchronization with images.

concepts.name: Electron (elementary charge and properties)
concepts.explanation: The electron as the fundamental (indivisible for chemical processes) carrier of negative charge; its elementary charge, basic mass, and role as a primary subatomic particle.

concepts.name: Atomic structure: electron mass and location
concepts.explanation: The placement of electrons in atoms (electron shells/cloud) and the comparative mass of the electron relative to protons and neutrons; relevance to atomic properties.

concepts.name: Photocell (photoelectric effect) demonstration
concepts.explanation: Use of a photocell to demonstrate the photoelectric effect: emission of electrons from a material when illuminated, threshold frequency, and dependence on light frequency and intensity.

concepts.name: Electronvolt and multiples (eV, keV, MeV, GeV)
concepts.explanation: Definition of the electronvolt as the energy gained by an electron accelerated through one volt, conversion to joules, and common multiples used in atomic and particle physics.
concepts.broader_concept: Energy Units in Atomic and Particle Physics

concepts.name: Thermionic emission and electron beam production
concepts.explanation: Principle of thermionic emission: electrons emitted from a heated cathode; application to producing focused beams of electrons (electron guns) for experiments and devices.

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) components and operation
concepts.explanation: Structure and functioning of a cathode ray tube: cathode, anode, electron beam formation, deflection systems (electric/magnetic), and fluorescent screen to visualize electron beams.

concepts.name: Photon energy relation (E = h f)
concepts.explanation: Quantization of electromagnetic energy: the energy of a single photon equals Planck's constant times its frequency (E = h f), used to calculate energies exchanged in photoelectric and other quantum processes.

concepts.name: Deflection of cathode rays by electric and magnetic fields
concepts.explanation: The forces exerted by electric and magnetic fields on moving charged particles cause measurable deflections of cathode rays (electron beams); principles used to determine charge sign and charge-to-mass ratio.
concepts.broader_concept: Charged particles in electric and magnetic fields

concepts.name: Cathode rays as electron beams
concepts.explanation: Identification of cathode rays as streams of electrons with mass and negative charge, based on deflection and other experimental evidence.

concepts.name: Radioactive decay law and half-life
concepts.explanation: Quantitative description of spontaneous nuclear decay: activity A = λN, decay constant λ, and relationship between half-life T1/2 and λ (T1/2 = ln2/λ).

concepts.name: Types of radioactive emissions (alpha, beta, gamma) and properties
concepts.explanation: Classification and characteristic properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation including charge, mass (where applicable), penetrating power and ionising ability.

concepts.name: Nuclear structure, mass number A, atomic number Z and isotopes
concepts.explanation: Composition of the atomic nucleus as protons and neutrons, notation A_Z X, definition of atomic number Z and mass number A, and concept of isotopes.

concepts.name: Nuclear reactions and mass–energy conservation (E=mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Interpretation of nuclear reactions including conservation of nucleon number and charge, and the conversion between mass and energy using E = mc^2.

concepts.name: Principles of nuclear fission and reactor components
concepts.explanation: Basic mechanism of fission, chain reactions and description of reactor components (fuel, moderator, control rods, shielding) and reactor operation issues.

concepts.name: Nuclear fusion and stellar energy
concepts.explanation: Fundamental fusion processes as the Sun's energy source and the basic principles and challenges of controlled fusion reactors and weapons.

concepts.name: Detection of ionising radiation (Geiger–Müller and solid-state detectors)
concepts.explanation: Principles of operation of common ionising radiation detectors such as the Geiger–Müller tube and solid-state detectors, and their use to measure activity and background radiation.

concepts.name: Radiation health hazards and protection
concepts.explanation: Sources and health risks of ionising radiation (e.g., radon, medical X-rays), concepts of background radiation, shielding and safe disposal of radioactive waste.

concepts.name: Applications of radioisotopes
concepts.explanation: Practical uses of radioactive isotopes including medical imaging and therapy, food irradiation, agricultural uses, radiocarbon dating, smoke detectors and industrial applications.

concepts.name: Bohr model and atomic energy levels
concepts.explanation: Descriptive Bohr model of the atom with quantised energy levels and photon emission/absorption corresponding to energy differences (hf = E2 − E1).

concepts.name: Emission line spectra and continuous spectra (spectroscopy)
concepts.explanation: Distinction between line spectra (discrete atomic transitions) and continuous spectra; use of spectroscopy as a tool to study atomic structure and composition.

concepts.name: Einstein's photoelectric law
concepts.explanation: Relationship describing photoelectron kinetic energy: maximum kinetic energy = hf − φ, where hf is photon energy and φ is work function; supports particle nature of light.

concepts.name: Threshold frequency (photoelectric effect)
concepts.explanation: Minimum frequency of incident light required to eject electrons from a material; below this frequency no photoelectrons are emitted regardless of intensity.

concepts.name: X-ray generation by high-energy electrons (electron–target collisions)
concepts.explanation: Production of X-rays when energetic electrons decelerate or eject inner-shell electrons in a target, yielding bremsstrahlung and characteristic X-rays.

concepts.name: Hot-cathode X-ray tube: principles of operation
concepts.explanation: Operation of an X-ray tube with a heated cathode emitting electrons, high-voltage acceleration toward a target, and production of X-rays at the anode.

concepts.name: Properties of X-rays: electromagnetic nature, ionisation and penetration
concepts.explanation: Key properties of X-rays: they are high-energy electromagnetic radiation, capable of ionising matter and penetrating materials to varying degrees depending on energy and thickness.

concepts.name: Experimental identification of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
concepts.explanation: Practical criteria used to distinguish radiation types experimentally: deflection in electric/magnetic fields, relative ionisation, and penetration through absorbers.

concepts.name: Rutherford scattering experiment (principle)
concepts.explanation: Core idea of Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment demonstrating a small, dense, positively charged nucleus and leading to the nuclear model of the atom.

concepts.name: Factors determining biological effect of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: The determinants of radiation harm to humans: type of radiation, activity of the source (in Bq), duration of exposure (time), and the radiosensitivity of the tissue irradiated.

concepts.name: Radioactive activity and the becquerel (Bq)
concepts.explanation: Activity quantifies the rate of radioactive decays from a source (SI unit: becquerel, 1 Bq = 1 decay per second) and is used to assess source strength and exposure potential.

concepts.name: Types of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Specific forms of ionising radiation (e.g., X-rays, alpha, beta, gamma, neutron emissions) with differing penetration, ionisation power, and biological effects.

concepts.name: Environmental (background) radiation
concepts.explanation: Radiation present in the environment from natural and artificial sources; a context for understanding typical exposures and incremental risks.

concepts.name: Elementary particles (leptons and quarks)
concepts.explanation: Classification of the fundamental constituents of matter into leptons and quarks, including the idea that these are not made of smaller particles in the standard model context.

concepts.name: Fundamental interactions (strong, electromagnetic, weak)
concepts.explanation: The three key forces relevant to particle behaviour: the strong interaction binding quarks in hadrons, the electromagnetic interaction between charged particles, and the weak interaction responsible for certain particle decays.

concepts.name: Conservation laws in particle reactions
concepts.explanation: Conserved quantities in particle processes such as energy, momentum, electric charge, baryon number and lepton number, and their use to determine allowed reactions.

concepts.name: Hadrons: baryons and mesons
concepts.explanation: Classification of composite particles made of quarks: baryons (three quarks) and mesons (quark–antiquark pairs), with examples (proton, neutron, pion).

concepts.name: Quark model and quark flavours
concepts.explanation: The model that describes hadrons in terms of constituent quarks with different 'flavours' (up, down, strange, etc.), including how combinations give observed particle charges and quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Antiparticles and annihilation
concepts.explanation: The concept that every particle has an antiparticle with opposite charge; when a particle meets its antiparticle they can annihilate producing photons or other particles.

concepts.name: Pair production
concepts.explanation: The process where a photon converts its energy into a particle–antiparticle pair (e.g., electron and positron) in the vicinity of a nucleus, with energy threshold determined by rest masses.

concepts.name: Mass–energy equivalence (E = mc^2) and rest energy
concepts.explanation: Relation between mass and energy establishing that mass can be converted into energy and vice versa, used to compute energies associated with particle creation and annihilation.

concepts.name: Particle decay and mean lifetime
concepts.explanation: Description of unstable particles that decay into other particles, characterized by decay modes, mean lifetime (or half-life) and exponential decay statistics.

concepts.name: Beta decay and the neutrino
concepts.explanation: Beta decay processes (β− and β+) in which a neutron converts to a proton or vice versa mediated by the weak interaction, accompanied by emission of an electron or positron and an (anti)neutrino.

concepts.name: Particle detectors: cloud chamber and bubble chamber
concepts.explanation: Experimental devices that make charged-particle tracks visible (cloud/bubble chambers) allowing qualitative and quantitative study of particle trajectories and interactions.

concepts.name: Particle accelerators and colliders
concepts.explanation: Machines that accelerate charged particles to high energies and bring them into collision to produce and study new particles; includes basic principles of operation and purpose.

concepts.name: Feynman diagrams as interaction representations
concepts.explanation: Graphical shorthand used to represent particle interactions and exchanges of force carriers, illustrating initial and final particles and interaction vertices.

concepts.name: Fundamental Forces of Nature
concepts.explanation: The four fundamental interactions (strong, weak, electromagnetic, gravitational) that govern particle behavior; includes properties such as range, relative strength, and which particles each force acts on.

concepts.name: Conservation of Energy and Momentum in Nuclear Reactions
concepts.explanation: Application of conservation laws to nuclear and particle reactions: total energy and vector momentum must be conserved, which constrains reaction products and can imply the existence of unseen particles.

concepts.name: Mass–Energy Equivalence and Conversion (E=mc^2)
concepts.explanation: The quantitative relation between mass and energy (E=mc^2), and its application to converting mass into energy (nuclear binding energy, Q-values) and converting energy into mass (pair production).

concepts.name: Quark Model
concepts.explanation: The model that describes hadrons as combinations of six fundamental quark flavors (up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom), including quark charges and the composition rules for baryons (three quarks) and mesons (quark–antiquark).

concepts.name: Particle Classification: Leptons, Baryons, Mesons, and Antiparticles
concepts.explanation: Definitions and distinguishing properties of particle families: leptons (point-like, not subject to strong force), baryons (three-quark hadrons), mesons (quark–antiquark), and the existence of corresponding antiparticles.

concepts.name: Pair Production and Annihilation
concepts.explanation: Processes in which energy converts to a particle–antiparticle pair (e.g., γ → e+ + e−) and the reverse annihilation (e+ + e− → 2γ), with conservation of charge, energy, and momentum requirements.

concepts.name: Neutrino and Momentum Conservation in Beta Decay
concepts.explanation: The role of the (anti)neutrino introduced to account for missing energy and momentum in beta decay; explains why a third particle is required if observed decay products do not conserve momentum.

concepts.name: Particle Production in High-Energy Collisions
concepts.explanation: How increasing collision energy (e.g., in proton–proton collisions) permits the creation of more and heavier particles; higher available energy leads to a larger variety of produced particles ('particle zoo').

concepts.name: Energy Scales and Unit Conversions in Particle Physics
concepts.explanation: Understanding and converting common energy and mass units used in particle physics (e.g., eV, MeV) and making quantitative estimates of magnitudes relevant to reactions and accelerator energies.

concepts.name: Cockcroft–Walton Nuclear Transmutation Experiment
concepts.explanation: The historical experiment demonstrating artificial splitting/transmutation of nuclei by accelerating protons (H) into lithium to produce helium (H + Li → He + He + Q), illustrating artificial nuclear reactions and early accelerator use.

concepts.name: Series and Parallel Resistor Combinations
concepts.explanation: Rules and formulas for calculating equivalent resistance in series (R_eq = sum R) and parallel (1/R_eq = sum 1/R) connections and implications for current and voltage distribution.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL)
concepts.explanation: Conservation of charge at a circuit node: the algebraic sum of currents entering and leaving a junction is zero; used for circuit analysis.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL)
concepts.explanation: The algebraic sum of potential differences (voltage drops and rises) around any closed loop in a circuit equals zero; used to solve multi-loop circuits.

concepts.name: Electromotive Force (EMF) and Internal Resistance
concepts.explanation: Definition of EMF as the open-circuit potential of a source, modelling a real cell/battery as an ideal EMF in series with internal resistance r, and using V_load = E - Ir to analyse terminal voltage under load.

concepts.name: Electrical Power and Energy Calculations
concepts.explanation: Formulas for instantaneous and average electrical power (P = VI, P = I^2R, P = V^2/R) and electrical energy (E = Pt, units and billing kWh), including energy transfer in resistive circuits.

concepts.name: Resistivity and Conductivity (including Temperature Dependence)
concepts.explanation: Material property resistivity ρ and conductivity σ, relation R = ρL/A, and how resistivity of conductors/semiconductors varies with temperature.

concepts.name: Voltmeter–Ammeter Measurement Methods and Meter Loading
concepts.explanation: Procedures for measuring current and voltage with ammeters and voltmeters (correct series/parallel connections), two common methods for measuring resistance (voltmeter-ammeter) and how meter internal resistance affects measurement accuracy.

concepts.name: Potentiometer Principle for Measuring EMF and Internal Resistance
concepts.explanation: Null-balance method using a potentiometer to measure the EMF of a cell without drawing current and to determine internal resistance by comparison methods.

concepts.name: Transformers: Step-up and Step-down and Turns Ratio
concepts.explanation: Operation of ideal transformer, relation between primary and secondary voltages and currents via turns ratio (V_p/V_s = N_p/N_s, I_p/I_s = N_s/N_p), and basic efficiency/loss considerations.

concepts.name: Three-Phase Connections: Star (Y) and Delta (Δ)
concepts.explanation: Configuration and analysis of three-phase systems including line and phase voltages/currents relationships for star and delta connections and basic advantages for power distribution.

concepts.name: Power Factor and Power Factor Correction
concepts.explanation: Distinction among real, apparent and reactive power, definition of power factor (cos φ), effects on system efficiency and methods of correction using capacitors or synchronous devices.

concepts.name: Circuit Protection: Fuses and Circuit Breakers
concepts.explanation: Principles of overcurrent protection devices—fuse operation (melting element) and circuit breaker operation (thermal/magnetic trip), selection criteria and coordination with rated currents.

concepts.name: Earthing (Grounding) and Protective Earth
concepts.explanation: Purpose and methods of earthing to provide a low-resistance path to earth for fault currents, reduce electric shock risk, and stabilize voltages in power systems.

concepts.name: Live, Neutral and Earth Conductors in Domestic Wiring
concepts.explanation: Roles and identification of live (phase), neutral and earth conductors in single-phase domestic supply, standard safety colour coding and correct connection practices.

concepts.name: Electric charge
concepts.explanation: Intrinsic property of matter causing electrical interactions; quantified in coulombs, conserved, and can be positive or negative.

concepts.name: Electric field
concepts.explanation: Field describing the force per unit positive test charge at a point: E = F/q; lines represent direction and strength of electrostatic influence.

concepts.name: Electric potential (voltage)
concepts.explanation: Electric potential is potential energy per unit charge; potential difference (V) between two points equals work done per unit charge moving between them.

concepts.name: Electric potential energy of point charges
concepts.explanation: Work required to assemble a system of charges; for two point charges U = k q1 q2 / r, relates to potential difference and conservative electrostatic forces.

concepts.name: Drift velocity and current relation
concepts.explanation: Microscopic relation between current and carrier motion: I = n e A v_d, where n is charge carrier density, e charge, A cross-sectional area, v_d drift speed.

concepts.name: Resistance and resistivity
concepts.explanation: Resistance R quantifies opposition to current; R = ρ L / A where ρ is resistivity, L length and A cross-sectional area; depends on material and temperature.

concepts.name: Series and parallel resistor networks
concepts.explanation: Rules for combining resistors: series R_eq = R1+R2+...; parallel 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...; implications for current and voltage distribution.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's circuit laws
concepts.explanation: Two rules for circuit analysis: junction rule (ΣI_in = ΣI_out) and loop rule (ΣΔV around closed loop = 0), used to solve complex circuits.

concepts.name: Electromotive force and internal resistance
concepts.explanation: Cell EMF ε is open-circuit potential; terminal voltage under load V = ε - I r where r is internal resistance; affects delivered voltage and power.

concepts.name: Electrical power and energy
concepts.explanation: Power is rate of energy transfer: P = V I = I^2 R = V^2 / R; electrical energy delivered E = P t (or use QV), and heating loss described by Joule's law Q = I^2 R t.

concepts.name: Using ammeters and voltmeters
concepts.explanation: Procedures for measuring current (ammeter in series, low internal resistance) and voltage (voltmeter in parallel, high internal resistance); accounting for meter errors in circuits.

concepts.name: Capacitance of a capacitor
concepts.explanation: Capacitance C = Q/V measures a capacitor's ability to store charge; for parallel-plate C = ε0 A / d (with dielectric C = κ ε0 A / d).

concepts.name: Charging and discharging RC circuits
concepts.explanation: Transient behavior of capacitor-resistor circuits: charge and voltage change exponentially with time constant τ = R C; equations q(t)=Q(1-e^{-t/RC}), discharging q(t)=Q e^{-t/RC}.

concepts.name: Dielectrics and effect on capacitance
concepts.explanation: Insertion of a dielectric increases capacitance by factor κ (relative permittivity) by reducing effective electric field and allowing more charge at same voltage.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) basics and mains supply
