concepts.explanation: A conceptual instrument that infers temperature from pressure or volume of a dilute gas, providing a practical route to the thermodynamic temperature scale.

concepts.name: Standard Thermometer (Reference Thermometer)
concepts.explanation: A designated thermometer used as the reference for temperature measurements in a lab or school, against which other thermometers are compared and calibrated.

concepts.name: Laboratory Thermometer (Commercial)
concepts.explanation: A commercially manufactured laboratory thermometer suitable for serving as a school temperature standard and for calibrating other thermometers.

concepts.name: Concept of Heat
concepts.explanation: Heat is energy transferred between systems solely due to a temperature difference; measured in joules and distinct from temperature and internal energy.

concepts.name: Heat Equation Q = mcΔT
concepts.explanation: Formula for sensible heating that relates the quantity of heat absorbed or released to mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change.

concepts.name: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.explanation: Fractions can represent the same value when numerator and denominator are scaled by the same factor.

concepts.name: Percent Increase and Decrease
concepts.explanation: Percent change measures how much a quantity grows or shrinks relative to its original value.

concepts.name: Properties of Exponents
concepts.explanation: Rules for multiplying, dividing, and raising powers simplify expressions with exponents.

concepts.name: Factoring Quadratics
concepts.explanation: Rewriting ax^2 + bx + c as a product of binomials to simplify expressions or solve equations.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions and Graphs
concepts.explanation: Quadratics model parabolic relationships; key features include vertex, axis of symmetry, and intercepts.

concepts.name: Function Notation and Evaluation
concepts.explanation: Using f(x) to denote a function clarifies inputs and outputs and supports evaluation and composition.

concepts.name: Transformations of Functions
concepts.explanation: Shifts, reflections, stretches, and compressions alter a function’s graph via changes to its equation.

concepts.name: Right Triangle Trigonometric Ratios
concepts.explanation: Sine, cosine, and tangent relate side lengths to angles in right triangles.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics: Mean, Median, Mode
concepts.explanation: Measures of center summarize data distribution; each highlights different aspects of typical value.

concepts.name: Variance and Standard Deviation
concepts.explanation: These quantify spread by measuring average squared deviation and its square root from the mean.

concepts.name: Probability Rules: Addition and Multiplication
concepts.explanation: Rules combine event probabilities for unions and intersections, assuming mutually exclusive or independent events as applicable.

concepts.name: Conditional Probability and Independence
concepts.explanation: Probability of an event given another; independence occurs when one event does not change the likelihood of the other.

concepts.name: Random Variables and Expected Value
concepts.explanation: A random variable assigns numerical outcomes; expected value is its long-run average.

concepts.name: Limits of Functions
concepts.explanation: Limits describe function behavior near a point and underpin continuity and calculus.

concepts.name: Derivative as Rate of Change
concepts.explanation: The derivative measures instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line.

concepts.name: Definite Integral and Area Under a Curve
concepts.explanation: The definite integral accumulates quantities and computes net area between a curve and the x-axis.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
concepts.explanation: Connects differentiation and integration, linking antiderivatives to definite integrals.

concepts.name: Sequences and Series (Arithmetic and Geometric)
concepts.explanation: Arithmetic sequences change by a constant difference; geometric by a constant ratio; series sum their terms.

concepts.name: Mathematical Induction
concepts.explanation: A proof technique establishing statements for all integers by verifying a base case and an inductive step.

concepts.name: Permutations and Combinations
concepts.explanation: Counting methods that enumerate arrangements (order matters) and selections (order does not).

concepts.name: Graph Theory Basics
concepts.explanation: Graphs model relationships using vertices and edges; paths and cycles capture connectivity.

concepts.name: Ratios and Unit Rates
concepts.explanation: A ratio compares two quantities; a unit rate compares per one unit of the second quantity.

concepts.name: Slope of a Line
concepts.explanation: Slope measures the rate of change of a line, computed as rise over run.

concepts.name: Function Concept
concepts.explanation: A function assigns each input exactly one output, often represented by tables, graphs, or equations.

concepts.name: Transformations: Rigid Motions
concepts.explanation: Translations, rotations, and reflections that preserve distance and angle measure, establishing congruence.

concepts.name: Trigonometric Ratios (SOH-CAH-TOA)
concepts.explanation: In right triangles, sine, cosine, and tangent relate side lengths to angles for solving triangles.

concepts.name: Measures of Center
concepts.explanation: Mean, median, and mode summarize the central tendency of a data set.

concepts.name: Thermal Convection
concepts.explanation: Heat transfer by the bulk motion of a fluid, driven by density differences or external forcing; includes natural and forced convection.

concepts.name: Counting within 100
concepts.explanation: Count forward and backward, read and write numbers to 100, and compare using >, <, and =.

concepts.name: Place Value to 1,000
concepts.explanation: Understand hundreds, tens, and ones to read, write, and compare three-digit numbers.

concepts.name: Fraction Equivalence and Comparison
concepts.explanation: Recognize and generate equivalent fractions and compare fractions with like denominators or numerators.

concepts.name: Decimal Place Value and Rounding
concepts.explanation: Read, write, compare, and round decimals to thousandths; relate decimals to fractions.

concepts.name: Integer Operations on the Number Line
concepts.explanation: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide integers using number line models and rules.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions and Vertex Form
concepts.explanation: Analyze quadratics in vertex form to identify vertex, axis of symmetry, and transformations.

concepts.name: Right Triangle Trigonometry
concepts.explanation: Use sine, cosine, and tangent to find missing sides or angles in right triangles.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics and Normal Distribution
concepts.explanation: Summarize data with center and spread, interpret z-scores, and use properties of the normal curve.

concepts.name: Limits and Continuity
concepts.explanation: Evaluate limits from graphs, tables, and algebra; determine continuity at a point.

concepts.name: Heat Pump (Refrigerator) Operation
concepts.explanation: A device that transfers thermal energy from a colder region to a warmer region by doing work; uses a vapor-compression cycle with evaporator, compressor, condenser, and expansion valve to move heat against the temperature gradient.

concepts.name: U-Value (Thermal Transmittance) in Buildings
concepts.explanation: A measure of the rate of heat transfer through a building element per unit area per unit temperature difference (W m^-2 K^-1); lower U-values indicate better insulation and are used to estimate domestic heat losses.

concepts.name: Evaporative Cooling in Perspiration
concepts.explanation: Cooling of the body when sweat evaporates, removing energy equal to the latent heat of vaporization from the skin; effectiveness depends on humidity, airflow, and surface area.

concepts.name: Heat Loss in Domestic Hot Water Systems
concepts.explanation: Understanding and reducing heat losses from hot water tanks and pipes via conduction and convection using insulation, thermostatic control, and efficient system design.

concepts.name: Solar Water Heating System (Active)
concepts.explanation: A system that uses solar collectors, a pump, and a storage tank to heat water using solar energy, often with a heat exchanger.

concepts.name: Passive Solar Heating of Buildings
concepts.explanation: Building design that captures and stores solar energy without mechanical devices using orientation, glazing, and thermal mass.

concepts.name: Flat-Plate Solar Collector
concepts.explanation: A solar thermal collector with a dark absorber plate and transparent cover that transfers absorbed solar energy to a working fluid.

concepts.name: U-value (Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient)
concepts.explanation: A measure of heat transfer through a building element per unit area per degree temperature difference; lower values indicate better insulation.

concepts.name: Radiator Heating via Convection
concepts.explanation: Space heating where hot-water radiators warm air, establishing convection currents that distribute heat in a room.

concepts.name: Thermostat-Controlled Heating
concepts.explanation: Feedback control of room or water temperature using a thermostat with setpoint and hysteresis to switch heating devices.

concepts.name: Solar Cooker
concepts.explanation: A device that concentrates or traps solar radiation to cook food, demonstrating solar thermal conversion and greenhouse effect.

concepts.name: Evacuated Tube Solar Collector
concepts.explanation: A solar thermal collector using evacuated glass tubes to minimize convective and conductive losses and achieve higher temperatures.

concepts.name: Heat Loss Pathways in Buildings
concepts.explanation: Analysis of heat loss through walls, roof, windows, floors, and ventilation via conduction, convection, and radiation.

concepts.name: Heat Energy Calculation (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Compute the thermal energy transferred using mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change.

concepts.name: Simple Calorimetry Experiment
concepts.explanation: Design and carry out a basic mixing-water experiment to measure heat transfer and estimate specific heat capacity.

concepts.name: Temperature Increase Due to Heat
concepts.explanation: Adding heat to a substance raises its temperature in proportion to the heat added and inversely to its mass and specific heat capacity (Q ∝ mΔT).

concepts.name: Difference Between Heat and Temperature
concepts.explanation: Heat is energy in transit between systems; temperature is a measure of average kinetic energy of particles and indicates thermal state.

concepts.name: Temperature Change Due to Heat Transfer (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: Adding heat to a substance raises its temperature and removing heat lowers it, with the change given by Q = mcΔT where m is mass and c is specific heat capacity.

concepts.name: Rate of Heat Conduction in Solids
concepts.explanation: Qualitative comparison of how quickly heat flows through different solids based on material, cross-sectional area, length, and temperature difference; trends consistent with Fourier’s law.

concepts.name: Thermal Conductivity
concepts.explanation: Material property (k) that measures a solid’s ability to conduct heat; higher k implies faster heat transfer; SI units are W m^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: Solar Radiation
concepts.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation emitted by the Sun that transfers energy through space to Earth; treated as thermal radiation in heat transfer contexts.

concepts.name: Thermometer Calibration Curve
concepts.explanation: Constructing a plot of thermometer readings versus true temperature (from a standard) to determine correction factors, linearity, and a calibration equation.

concepts.name: Comparison Calibration Using Standard Mercury Thermometer
concepts.explanation: Calibrating an unknown thermometer by comparing simultaneous readings with a laboratory mercury-in-glass standard to map indicated to true temperatures.

concepts.name: Measurement of Specific Latent Heat of Fusion of Ice
concepts.explanation: Calorimetry procedure: add dried ice at 0°C to warm water in a calorimeter, measure masses and initial/final temperatures, and compute L_f using energy balance where heat lost by water and calorimeter equals heat to melt ice plus warm the meltwater.

concepts.name: Calculating Energy to Boil Water Using Q = m L_v
concepts.explanation: Apply the latent heat relation Q = m L_v, using the specific latent heat of vaporization for water, to determine the energy needed to vaporize a given mass of water at its boiling point.

concepts.name: Wave Speed Equation
concepts.explanation: Relates the speed of a wave to its frequency and wavelength via v = fλ.

concepts.name: Frequency of a Wave
concepts.explanation: Number of oscillations or cycles per second at a point, measured in hertz (Hz).

concepts.name: Period of a Wave
concepts.explanation: Time taken for one complete cycle of oscillation; T = 1/f.

concepts.name: Amplitude of a Wave
concepts.explanation: Maximum displacement from the equilibrium position, linked to wave energy.

concepts.name: Principle of Superposition
concepts.explanation: When two or more waves overlap, the resultant displacement is the vector sum of individual displacements.

concepts.name: Doppler Shift Calculations (Sound)
concepts.explanation: Use of the Doppler formulas f' = f((v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s)) to compute observed frequency for moving sources or observers in a medium.

concepts.name: Astronomical Redshift
concepts.explanation: Increase in observed wavelength of starlight due to recession of the source; quantified by z = Δλ/λ and approximated by v ≈ cz for low speeds.

concepts.name: Slinky Demonstration of Longitudinal and Transverse Waves
concepts.explanation: Using a slinky to produce and observe longitudinal and transverse pulses, illustrating wavelength, amplitude, and speed qualitatively.

concepts.name: Ripple Tank: Measuring Wave Speed and Wavelength
concepts.explanation: Laboratory use of a ripple tank to visualize wavefronts and measure λ and v using v = fλ for surface water waves.

concepts.name: Seismic Waves: P and S Waves
concepts.explanation: Characteristics and propagation of primary (longitudinal) and secondary (transverse) seismic waves through Earth’s interior.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect for Sound
concepts.explanation: Change in observed frequency and wavelength of sound due to relative motion between the source and the observer.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect Calculations (Sound)
concepts.explanation: Applying Doppler effect equations to determine observed frequency for moving source and/or observer without deriving the formulas.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Wave Equation (c = fλ)
concepts.explanation: For electromagnetic waves in vacuum, the speed of light c equals frequency times wavelength, linking how often waves oscillate to their spatial period.

concepts.name: Wave Frequency
concepts.explanation: The number of oscillations per second of a wave, measured in hertz (Hz); determines energy for light and pitch for sound.

concepts.name: Wave Speed (Velocity)
concepts.explanation: The rate at which a wave disturbance travels through a medium or space; for a given medium v = fλ and for EM waves in vacuum v = c.

concepts.name: Wave Amplitude
concepts.explanation: The maximum displacement from equilibrium in a wave, related to the wave’s energy or intensity.

concepts.name: Reflection of Light
concepts.explanation: Change in direction of light at a boundary so it returns to the original medium; obeys the law of reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection).

concepts.name: Refraction of Light
concepts.explanation: Bending of light as it passes between media with different refractive indices due to a change in speed; governed by Snell’s law.

concepts.name: Stationary (Standing) Waves
concepts.explanation: A wave pattern with nodes and antinodes formed by the superposition of two identical waves traveling in opposite directions.

concepts.name: Wavelength–aperture size relation in diffraction
concepts.explanation: The degree of wave spreading depends on the ratio of wavelength to aperture or obstacle size; diffraction is pronounced when the size is comparable to the wavelength and minimal when it is much larger.

concepts.name: Diffraction around obstacles (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative description of wave bending into the geometric shadow when encountering an edge or obstacle, increasing as the obstacle size approaches the wavelength.

concepts.name: Doppler effect for a moving source and stationary observer
concepts.explanation: Quantitative relation for observed frequency change when the source moves and the observer is at rest: f' = f·v/(v ∓ v_s), with higher frequency on approach and lower on recession.

concepts.name: Standing waves in strings
concepts.explanation: Node–antinode patterns form on stretched strings, yielding harmonics and a fundamental frequency set by length, tension, and linear density.

concepts.name: Standing waves in air columns (pipes)
concepts.explanation: Resonant modes in open and closed pipes produce harmonic series determined by pipe length and boundary conditions.

concepts.name: Interference of sound
concepts.explanation: Superposition of coherent sound waves produces regions of constructive and destructive interference.

concepts.name: Sound requires a medium
concepts.explanation: As a mechanical wave, sound cannot propagate in a vacuum and needs a material medium for transmission.

concepts.name: Noise reduction by destructive interference
concepts.explanation: Active noise control uses antiphase sound to cancel unwanted noise through destructive interference.

concepts.name: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string
concepts.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, f1 = (1/2L)√(T/μ), where L is length, T tension, and μ linear density.

concepts.name: Resonant frequencies of open and closed pipes
concepts.explanation: Open pipes support all harmonics; closed pipes support only odd harmonics, with fn set by pipe length and sound speed.

concepts.name: Two-loudspeaker interference demonstration
concepts.explanation: Using two coherent speakers and a signal generator to map nodal and antinodal lines verifies sound interference.

concepts.name: Measurement of sound intensity level with a sound-level meter
concepts.explanation: Procedure to quantify environmental sound in dB using calibrated meters and appropriate weighting scales.

concepts.name: Tuning fork resonance demonstration
concepts.explanation: Using tuning forks to demonstrate resonance by driving another fork or an air column at its natural frequency.

concepts.name: Dog whistle (ultrasound)
concepts.explanation: A source of ultrasonic sound above 20 kHz, inaudible to humans but audible to some animals.

concepts.name: Sound Intensity (Definition and Unit)
concepts.explanation: Rate of sound energy crossing unit area perpendicular to the wave direction; measured in watts per square meter (W m^-2).

concepts.name: Frequency of a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Fundamental frequency of a stretched string is f = (1/2L)√(T/μ), where L is length, T is tension, and μ is linear mass density.

concepts.name: Harmonics in Strings and Pipes
concepts.explanation: Standing wave modes in resonators: strings support all integer harmonics; open pipes support all integers; closed pipes support odd-numbered harmonics.

concepts.name: Fundamental Frequency–Length Relationship
concepts.explanation: For many resonators (strings, air columns), the fundamental frequency is inversely proportional to the effective length (f ∝ 1/L) under fixed wave speed/boundary conditions.

concepts.name: 3 dB Rule for Intensity Doubling
concepts.explanation: Doubling the sound intensity increases the sound intensity level by approximately 3 dB: ΔL = 10 log10(2) ≈ 3 dB.

concepts.name: Experiment: Measurement of the Speed of Sound in Air
concepts.explanation: Determine the speed of sound using methods such as resonance in air columns, time-of-flight, or standing wave interference.

concepts.name: Experiment: Fundamental Frequency vs Length of a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Investigate how the fundamental frequency varies inversely with string length while keeping tension and linear density constant.

concepts.name: Experiment: Fundamental Frequency vs Tension of a Stretched String
concepts.explanation: Investigate how the fundamental frequency varies with the square root of tension while keeping length and linear density constant.

concepts.name: Laws of Refraction (Snell’s Law)
concepts.explanation: The relationship n1 sin i = n2 sin r governing refraction at a boundary between two media, defining how light bends when entering a medium with different refractive index.

concepts.name: Refractive Index in Terms of Speed
concepts.explanation: Defines refractive index using speeds: n = c/v for a medium, or n1/n2 = v2/v1 for two media.

concepts.name: Spherical Mirror Formula
concepts.explanation: The image equation 1/f = 1/u + 1/v for spherical mirrors relating focal length f, object distance u, and image distance v.

concepts.name: Magnification in Geometric Optics
concepts.explanation: Linear magnification given by m = v/u (with sign convention), relating image and object distances to image size and orientation.

concepts.name: Image Formation by Spherical Mirrors
concepts.explanation: Determining real/virtual, inverted/upright images formed by concave and convex mirrors based on object position relative to focal length and radius of curvature.

concepts.name: Apparent Depth Due to Refraction
concepts.explanation: Objects under a refracting surface (e.g., fish in water) appear at a shallower depth due to bending of light at a plane boundary.

concepts.name: Mirage Formation from Refractive Index Gradients
concepts.explanation: Optical path bending in air with temperature gradients creates inferior mirages via continuous refraction and total internal reflection effects.

concepts.name: Prism Reflectors Using Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: Right-angle prisms or corner-cube prisms use total internal reflection to deviate or retroreflect light efficiently without metallic coatings.

concepts.name: Optical Fiber Transmission via Total Internal Reflection
concepts.explanation: Guiding light along a core by repeated total internal reflection at the core–cladding interface for telecommunications and endoscopy.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Snell’s Law with a Ray Box or Laser
concepts.explanation: Procedure to measure incident and refracted angles across a flat interface, plotting sin i vs sin r to determine refractive index.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of the Laws of Reflection
concepts.explanation: Using a ray box and plane mirror to show angle of incidence equals angle of reflection and coplanarity of rays and normal.

concepts.name: Retroreflection in Road Signs
concepts.explanation: Use of microprisms or glass beads to return incident light toward its source, enhancing visibility through retroreflection.

concepts.name: Linear magnification of a lens (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Defines image magnification as the ratio of image to object distance (and height), with sign indicating image orientation.

concepts.name: Power of a lens (P = 1/f)
concepts.explanation: Defines lens power in dioptres as the reciprocal of focal length in metres; positive for converging, negative for diverging lenses.

concepts.name: Power of lenses in contact (P_total = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: The net power of thin lenses in contact equals the algebraic sum of their individual powers.

concepts.name: Thin-Film Interference (Interference Colours)
concepts.explanation: Colour patterns arise from constructive and destructive interference between light reflected at the two surfaces of a thin film, as in soap bubbles and oil films.

concepts.name: Polarization by Absorption (Polaroid Sunglasses)
concepts.explanation: Dichroic filters transmit one plane of polarization and absorb the orthogonal plane, reducing glare from horizontal surfaces.

concepts.name: Stress-Induced Birefringence (Photoelasticity)
concepts.explanation: Mechanical stress in transparent materials induces birefringence, producing coloured fringe patterns between crossed polarizers and revealing stress distribution.

concepts.name: Rainbow Formation
concepts.explanation: Primary and secondary rainbows form via dispersion, refraction, and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets, yielding specific angular positions and colour order.

concepts.name: Diffraction from a Grating (Colours on Compact Discs)
concepts.explanation: Periodic grooves act as a reflection grating, producing angle-dependent constructive interference that creates iridescent colours.

concepts.name: Spectrometer: Operation and Use
concepts.explanation: An optical instrument for measuring angles of deviation, refractive index, and spectral lines using prisms or gratings; includes alignment and calibration procedures.

concepts.name: Young’s Double-Slit Experiment
concepts.explanation: Demonstrates the wave nature of light by producing interference fringes when coherent light passes through two slits; fringe spacing relates to wavelength, slit separation, and screen distance.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet Absorption by the Ozone Layer
concepts.explanation: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV-B and UV-C radiation, illustrating wavelength-dependent interaction of electromagnetic waves with atmospheric gases.

concepts.name: Infrared Thermography (Medical Applications)
concepts.explanation: Use of infrared cameras to detect emitted thermal radiation and map surface temperature variations for diagnostic purposes.

concepts.name: Night Vision Using Infrared Detection
concepts.explanation: Enhances vision in low-light conditions by detecting infrared radiation or amplifying available light to form images.

concepts.name: Greenhouse Effect and Infrared Trapping
concepts.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit terrestrial infrared radiation, reducing radiative heat loss and warming Earth’s surface.

concepts.name: Television Signal Transmission and Reception
concepts.explanation: Images are converted to electrical signals, modulated onto carrier waves, transmitted, received, and demodulated to reconstruct moving pictures and sound.

concepts.name: Photometric Quantities: Luminous Flux and Illuminance
concepts.explanation: Defines lumen and lux to quantify perceived light output and light incident per unit area, foundational to lighting design and measurement.

concepts.name: Diffraction Grating Equation (nλ = d sinθ)
concepts.explanation: Relates wavelength λ, grating spacing d, diffraction order n, and diffraction angle θ to predict or measure spectral lines with a grating.

concepts.name: Derivation of the Diffraction Grating Equation
concepts.explanation: Obtains nλ = d sinθ from path difference and constructive interference conditions for parallel slits in a grating.

concepts.name: Dispersion of Light by a Diffraction Grating
concepts.explanation: Separation of wavelengths due to wavelength-dependent diffraction angles, producing a line spectrum with high angular resolution.

concepts.name: Polarization of Light
concepts.explanation: Restriction of transverse light vibrations to a single plane; demonstrated using polaroids or other polarizing methods.

concepts.name: Recombination of White Light with a Prism
concepts.explanation: Using a second prism (or inverted arrangement) to recombine dispersed colors back into white light.

concepts.name: Additive Color Mixing: Primary, Secondary, and Complementary Colors
concepts.explanation: Combining red, green, and blue light to form secondary colors and complementary pairs; excludes pigment (subtractive) mixing.

concepts.name: Ordering the Electromagnetic Spectrum by Wavelength and Frequency
concepts.explanation: Identifying the relative positions of UV, visible, and IR by increasing/decreasing wavelength and frequency.

concepts.name: Detection of Ultraviolet and Infrared Radiation
concepts.explanation: Methods include fluorescence and photographic detection for UV, and thermopiles/bolometers/IR sensors for IR.

concepts.name: Measurement of Refractive Index of a Liquid or Solid
concepts.explanation: Determine a material's refractive index by measuring refraction (e.g., using Snell’s law or apparent depth displacement).

concepts.name: Measurement of Focal Length of a Converging Lens
concepts.explanation: Find the focal length of a thin converging lens using object-image distances and the lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.

concepts.name: Measurement of Focal Length of a Concave Mirror
concepts.explanation: Determine the focal length of a concave spherical mirror using object-image distances and the mirror formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v.

concepts.name: Measurement of Wavelength of Monochromatic Light
concepts.explanation: Measure the wavelength of a single-color light source from interference or diffraction patterns using relations like λ = d sin(θ) or λ = x d / L.

concepts.name: Ratios and Proportional Relationships
concepts.explanation: Using ratios to compare quantities and solving problems involving unit rates and proportions.

concepts.name: Area of Triangles and Parallelograms
concepts.explanation: Applying formulas for area using base and height and decomposing shapes to find area.

concepts.name: Volume of Right Rectangular Prisms
concepts.explanation: Computing volume using V = lwh and understanding volume as packing with unit cubes.

concepts.name: Experimental and Theoretical Probability
concepts.explanation: Comparing empirical results with expected probabilities and using sample spaces.

concepts.name: Electrification by Induction
concepts.explanation: Charging a conductor without contact by redistributing charges using a nearby charged body, typically with grounding steps.

concepts.name: Electrification by Contact
concepts.explanation: Charging an object through direct contact or rubbing, transferring electrons between materials.

concepts.name: Distribution of Charge on Conductors
concepts.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, excess charge resides on the surface of conductors and concentrates at sharp points; the field inside is zero.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Hazards During Aircraft Refueling
concepts.explanation: Charge buildup on aircraft or fuel lines can cause sparks and fires; mitigated by bonding and grounding procedures.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Hazards in Flour Mills
concepts.explanation: Triboelectric charging of dust and equipment can lead to ignition and explosions; controlled via grounding and humidity.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Attraction of Dust on Television Screens
concepts.explanation: Charged screens (e.g., CRTs) attract airborne dust due to electrostatic forces, illustrating charge accumulation effects.
concepts.broader_concept: Electrostatic Applications and Effects in Daily Life

concepts.name: Static Electricity on Clothes
concepts.explanation: Fabrics become charged by friction, causing clinging and small discharges; demonstrates triboelectric effects.
concepts.broader_concept: Electrostatic Applications and Effects in Daily Life

concepts.name: Place Value in Base Ten
concepts.explanation: Understanding the value of digits based on their position (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands) in base-ten numbers.
concepts.broader_concept: Number and Operations in Base Ten

concepts.name: Multi-digit Addition and Subtraction with Regrouping
concepts.explanation: Adding and subtracting three- and four-digit numbers by composing or decomposing units (regrouping).

concepts.name: Multiplication as Equal Groups
concepts.explanation: Interpreting multiplication as combining equal-sized groups and relating it to repeated addition.

concepts.name: Division as Sharing and Grouping
concepts.explanation: Interpreting division as sharing equally or forming equal groups, and relating it to multiplication.

concepts.name: Decimal Place Value to Thousandths
concepts.explanation: Reading, writing, and comparing decimals and understanding place value relationships to thousandths.
concepts.broader_concept: Number and Operations in Base Ten

concepts.name: Unit Rate and Proportional Relationships
concepts.explanation: Determining unit rates and using them to solve problems involving proportional relationships.

concepts.name: Operations with Integers
concepts.explanation: Adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing positive and negative integers using number lines and rules.

concepts.name: Writing and Evaluating Algebraic Expressions
concepts.explanation: Using variables, constants, and operations to write expressions and evaluate them for given values.

concepts.name: Solving One-Step Linear Equations
concepts.explanation: Solving equations of the form x + a = b and ax = b using inverse operations and balance.

concepts.name: Proportional Graphs and Constant of Proportionality
concepts.explanation: Interpreting and graphing proportional relationships and identifying the constant of proportionality (unit rate).

concepts.name: Quadratic Factoring and Zeros
concepts.explanation: Factoring quadratic expressions to find x-intercepts and relate factors to roots and graph features.

concepts.name: Vertex Form and Completing the Square
concepts.explanation: Rewriting quadratics in vertex form to reveal the vertex and transformations, using completing the square.

concepts.name: Exponential Functions and Growth
concepts.explanation: Modeling growth and decay with functions of the form f(x) = a*b^x and interpreting parameters.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics: Center and Spread
concepts.explanation: Summarizing data using mean, median, mode, range, interquartile range, and standard deviation.

concepts.name: Definite Integrals and Accumulated Change
concepts.explanation: Using definite integrals to compute net area under a curve and total accumulated change over an interval.

concepts.name: Coulomb’s Law for Point Charges
concepts.explanation: The electrostatic force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation: F = (1/4πε) |q1 q2| / r^2.

concepts.name: Electric Field Strength (Definition and Vector Nature)
concepts.explanation: Electric field strength at a point is the force per unit positive test charge placed at that point; it has magnitude and direction.

concepts.name: Electric Potential Difference (Work per Unit Charge)
concepts.explanation: Potential difference between two points is the work done per unit charge in moving a test charge from one point to the other.

concepts.name: Electric Field Lines (Lines of Force)
concepts.explanation: A pictorial representation of electric fields where tangent direction gives the field direction and line density indicates field strength.

concepts.name: Types of Electric Charge (Positive and Negative)
concepts.explanation: Matter exhibits two kinds of charge, positive and negative, with like charges repelling and unlike charges attracting.

concepts.name: Unit of Electric Charge: Coulomb
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of electric charge; one coulomb is the charge transported by a current of one ampere in one second.

concepts.name: Superposition for Collinear Point Charges
concepts.explanation: Calculation of net electrostatic force on a charge due to multiple charges along a line by vector addition of individual Coulomb forces.

concepts.name: Charging by Friction (Triboelectric Effect)
concepts.explanation: Transfer of electrons between dissimilar materials when rubbed together, resulting in opposite charges on the materials.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Equilibrium on Conductors (Charge on Outer Surface)
concepts.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, excess charge resides on the outer surface of a conductor and the internal electric field is zero.

concepts.name: Field Enhancement at Sharp Points
concepts.explanation: Charge density and electric field are greatest at sharp points on conductors, leading to enhanced effects and possible discharge.

concepts.name: Mapping Electric Field Patterns with Oil and Semolina
concepts.explanation: Laboratory technique to visualize electric field lines by observing particle alignment in a dielectric medium between electrodes.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Induction Demonstration with an Insulated Conductor
concepts.explanation: Procedure to show charge separation and induced charges in a neutral conductor brought near a charged object.

concepts.name: Van de Graaff Generator (Electrostatic Demonstrations)
concepts.explanation: A belt-driven electrostatic generator used to accumulate high voltages for demonstrating charging, discharge, and field effects.

concepts.name: Zero Potential (Reference Potential)
concepts.explanation: Choice of a reference point where electric potential is defined to be zero, commonly at infinity or the Earth.

concepts.name: Lightning Conductors (Principle and Use)
concepts.explanation: Metallic rods that protect structures by providing a low-resistance path to ground, exploiting field enhancement and discharge.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Precipitators
concepts.explanation: Devices that remove particulates from exhaust gases by charging particles and collecting them on oppositely charged plates.

concepts.name: Hazards of Electric Fields to Integrated Circuits (ESD)
concepts.explanation: Electrostatic discharge can damage sensitive electronic components; prevention includes grounding and antistatic handling.

concepts.name: Capacitors and Capacitance
concepts.explanation: Components that store charge and energy; capacitance is the ratio of stored charge to potential difference.

concepts.name: Common Uses of Capacitors
concepts.explanation: Applications of capacitors including tuning circuits, camera flash units, smoothing rectified outputs, and filtering signals.

concepts.name: Conduction in Materials
concepts.explanation: Mechanisms of charge transport in different media, including metals, electrolytes, and gases.

concepts.name: Capacitance Definition (C = Q/V)
concepts.explanation: Capacitance is the ratio of charge stored on a conductor to the potential difference across it: C = Q/V.

concepts.name: Energy Stored in a Capacitor (W = 1/2 C V^2)
concepts.explanation: The electrical energy stored in a capacitor depends on its capacitance and the voltage across it: W = 1/2 C V^2.

concepts.name: Parallel-Plate Capacitor Formula (C = εA/d)
concepts.explanation: For a parallel-plate capacitor, capacitance is proportional to plate area and dielectric permittivity and inversely proportional to plate separation.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Capacitance
concepts.explanation: Capacitance increases with plate area and dielectric permittivity and decreases with plate separation.

concepts.name: Capacitor Behavior in AC vs DC
concepts.explanation: Capacitors block steady DC (after charging) but allow alternating current to pass due to time-varying voltage.

concepts.name: Capacitor Charge–Discharge Experiment
concepts.explanation: Procedure to charge a capacitor and discharge it through a lamp or low-voltage DC motor to observe energy release and current flow.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristic Curves Interpretation
concepts.explanation: Reading and interpreting current–voltage graphs to distinguish ohmic and non-ohmic behavior and device characteristics.

concepts.name: Electric Current and Its Unit (1 A = 1 C s^-1)
concepts.explanation: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge; one ampere equals one coulomb per second.

concepts.name: Potential Difference and EMF
concepts.explanation: Potential difference (voltage) is the energy per unit charge between two points; EMF is the source voltage applied to a circuit.

concepts.name: Unit of Capacitance (Farad)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of capacitance is the farad (F), equal to one coulomb per volt.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Metals
concepts.explanation: Conduction in metals occurs via mobile electrons (electron drift) under an applied electric field.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Ionic Solutions
concepts.explanation: Ionic solutions conduct via positive and negative ions; electrode activity can cause chemical changes during conduction.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Gases
concepts.explanation: Gases conduct when ionized, with ions and electrons acting as charge carriers under high fields or specific conditions.

concepts.name: Electrical Conduction in Vacuum
concepts.explanation: In vacuum, conduction occurs via free electrons emitted from a cathode (thermionic or field emission) and accelerated by an electric field.

concepts.name: Conduction in Semiconductors (Electrons and Holes)
concepts.explanation: Semiconductors conduct via mobile electrons in the conduction band and holes in the valence band.

concepts.name: Intrinsic vs Extrinsic Semiconductor Conduction
concepts.explanation: Intrinsic conduction arises from pure material; extrinsic conduction is due to doping with donors or acceptors to increase carriers.

concepts.name: p-type and n-type Semiconductors
concepts.explanation: Doping creates p-type (hole majority) or n-type (electron majority) materials with distinct conduction properties.

concepts.name: Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: A four-resistor bridge circuit that determines an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of the bridge and detecting a null (zero current) condition.

concepts.name: Balance Condition of a Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: At balance, no current flows through the galvanometer and the resistance ratios satisfy R1/R2 = R3/Rx, enabling calculation of the unknown resistance.

concepts.name: Measuring Unknown Resistance with a Wheatstone Bridge
concepts.explanation: A null-method procedure: vary known resistances until the galvanometer reads zero, then use the bridge ratio to compute the unknown resistance.

concepts.name: Potentiometer as a Variable Potential Divider
concepts.explanation: A three-terminal resistor with a sliding contact used to provide a controllable fraction of an input voltage (Vout = (R2/(R1+R2))Vin), enabling adjustable voltage control and sensing in DC circuits.

concepts.name: Thermostat for Temperature Control
concepts.explanation: An automatic switch (often using a bimetallic strip) that maintains a set temperature by opening and closing a circuit based on thermal expansion, implementing simple feedback control.

concepts.name: Thermal Fuse as a Fail-Safe Device
concepts.explanation: A one-time temperature-activated cutoff that permanently opens a circuit when a designated temperature is exceeded, providing fail-safe protection against overheating.

concepts.name: Electroplating
concepts.explanation: Deposition of a metal layer onto a conductive surface using an electrolytic cell; used for corrosion protection, wear resistance, and aesthetics; governed by Faraday’s laws of electrolysis.

concepts.name: Electrolytic Refining of Metals
concepts.explanation: Purification of impure metals by electrolysis, where the impure metal serves as the anode and pure metal is deposited at the cathode, separating impurities.

concepts.name: Electrical Resistance (definition and unit)
concepts.explanation: Resistance is the opposition to current flow in a component, defined as R = V/I with SI unit ohm (Ω).

concepts.name: Dependence of Resistance on Length and Cross-sectional Area
concepts.explanation: For a uniform conductor, resistance varies directly with length and inversely with cross-sectional area, expressed as R = ρL/A.

concepts.name: p–n Junction Forward and Reverse Bias (Diode I–V Characteristics)
concepts.explanation: In forward bias the depletion barrier is reduced and current increases rapidly; in reverse bias the barrier increases and only a small leakage current flows until breakdown.

concepts.name: Depletion Region and Barrier Potential in a p–n Junction
concepts.explanation: Carrier diffusion and drift create a depletion region and built-in potential at the junction, governing current flow under applied bias.

concepts.name: Fuse Rating Calculations
concepts.explanation: Selecting an appropriate fuse based on expected circuit current (e.g., using I = P/V) with a safety margin to protect against overcurrent.

concepts.name: Wiring a Plug (Live, Neutral, Earth)
concepts.explanation: Procedure for safely connecting live, neutral, and earth conductors to the correct plug terminals and fitting a suitable fuse.

concepts.name: Using an Ohmmeter to Measure Resistance
concepts.explanation: Procedure to measure resistance by isolating the component, selecting range, zeroing if needed, and interpreting the reading.

concepts.name: Metre Bridge Method for Resistance Measurement
concepts.explanation: Determining an unknown resistance using a metre bridge (Wheatstone bridge) at balance, applying the ratio of bridge arms.

concepts.name: Light-Dependent Resistor (LDR) Characteristics
concepts.explanation: A photoresistor whose resistance decreases with increasing light intensity; characterized by an R–illuminance curve and used in light sensing circuits.

concepts.name: Thermistor Characteristics
concepts.explanation: A temperature-dependent resistor (NTC or PTC) with a non-linear R–T relationship used for temperature sensing and compensation.

concepts.name: Function of a Fuse Box (Consumer Unit)
concepts.explanation: Central domestic distribution unit that splits the supply into circuits, provides isolation, and houses protective devices such as fuses or MCBs.

concepts.name: Electricity Meter Function in Domestic Supply
concepts.explanation: Measures electrical energy consumption in kilowatt-hours (kWh) for billing and monitoring in household installations.

concepts.name: Equivalent Resistance in Series
concepts.explanation: For resistors connected in series, the equivalent resistance equals the sum of individual resistances: Req = R1 + R2 + ... . The same current flows through each resistor.

concepts.name: Equivalent Resistance in Parallel
concepts.explanation: For resistors connected in parallel, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance equals the sum of reciprocals: 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... . Each branch has the same voltage.

concepts.name: Resistivity (ρ)
concepts.explanation: An intrinsic material property relating a conductor’s resistance to its dimensions via R = ρL/A; depends on material and temperature, measured in ohm–meter.

concepts.name: Temperature Coefficient of Resistivity
concepts.explanation: A parameter α that quantifies how resistivity changes with temperature, typically modeled as ρ ≈ ρ0(1 + αΔT) over a limited range.

concepts.name: Derivation of Equivalent Resistance Formulas Using Ohm's Law
concepts.explanation: A procedure to obtain series and parallel resistance relations by applying Ohm’s law and basic circuit constraints for current and voltage.

concepts.name: Light Dependent Resistor (LDR)
concepts.explanation: A photoresistive component whose resistance decreases with increasing light intensity; commonly used in voltage-divider light sensors and control circuits.

concepts.name: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction
concepts.explanation: The induced emf in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through it (E = −dΦ/dt for a single loop).

concepts.name: Lenz's law
concepts.explanation: The direction of an induced emf opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it, ensuring energy conservation.

concepts.name: Magnetic flux (Φ = BA)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux measures the total magnetic field through an area; for uniform fields normal to the surface, Φ = BA.

concepts.name: Magnetic force on a moving charge (Lorentz force)
concepts.explanation: A charge moving in a magnetic field experiences F = qvB sinθ, perpendicular to both velocity and field.

concepts.name: Magnetic flux density (definition of B)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux density is defined by B = F/(Il) for a conductor at right angles to the field, quantifying field strength.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a solenoid
concepts.explanation: A solenoid produces a near-uniform internal magnetic field with direction given by the right-hand rule; basis of electromagnets.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a long straight current-carrying wire
concepts.explanation: A current in a long straight wire creates concentric magnetic field lines whose strength decreases with distance.

concepts.name: Magnetic field of a current loop
concepts.explanation: A single current loop produces a dipole-like magnetic field; axial field enhanced by multiple turns.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic induction in generators
concepts.explanation: Changing flux through rotating coils induces emf, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy in generators.

concepts.name: Alternating current (AC) fundamentals
concepts.explanation: AC reverses direction periodically and is characterized by frequency and RMS values; used in mains supply.

concepts.name: Transformer operation
concepts.explanation: Transformers use mutual induction and the turns ratio to step AC voltages up or down with minimal power loss.

concepts.name: Definition of the ampere (force between parallel currents)
concepts.explanation: The ampere is defined via the force per unit length between two long parallel conductors carrying equal currents.

concepts.name: Joule heating of a resistor (W = I²Rt)
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy dissipated as heat in a resistor equals W = I²Rt, with power P = I²R.

concepts.name: Kilowatt-hour as a unit of electrical energy
concepts.explanation: The kilowatt-hour is an energy unit used for billing; 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.

concepts.name: AC power transmission and the national grid
concepts.explanation: High-voltage AC and transformers minimize I²R losses for efficient long-distance power transmission.

concepts.name: Electromagnets and their uses
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying solenoid with a ferromagnetic core produces a strong, controllable magnetic field used in relays and lifting magnets.

concepts.name: Principle of operation of a DC motor
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque that produces continuous rotation with a commutator.

concepts.name: Residual current device (RCD) operation
concepts.explanation: RCDs compare live and neutral currents and trip on imbalance due to earth leakage, reducing shock risk.

concepts.name: Miniature circuit breaker (MCB) function
concepts.explanation: MCBs provide resettable overcurrent and short-circuit protection using thermal-magnetic trip mechanisms.

concepts.name: Electrical fuse and overcurrent protection
concepts.explanation: A fuse is a sacrificial link that melts to interrupt excessive current, protecting circuits from damage.

concepts.name: Earthing and bonding in electrical installations
concepts.explanation: Earthing connects exposed metal parts to ground to clear faults; bonding equalizes potentials between conductive parts.

concepts.name: Ring versus radial circuits in domestic wiring
concepts.explanation: Ring mains form closed loops sharing current, while radial circuits feed outlets along a single run; each has distinct protection requirements.

concepts.name: Earth's magnetic field and navigation
concepts.explanation: Earth behaves like a magnetic dipole; compasses align with its field and are used for navigation.

concepts.name: Magnetic poles exist in pairs
concepts.explanation: Magnetic monopoles are not observed in classical magnetism; every magnet has both north and south poles.

concepts.name: Vector nature of the magnetic field
concepts.explanation: The magnetic field is a vector quantity with magnitude and direction and follows superposition.

concepts.name: Loudspeaker operation (electromagnetic)
concepts.explanation: A voice coil in a magnetic field experiences a force proportional to current, driving a diaphragm to produce sound.

concepts.name: Moving-coil meter (galvanometer) principle
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque causing pointer deflection proportional to current.

concepts.name: RMS Value of Alternating Voltage and Current
concepts.explanation: Defines the root-mean-square value as the effective DC value that delivers the same heating effect; for a sinusoid Vrms = Vpeak / sqrt(2) and Irms = Ipeak / sqrt(2).

concepts.name: Peak Value of Alternating Voltage and Current
concepts.explanation: Identifies the maximum instantaneous value of a sinusoidal voltage or current; related to RMS by Vpeak = Vrms * sqrt(2) and Ipeak = Irms * sqrt(2).

concepts.name: Converting Between Peak, Peak-to-Peak, and RMS for Sinusoidal AC
concepts.explanation: Performs calculations using Vpp = 2*Vpeak, Vrms = Vpeak / sqrt(2), and analogous relations for current to compare and convert AC measures.

concepts.name: Time Variation of Alternating Voltage and Current
concepts.explanation: Describes sinusoidal time dependence v(t) = Vpeak sin(ωt) and i(t) = Ipeak sin(ωt), including period, frequency, and phase.

concepts.name: Oscilloscope Measurement of AC Waveforms
concepts.explanation: Uses an oscilloscope to display AC signals, adjust timebase and volts/div, and measure amplitude, period, frequency, and peak-to-peak values.

concepts.name: Mutual Induction Between Coils
concepts.explanation: States that a changing magnetic field in one coil induces an emf in a nearby coil; direction given by Lenz’s law and magnitude dependent on coupling.

concepts.name: Self-Induction in a Coil (Inductor)
concepts.explanation: Defines the induced emf in a coil caused by changes in its own current; opposes current change (Lenz’s law) and stores energy in its magnetic field.

concepts.name: Effects of Inductors on Alternating Current (Qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Describes how inductors impede changes in current, reducing AC amplitude and introducing a delay between voltage and current without using phasor math.

concepts.name: Applications of Inductors in Lighting Circuits
concepts.explanation: Identifies inductors as ballasts that limit current and aid starting in discharge and fluorescent lighting systems.

concepts.name: Experimental Verification of Joule’s Law of Heating (Δθ ∝ I^2)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to confirm that the temperature rise of a resistor is proportional to the square of the current for fixed resistance and time, consistent with H = I^2 R t.

concepts.name: Investigation of the Temperature Dependence of Resistance in Metals
concepts.explanation: Experimentally study how a metallic conductor’s resistance varies with temperature, typically linearly, and extract the temperature coefficient of resistance.

concepts.name: Investigation of Thermistor Resistance versus Temperature
concepts.explanation: An experiment to measure a thermistor’s resistance at different temperatures and plot R–T to observe its temperature dependence.

concepts.name: Resistance–Temperature Characteristic of a Thermistor
concepts.explanation: The relationship showing thermistor resistance changing with temperature, typically decreasing rapidly as temperature rises.

concepts.name: Thermistor (NTC)
concepts.explanation: A temperature-sensitive resistor with a negative temperature coefficient, commonly used as a temperature sensor.

concepts.name: Negative Temperature Coefficient of Resistance
concepts.explanation: A property where a material’s resistance decreases as its temperature increases; characteristic of NTC thermistors.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Metallic Conductor
concepts.explanation: At constant temperature, current is directly proportional to potential difference, giving a straight-line I–V graph through the origin with constant resistance.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Filament Lamp
concepts.explanation: Shows non-linear I–V behavior due to self-heating; filament temperature rises with current, increasing resistance and producing a curve that flattens at higher voltages.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of an Electrolyte (CuSO4 with Copper Electrodes)
concepts.explanation: Demonstrates ionic conduction where current arises from ion motion and electrode reactions; with copper electrodes in copper sulfate solution, the I–V relationship can be approximately linear over a range, illustrating electrolytic conduction.

concepts.name: I–V Characteristics of a Semiconductor Diode
concepts.explanation: Exhibits a strongly non-linear I–V curve with a forward-bias threshold (knee voltage) and minimal reverse current up to breakdown, demonstrating rectification.

concepts.name: Elementary charge (e)
concepts.explanation: The fundamental unit of electric charge, magnitude 1.602×10^-19 C; the electron carries charge −e. Determined experimentally by Millikan.

concepts.name: Millikan oil-drop experiment
concepts.explanation: An experiment that measures the elementary charge by balancing gravitational and electric forces on tiny charged oil droplets, demonstrating charge quantization.

concepts.name: X-rays
concepts.explanation: High-frequency electromagnetic radiation produced by rapid deceleration of high-speed electrons (bremsstrahlung) or inner-shell electron transitions.

concepts.name: Photoelectric sensors
concepts.explanation: Devices that use the photoelectric effect to convert light into electrical signals for detection and control, e.g., burglar alarms, automatic doors, burner control.

concepts.name: Production of Electron Beams in a Cathode Ray Tube
concepts.explanation: Using an electron gun and accelerating electrodes to generate and focus a beam of electrons visible on a fluorescent screen.

concepts.name: Deflection of Electrons in Electric Fields
concepts.explanation: An electron beam experiences a force proportional to charge and field strength, producing a controllable deflection (parabolic path) between deflection plates in a CRT.
concepts.broader_concept: Motion of Charged Particles in Electric Fields

concepts.name: Deflection of Electrons in Magnetic Fields
concepts.explanation: A moving electron in a magnetic field is deflected by the Lorentz force, following a circular arc with radius increasing with momentum and decreasing with field strength.
concepts.broader_concept: Motion of Charged Particles in Magnetic Fields

concepts.name: Photoelectric Effect Demonstration with Zinc Plate and Electroscope
concepts.explanation: Ultraviolet illumination ejects electrons from a charged zinc plate, causing an electroscope to discharge and illustrating threshold frequency and photon energy.

concepts.name: Hazards of X-ray Radiation and Safety Precautions
concepts.explanation: Biological effects of ionizing X-rays and methods to minimize dose using time, distance, and shielding practices.

concepts.name: Electron Gun Operation
concepts.explanation: Production, acceleration, and focusing of an electron beam using a heated cathode (thermionic source), control grid, and accelerating/focusing anodes.

concepts.name: Cathode Ray Tube (CRT): Components and Function
concepts.explanation: Structure and operation of a CRT, including electron gun, deflection system, and phosphor screen, to produce and steer cathode rays for visualization.

concepts.name: Photocell Operation (Photoelectric Device)
concepts.explanation: Conversion of light to electric current via the photoelectric effect; demonstration of how incident photons liberate electrons to produce a measurable current.

concepts.name: Electronvolt (eV) and Its Multiples
concepts.explanation: Definition and use of the electronvolt as an energy unit (eV, keV, MeV, GeV), equal to the work done on an electron by a 1 V potential difference.

concepts.name: Electron Mass and Position in the Atom
concepts.explanation: Recognition of the electron’s small rest mass and its location in the atomic structure as a cloud/shell surrounding the nucleus.

concepts.name: Photon Model of Light
concepts.explanation: Light consists of discrete quanta (photons) whose energies are proportional to frequency, explaining phenomena such as the photoelectric effect.

concepts.name: Photon Energy (E = hf)
concepts.explanation: The energy of a photon equals Planck’s constant multiplied by the light frequency, E = hf.

concepts.name: Effect of Light Intensity and Frequency on Photoelectric Emission
concepts.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, increasing intensity increases photoelectron rate (current), while increasing frequency raises maximum kinetic energy and requires exceeding a threshold frequency for emission.

concepts.name: Deflection of Cathode Rays in Electric Fields
concepts.explanation: Electron beams are deflected toward positive potentials in an electric field; the deflection depends on field strength, path length, and electron velocity.

concepts.name: Deflection of Cathode Rays in Magnetic Fields
concepts.explanation: Magnetic fields exert a force on moving electrons (qvB), producing circular or helical paths with radius set by momentum and field strength.

concepts.name: Einstein's photoelectric law
concepts.explanation: Relates the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons to the incident light frequency: KE_max = hf − φ, explaining the linear dependence of stopping potential on frequency.

concepts.name: Threshold frequency
concepts.explanation: The minimum frequency f0 of incident light needed to eject electrons from a material, given by f0 = φ/h.

concepts.name: Spectroscopic transition formula hf = E2 − E1
concepts.explanation: The photon energy for an atomic transition equals the difference between two energy levels, predicting spectral line wavelengths.

concepts.name: Emission line spectra
concepts.explanation: Discrete spectral lines produced when excited atoms emit photons during transitions to lower energy levels.

concepts.name: X-ray production by high-energy electrons colliding with a target
concepts.explanation: X-rays are emitted when accelerated electrons decelerate in a target (bremsstrahlung) or when inner-shell vacancies are filled (characteristic X-rays).

concepts.name: Hot-cathode X-ray tube: principle of operation
concepts.explanation: Thermionic emission from a heated cathode provides electrons that are accelerated to a metal target by high voltage, generating X-rays.

concepts.name: Inverse photoelectric effect (X-ray production)
concepts.explanation: Conversion of electron kinetic energy into photon energy when electrons are decelerated in matter, producing X-rays; conceptual inverse of photoemission.

concepts.name: Rutherford scattering experiment: principle
concepts.explanation: Alpha particles scattered by thin foil reveal a small, dense, positively charged nucleus, disproving the plum pudding model.

concepts.name: Atomic nucleus composition: protons and neutrons
concepts.explanation: The nucleus consists of protons and neutrons (nucleons), defining atomic number Z and contributing to mass number A.

concepts.name: Isotope notation (A, Z, X) and definitions
concepts.explanation: Symbols specifying mass number A, atomic number Z, and element X; isotopes are nuclei with the same Z but different A.

concepts.name: Alpha, beta, and gamma radiation: nature and identification
concepts.explanation: Three types of nuclear radiation distinguished by charge/mass and by deflection in fields, ionisation strength, and penetration.

concepts.name: Law of radioactive decay
concepts.explanation: The rate of decay is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei: dN/dt = −λN, giving exponential decay N(t) = N0 e^(−λt).

concepts.name: Decay constant (λ)
concepts.explanation: Probability per unit time that a nucleus decays; relates activity to number of nuclei via A = λN.

concepts.name: Half-life (T1/2) and T1/2 = ln 2 / λ
concepts.explanation: Time for half the nuclei in a sample to decay; inversely related to decay constant by T1/2 = ln 2 / λ.

concepts.name: Becquerel (Bq): unit of activity
concepts.explanation: SI unit of radioactivity defined as one nuclear disintegration per second.

concepts.name: Changes in atomic and mass numbers in radioactive decay
concepts.explanation: Rules for decay processes: alpha decay decreases A by 4 and Z by 2; beta-minus increases Z by 1; gamma leaves A and Z unchanged.

concepts.name: Principles of nuclear fission and fusion
concepts.explanation: Fission splits heavy nuclei to release energy; fusion combines light nuclei to release energy due to mass defect.

concepts.name: Principle of operation of a detector of ionising radiation
concepts.explanation: Basic operation of devices like the Geiger–Müller tube or solid-state detectors that register ionising events as electrical pulses.

concepts.name: Background radiation and radon
concepts.explanation: Sources and significance of natural background radiation, with radon gas as a major contributor in certain regions (e.g., granite areas).

concepts.name: Biological Effects of Ionising Radiation
concepts.explanation: How ionising radiation damages living tissue and health, with effects depending on radiation type, source activity, exposure time, and tissue type.

concepts.name: Activity (Becquerel)
concepts.explanation: The rate of radioactive decay of a source; 1 Bq equals one disintegration per second.

concepts.name: Types of Ionising Radiation
concepts.explanation: Different ionising radiations (e.g., alpha, beta, gamma, X-rays) with characteristic ionisation and penetration affecting their hazards.

concepts.name: Exposure Time and Radiation Dose
concepts.explanation: For a given source and geometry, longer exposure increases received dose and risk of adverse biological effects.

concepts.name: Tissue Radiosensitivity
concepts.explanation: Different tissues exhibit varying sensitivity to ionising radiation, influencing the severity of biological effects for the same exposure.

concepts.name: Environmental Radiation and Background Exposure
concepts.explanation: Natural and man-made environmental sources of ionising radiation contribute to human exposure and associated health risks.

concepts.name: Photon Energy from Atomic Transitions
concepts.explanation: Photon energy equals the difference between atomic energy levels, E = hf = ΔE, with wavelength given by λ = hc/ΔE.

concepts.name: Emission Spectra of Atoms
concepts.explanation: Bright-line spectra produced when excited electrons drop to lower energy levels; line positions correspond to allowed transitions.

concepts.name: Absorption Spectra of Atoms
concepts.explanation: Dark-line spectra formed when atoms absorb photons with energies matching level gaps; absorption lines align with emission lines for the same atom.

concepts.name: Energy Level Diagram Interpretation
concepts.explanation: Reading and constructing energy-level diagrams to link transitions with emitted or absorbed photon wavelengths and series.

concepts.name: Electron Volt (eV)
concepts.explanation: A convenient atomic-scale energy unit equal to 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J, defined as the work done on an electron by a potential difference of 1 volt.

concepts.name: Ionization Energy of an Atom
concepts.explanation: The minimum energy required to remove an electron from the ground state to the continuum; equals the magnitude of the ground-state binding energy.

concepts.name: Rydberg Formula for Hydrogen Spectrum
concepts.explanation: Predicts hydrogen spectral lines: 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), explaining series such as Lyman and Balmer from quantized energy levels.

concepts.name: de Broglie Wavelength of Electrons
concepts.explanation: Matter-wave relation λ = h/p for particles; explains electron diffraction and supports quantization in atomic orbits.

concepts.name: X-ray Production in an X-ray Tube
concepts.explanation: High-speed electrons striking a target produce bremsstrahlung and characteristic X-rays from inner-shell transitions; λmin set by accelerating voltage.

concepts.name: Measuring Emission Line Wavelengths with a Diffraction Grating
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure using the grating equation d sinθ = mλ to determine atomic line wavelengths and identify elements.

concepts.name: Energy and Momentum Conservation in Particle Reactions
concepts.explanation: Total energy and momentum are conserved in nuclear decays and particle collisions; these constraints are used to analyze and predict reaction outcomes.

concepts.name: Mass–Energy Equivalence in Particle Reactions (E=mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Rest mass can be converted to and from other forms of energy in nuclear and particle processes; used to compute reaction energies and particle creation.

concepts.name: Antimatter and Antiparticles
concepts.explanation: Every particle has a corresponding antiparticle with opposite charge and other quantum numbers; e.g., the positron is the electron’s antiparticle.

concepts.name: Pair Production (γ → e+ e−)
concepts.explanation: A high-energy photon can transform into an electron–positron pair (usually near a nucleus) while conserving energy, momentum, and charge.

concepts.name: Electron–Positron Annihilation to Two Gamma Rays
concepts.explanation: An electron and positron annihilate to produce two gamma photons (each with energy hf), conserving energy, momentum, and charge.

concepts.name: Leptons
concepts.explanation: Fundamental particles not subject to the strong force; examples include electrons, positrons, and neutrinos.

concepts.name: Baryons
concepts.explanation: Hadrons composed of three quarks; subject to all fundamental forces; examples include protons and neutrons.

concepts.name: Mesons
concepts.explanation: Hadrons composed of a quark–antiquark pair; subject to strong, weak, electromagnetic, and gravitational interactions; masses intermediate between electrons and protons.

concepts.name: Quark Flavors (u, d, s, c, t, b)
concepts.explanation: Six types of quarks—up, down, strange, charm, top, and bottom—combine to form hadrons.

concepts.name: Quark Electric Charges (+2/3, −1/3) and Antiquarks
concepts.explanation: Up-type quarks carry +2/3e while down-type quarks carry −1/3e; antiquarks have opposite charge to their quark counterparts with the same mass.

concepts.name: Baryon Quark Structure (p = uud, n = udd)
concepts.explanation: Baryons are three-quark states; the proton (uud) and neutron (udd) quark compositions account for their charges and properties.

concepts.name: Meson Quark–Antiquark Structure
concepts.explanation: Mesons consist of a quark and an antiquark; their quark content determines their charges and quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Determining Particle Charge from Quark Content
concepts.explanation: The electric charge of a hadron is found by summing the charges of its constituent quarks or antiquarks.

concepts.name: Strong Nuclear Force (Short-Range Binding)
concepts.explanation: The strong interaction binds quarks into hadrons and nucleons into nuclei; it is short range and very strong.

concepts.name: Weak Nuclear Force
concepts.explanation: A short-range interaction responsible for processes like beta decay; acts on particles that may not participate in the strong force.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Interaction in Particle Physics
concepts.explanation: The inverse-square force between charged particles; mediates many scattering and interaction processes in particle physics.

concepts.name: Neutrino Inference from Beta Decay
concepts.explanation: Apparent non-conservation of energy and momentum in beta decay implies emission of an unseen neutrino to restore conservation laws.

concepts.name: Q-Value of Nuclear Reactions
concepts.explanation: The net energy released or absorbed in a reaction, computed from the mass difference of initial and final states using E=mc^2.

concepts.name: Cockcroft–Walton Proton-Induced Disintegration
concepts.explanation: First artificial nuclear splitting: ~1 MeV protons on lithium produce two alpha particles, confirming mass–energy conversion.

concepts.name: Electrostatic Proton Acceleration (Cockcroft–Walton Accelerator)
concepts.explanation: A voltage-multiplier accelerator that accelerates ions to MeV energies for inducing nuclear reactions.

concepts.name: High-Energy Proton–Proton Collisions and Particle Creation
concepts.explanation: Increasing center-of-mass energy in circular accelerators enables p+p→p+p plus additional particles via energy-to-mass conversion.

concepts.name: Gravitational Interaction at Subatomic Scales
concepts.explanation: The gravitational inverse-square force is extremely weak and typically negligible in particle interactions.

concepts.name: Particle Creation Thresholds and "Particle Zoo"
concepts.explanation: Higher available reaction energy allows creation of a greater variety of particles; rest masses arise from conversion of energy via E=mc^2.

concepts.name: Slope and Intercept of a Line
concepts.explanation: Interpreting slope as rate of change and y-intercept as initial value in linear models (y = mx + b).

concepts.name: Area and Circumference of Circles
concepts.explanation: Using formulas C = 2πr and A = πr^2 to solve measurement problems involving circles.

concepts.name: Measures of Central Tendency
concepts.explanation: Summarizing data using mean, median, and mode, and choosing appropriate measures for distributions.

concepts.name: Simple Probability
concepts.explanation: Determining likelihood of events using ratios of favorable to total equally likely outcomes.

concepts.name: Area Model for Multiplication
concepts.explanation: Using rectangular arrays to represent and compute products, connecting area to the distributive property.

concepts.name: Decimals and Place Value
concepts.explanation: Interpreting digits to the right of the decimal point as tenths, hundredths, etc., and comparing and rounding decimals.

concepts.name: Mean and Median
concepts.explanation: Calculating the arithmetic average and the middle value of an ordered data set to summarize central tendency.

concepts.name: Percent as Rate per Hundred
concepts.explanation: Interpreting percent as a ratio out of 100 to solve problems involving discounts, tax, and interest.

concepts.name: Linear Equation in One Variable
concepts.explanation: Solving equations of the form ax + b = c using inverse operations and maintaining equality.

concepts.name: Slope-Intercept Form
concepts.explanation: Expressing a linear function as y = mx + b, where m is slope and b is the y-intercept, to model and graph lines.

concepts.name: Function as Input-Output Rule
concepts.explanation: Understanding a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input from its domain.

concepts.name: Systems of Linear Equations (Substitution)
concepts.explanation: Solving two linear equations in two variables by substituting one equation into the other to find an intersection point.

concepts.name: Quadratic Function Vertex Form
concepts.explanation: Writing a quadratic as y = a(x − h)^2 + k to identify the vertex, direction of opening, and transformations.

concepts.name: Correlation and Line of Best Fit
concepts.explanation: Describing the strength and direction of linear relationships and fitting a regression line to bivariate data.

concepts.name: Derivative as Instantaneous Rate of Change
concepts.explanation: Viewing the derivative as the slope of the tangent line or the limit of average rates of change over shrinking intervals.

concepts.name: Definite Integral as Net Area
concepts.explanation: Interpreting the definite integral as the signed area under a curve and relating it to accumulation and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

concepts.name: Area and Perimeter of Rectangles
concepts.explanation: Compute perimeter as the sum of side lengths and area as length x width; apply to real-world problems.

concepts.name: Surface Area and Volume of Rectangular Prisms
concepts.explanation: Find surface area using nets and compute volume as length x width x height; relate to unit cubes.

concepts.name: Scatter Plots and Line of Best Fit
concepts.explanation: Plot bivariate data, describe associations, draw and interpret a trend line, and use it for predictions.

concepts.name: Exponential Functions
concepts.explanation: Functions with constant multiplicative rate, y = a b^x; distinguish from linear; interpret growth/decay factors and doubling/half-life.

concepts.name: Faraday's Law of Induction
concepts.explanation: An emf is induced in a circuit proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through it; direction given by Lenz's law.

concepts.name: Transformer Efficiency and Losses
concepts.explanation: Efficiency depends on copper losses, core losses (hysteresis, eddy currents), and leakage; η = P_out/P_in.

concepts.name: Simple AC Generator Operation
concepts.explanation: A rotating coil in a magnetic field produces alternating emf; structure and working of an alternator.

concepts.name: DC Motor Principle of Operation
concepts.explanation: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque; commutator maintains unidirectional torque.

concepts.name: Induction Motor Principle
concepts.explanation: A rotating magnetic field induces rotor currents that produce torque; concept of slip.

concepts.name: Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
concepts.explanation: A wire of length L carrying current I in magnetic field B experiences force F = BIL sinθ; direction by Fleming's left-hand rule.

concepts.name: Half-Wave Rectification with a p–n Diode
concepts.explanation: A single diode conducts on one half-cycle, converting AC to pulsating DC with high ripple.

concepts.name: Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier with Smoothing Capacitor
concepts.explanation: A four-diode bridge provides full-wave rectification; a parallel capacitor filters ripple to yield smoother DC.

concepts.name: Light-Emitting Diode (LED) Operation and Applications
concepts.explanation: A forward-biased p–n junction emits light via electron–hole recombination; used in indicators and displays.

concepts.name: Transistor as a Switch (Inverter/NOT)
concepts.explanation: Using cutoff and saturation of BJT/MOSFET to implement logic inversion and drive loads such as relays.

concepts.name: AND Gate Truth Table
concepts.explanation: Digital gate whose output is 1 only when all inputs are 1; establish and verify its truth table.

concepts.name: OR Gate Truth Table
concepts.explanation: Digital gate whose output is 1 when any input is 1; establish and verify its truth table.

concepts.name: NOT Gate Truth Table
concepts.explanation: Digital inverter outputs the complement of the input; construct and verify its truth table.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Relay Operation
concepts.explanation: A current through a coil actuates an armature to switch contacts, providing isolation and control of higher currents.

concepts.name: Moving-Coil Galvanometer Principle
concepts.explanation: A coil in a magnetic field experiences torque proportional to current, producing measurable deflection.

concepts.name: Conversion of a Galvanometer to an Ammeter
concepts.explanation: Add a low-resistance shunt parallel to the movement to extend current range; determine shunt value.

concepts.name: Conversion of a Galvanometer to a Voltmeter
concepts.explanation: Add a series multiplier resistor to extend voltage range; compute required series resistance.

concepts.name: Conversion of a Galvanometer to an Ohmmeter
