concepts.explanation: Use an internal cell and resistors to measure resistance via calibrated deflection.

concepts.name: Ammeter and Voltmeter Range Calculations
concepts.explanation: Calculate shunt and series multiplier resistances from galvanometer sensitivity and desired measurement range.

concepts.name: Induction Coil (Ruhmkorff) Operation
concepts.explanation: An interrupter and transformer produce high-voltage pulses via rapid changes in current and mutual induction.

concepts.name: Fibre Optic Receiver Principle
concepts.explanation: A photodetector converts light carried in optical fibre into electrical signals; includes biasing and signal conditioning.

concepts.name: Transistor as a Voltage Amplifier
concepts.explanation: Using a bipolar junction transistor (BJT) in a common-emitter configuration to increase the amplitude of an input voltage signal at the output.

concepts.name: Purpose of Bias Resistors in Transistor Amplifiers
concepts.explanation: Bias resistors set the transistor’s operating point (Q-point) to ensure linear amplification and prevent cutoff or saturation.

concepts.name: Purpose of Load Resistor in Transistor Amplifiers
concepts.explanation: The load resistor converts the transistor’s collector current variations into an output voltage and determines gain and output swing.

concepts.name: Transistor as a Voltage Inverter
concepts.explanation: A common-emitter transistor stage produces a 180° phase shift, outputting a logical low when the input is high and vice versa.

concepts.name: Basic Structure of a Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)
concepts.explanation: A BJT consists of two p–n junctions forming either npn or pnp layers with emitter, base, and collector regions of differing doping and geometry.

concepts.name: Light-Emitting Diode (LED) Principle of Operation
concepts.explanation: Under forward bias, electron–hole recombination in a p–n junction emits photons; emission wavelength depends on the semiconductor band gap.

concepts.name: Photodiode Operation
concepts.explanation: A reverse-biased p–n junction that generates a photocurrent proportional to incident light via the photovoltaic or photoconductive effect.

concepts.name: AND Gate Function
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1; implements logical conjunction.

concepts.name: OR Gate Function
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 when at least one input is 1; implements logical disjunction.

concepts.name: NOT Gate Function
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs the logical complement of its input; implements inversion.

concepts.name: Potential Difference (pd) Definition
concepts.explanation: The work done per unit charge to move a charge between two points in an electric circuit; measured in volts.

concepts.name: Electromotive Force (emf) Definition
concepts.explanation: The energy supplied per unit charge by a source such as a cell or generator when no current flows; measured in volts.

concepts.name: Light-Emitting Diode (LED)
concepts.explanation: A p-n junction semiconductor diode that emits light under forward bias via electron–hole recombination (electroluminescence); the emitted photon energy, and thus color, is set by the band gap and relates to the threshold voltage.

concepts.name: Proton
concepts.explanation: A positively charged baryon found in atomic nuclei, composed of two up quarks and one down quark (+e charge).

concepts.name: Neutron
concepts.explanation: An electrically neutral baryon in atomic nuclei, composed of one up quark and two down quarks; unstable in free space (beta decay).

concepts.name: Electron
concepts.explanation: A negatively charged lepton with small mass that orbits the nucleus; fundamental to atomic structure and electricity.

concepts.name: Neutrino
concepts.explanation: A neutral lepton with very small mass that interacts via the weak force; denoted by the symbol ν.

concepts.name: Quark Flavors
concepts.explanation: The six types of quarks—up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom—that combine to form hadrons.

concepts.name: Positron
concepts.explanation: The antiparticle of the electron with the same mass and a +e charge; annihilates with an electron to produce gamma photons.

concepts.name: Antiquarks
concepts.explanation: Antiparticles of quarks (e.g., anti-up, anti-down) that combine with quarks to form mesons and with each other to form antibaryons.

concepts.name: Electronvolt (eV)
concepts.explanation: A unit of energy equal to the energy gained by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 1 volt; 1 eV = 1.602e-19 J.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic Temperature (Kelvin, T)
concepts.explanation: Absolute temperature measured in kelvin (K), denoted by T; the SI base unit for temperature starting from absolute zero.

concepts.name: Celsius Temperature (Degree Celsius, t or θ)
concepts.explanation: Temperature measured on the Celsius scale in degrees Celsius (°C), commonly denoted by t or θ in notation and calculations.

concepts.name: Temperature Symbols and Units Notation
concepts.explanation: Convention that absolute temperature uses T with unit K, while Celsius temperatures use t or θ with unit °C; symbols and units must match the chosen scale.

concepts.name: Temperature Change (Δθ)
concepts.explanation: The difference between final and initial temperatures; used in heat calculations such as Q = mcΔθ and expressed in °C or K increments.

concepts.name: Degree Celsius (°C)
concepts.explanation: A temperature unit on the Celsius scale with 0 °C at the freezing point and 100 °C at the boiling point of water at 1 atm; increments equal to the kelvin.

concepts.name: Quantity of Heat (Q)
concepts.explanation: The amount of energy transferred between bodies due to a temperature difference; denoted by Q and measured in joules.

concepts.name: Joule (J)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of energy used to quantify work and heat, including the amount of heat Q.

concepts.name: Heat Capacity (C)
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a body by 1 kelvin; for finite changes Q = C ΔT and SI units are J K^-1.

concepts.name: SI Unit of Heat Capacity (J K^-1)
concepts.explanation: Joule per kelvin is the SI derived unit of heat capacity, indicating heat needed per kelvin temperature change.

concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity (c)
concepts.explanation: Amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K; Q = mcΔT with units J kg^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: SI Unit of Specific Heat Capacity (J kg^-1 K^-1)
concepts.explanation: The SI derived unit for specific heat capacity, meaning joules of heat per kilogram of substance per kelvin temperature change.

concepts.name: kJ kg^-1 K^-1 as a Unit of Specific Heat Capacity
concepts.explanation: A commonly used unit for specific heat capacity; 1 kJ kg^-1 K^-1 equals 1000 J kg^-1 K^-1.

concepts.name: Joule (J) as SI Unit of Heat
concepts.explanation: The SI unit of energy used to measure heat quantities including latent heat and sensible heat.

concepts.name: Angle of Refraction
concepts.explanation: The angle between the refracted ray and the normal at the boundary when light passes between media.

concepts.name: Focal Length
concepts.explanation: The distance from a lens to its focal point where parallel rays converge or appear to diverge.

concepts.name: Image Distance
concepts.explanation: The distance from a lens to the formed image, used in 1/f = 1/u + 1/v calculations.

concepts.name: Object Distance
concepts.explanation: The distance from a lens to the object, used in the thin lens formula.

concepts.name: Magnification
concepts.explanation: The ratio of image height to object height (or v/u) describing image size relative to the object.

concepts.name: Angle of Incidence
concepts.explanation: The angle between the incident ray and the normal at a boundary between two media.

concepts.name: Angle of Reflection
concepts.explanation: The angle between the reflected ray and the normal; equals the angle of incidence for specular reflection.

concepts.name: Grating Spacing
concepts.explanation: The distance between adjacent slits in a diffraction grating, used in d sinθ = nλ.

concepts.name: Slit Separation
concepts.explanation: The spacing between two slits in a double-slit setup that determines interference fringe spacing.

concepts.name: Sound Intensity
concepts.explanation: Acoustic power per unit area (W m−2) carried by a sound wave.

concepts.name: Tension in a String
concepts.explanation: The force along a stretched string or wire that influences wave speed v = sqrt(T/μ).

concepts.name: Linear Mass Density (String)
concepts.explanation: Mass per unit length of a string (kg m−1) affecting wave speed on the string.

concepts.name: Radioactive decay constant (λ)
concepts.explanation: The probability per unit time that a nucleus decays; relates to half-life by λ = ln(2)/T1/2 and has units of s^-1.

concepts.name: Activity of a radioactive source (A)
concepts.explanation: The rate of nuclear decays per second in a sample; measured in becquerels (Bq) and given by A = λN.

concepts.name: Atomic number (Z)
concepts.explanation: The number of protons in an atomic nucleus; defines the chemical element and equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom.

concepts.name: Mass number (A)
concepts.explanation: The total number of protons and neutrons (nucleons) in an atomic nucleus; distinguishes isotopes of the same element.

concepts.name: Planck constant (h)
concepts.explanation: A fundamental constant linking photon energy and frequency via E = hf; central to quantization in quantum theory.

concepts.name: Electronic charge (e)
concepts.explanation: The magnitude of the elementary charge carried by an electron (approximately 1.602×10^-19 C); fundamental unit of electric charge.

concepts.name: Diode Rectifier
concepts.explanation: A circuit using semiconductor diodes to convert alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC), implemented as half-wave or full-wave rectification with optional filtering to reduce ripple.

concepts.name: NPN Junction Transistor
concepts.explanation: A bipolar junction transistor with an n-p-n structure in which electrons are the majority carriers; used for current amplification and switching when properly biased.

concepts.name: PNP Junction Transistor
concepts.explanation: A bipolar junction transistor with a p-n-p structure in which holes are the majority carriers; operates with opposite biasing and current directions compared to NPN devices.

concepts.name: Photovoltaic Cell
concepts.explanation: A p–n junction device that converts light into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect, characterized by I–V curves, open-circuit voltage, and short-circuit current.

concepts.name: Electric Motor
concepts.explanation: An electromechanical device that converts electrical energy into mechanical rotation using the motor effect (torque on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field).

concepts.name: Loudspeaker
concepts.explanation: An electroacoustic transducer that converts electrical signals into sound via a voice coil in a magnetic field driving a diaphragm.

concepts.name: Microphone
concepts.explanation: An electroacoustic transducer that converts sound waves into electrical signals; common types include dynamic (induction) and condenser (capacitive).

concepts.name: Earphone
concepts.explanation: A small electroacoustic transducer (miniature loudspeaker) that converts electrical audio signals into sound for personal listening, characterized by impedance and sensitivity.

concepts.name: Electric Bell
concepts.explanation: An electromechanical signaling device using an electromagnet and a make-and-break circuit to repeatedly strike a bell.

concepts.name: Photodiode
concepts.explanation: A light-sensitive PN-junction diode that converts incident light into electrical current via generation of electron–hole pairs; typically operated in reverse bias for light detection and measurement.

concepts.name: NOT Gate (Inverter)
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs the opposite logic level of its single input (1 becomes 0, 0 becomes 1).

concepts.name: AND Gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 only if all of its inputs are 1; otherwise it outputs 0.

concepts.name: OR Gate
concepts.explanation: A digital logic gate that outputs 1 if at least one of its inputs is 1; outputs 0 only if all inputs are 0.

concepts.name: Newton’s Second Law (F = ma)
concepts.explanation: The net force on a body equals its mass times its acceleration, defining how forces change motion.

concepts.name: Equations of Motion for Constant Acceleration (SUVAT)
concepts.explanation: Kinematics relations v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2, and v^2 = u^2 + 2as for straight-line motion with uniform acceleration.

concepts.name: Momentum (p = mv)
concepts.explanation: A measure of motion equal to mass times velocity; vector quantity conserved in isolated systems.

concepts.name: Work (W = Fs)
concepts.explanation: Energy transferred by a constant force acting along the displacement of an object.

concepts.name: Kinetic Energy (Ek = 1/2 mv^2)
concepts.explanation: Energy of motion proportional to mass and the square of speed.

concepts.name: Power (P = W/t)
concepts.explanation: Rate of doing work or transferring energy over time.

concepts.name: Percentage Efficiency
concepts.explanation: The ratio of useful power output to power input expressed as a percentage.

concepts.name: Angular Velocity (ω = dθ/dt)
concepts.explanation: Rate of change of angular displacement with time in rotational motion.

concepts.name: Radian Measure (θ = s/r)
concepts.explanation: Definition of angle in radians as arc length divided by radius.

concepts.name: Linear–Angular Speed Relationship (v = rω)
concepts.explanation: Relates tangential speed to angular speed and radius in circular motion.

concepts.name: Centripetal Acceleration (a = v^2/r = rω^2)
concepts.explanation: Inward acceleration required for uniform circular motion.

concepts.name: Centripetal Force (F = mv^2/r = mrω^2)
concepts.explanation: Net inward force that maintains circular motion of an object.

concepts.name: Weight (W = mg)
concepts.explanation: The gravitational force on a mass in a gravitational field.

concepts.name: Acceleration Due to Gravity (g = GM/R^2)
concepts.explanation: Gravitational field strength at the surface of a spherical mass.

concepts.name: Orbital Period–Radius Relation (T^2 = 4π^2 R^3 / GM)
concepts.explanation: For near-circular orbits, period squared is proportional to orbital radius cubed.

concepts.name: Hydrostatic Pressure (p = ρgh)
concepts.explanation: Pressure at a depth in a fluid due to the weight of the fluid above.

concepts.name: Boyle’s Law (pV = constant)
concepts.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume.

concepts.name: Moment of a Force
concepts.explanation: Turning effect of a force about a pivot equals force times perpendicular distance.

concepts.name: Torque of a Couple (τ = Fd)
concepts.explanation: A pair of equal, opposite forces produces a pure rotation with torque equal to force times separation.

concepts.name: Hooke’s Law (F = −kx)
concepts.explanation: Extension or compression of a spring is proportional to the applied force within the elastic limit.

concepts.name: SHM Acceleration Law (a = −ω^2 x)
concepts.explanation: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium.

concepts.name: Period–Frequency–Angular Frequency Relationship
concepts.explanation: For periodic motion, T = 2π/ω and f = 1/T link period, frequency, and angular frequency.

concepts.name: Simple Pendulum Period (T = 2π√(l/g))
concepts.explanation: For small oscillations, a pendulum’s period depends on its length and gravitational acceleration.

concepts.name: Mass–Energy Equivalence (E = mc^2)
concepts.explanation: Mass and energy are interconvertible; a body’s rest mass corresponds to an energy mc^2.

concepts.name: Place Value (Base-10)
concepts.explanation: Understand that the value of a digit depends on its place (ones, tens, hundreds, tenths, etc.) and use this to compare and compose numbers.

concepts.name: Solving One-Variable Linear Equations
concepts.explanation: Solve equations of the form ax + b = c by using inverse operations and properties of equality.

concepts.name: Function Concept and Notation
concepts.explanation: Understand a function as a rule that assigns each input exactly one output and use f(x) notation.

concepts.name: Quadratic Functions (Vertex Form)
concepts.explanation: Analyze y = a(x - h)^2 + k to identify vertex, axis of symmetry, direction of opening, and effects of parameters.

concepts.name: Descriptive Statistics and Variability
concepts.explanation: Summarize data with center (mean or median) and spread (MAD or standard deviation) and interpret in context.

concepts.name: Probability of Independent and Dependent Events
concepts.explanation: Compute probabilities using the multiplication rule, distinguishing independent from dependent events.

concepts.name: Transformations in the Plane
concepts.explanation: Describe and perform translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations; analyze congruence and similarity via rigid motions and scaling.

concepts.name: Degree Celsius (°C) as a Temperature Unit
concepts.explanation: The unit used to express temperature on the Celsius scale, where each degree represents an equal interval of temperature.

concepts.name: Temperature Units: Celsius (°C) and Kelvin (K)
concepts.explanation: Recognition and use of °C for Celsius and K for Kelvin as standard temperature units in physics problems and formulas.

concepts.name: Absolute Zero Offset (273.15)
concepts.explanation: The constant difference of 273.15 between Kelvin and Celsius scales, reflecting that 0 °C corresponds to 273.15 K.

concepts.name: Heat energy to change temperature (Q = mcΔT)
concepts.explanation: The thermal energy required to change the temperature of a substance is proportional to its mass, specific heat capacity, and temperature change: Q = mcΔT.

concepts.name: Heat energy for phase change (Q = mL)
concepts.explanation: During a change of state at constant temperature, the heat absorbed or released equals the mass times the specific latent heat: Q = mL; temperature remains constant during the phase change.

concepts.name: Specific Heat Capacity Equation (Q = mcΔθ)
concepts.explanation: Relates thermal energy transferred Q to a substance's mass m, specific heat capacity c, and temperature change Δθ.

concepts.name: Heat Capacity Equation (Q = CΔθ)
concepts.explanation: Relates thermal energy transferred Q to an object's heat capacity C and its temperature change Δθ.

concepts.name: Specific Latent Heat (L)
concepts.explanation: Heat per unit mass required to change a substance's state at constant temperature; calculated by Q = mL (units J/kg).

concepts.name: Latent Heat of Phase Change
concepts.explanation: Energy absorbed or released during a phase change (e.g., melting or boiling) without a temperature change.

concepts.name: Phase Change Energy Calculations (Q = mL)
concepts.explanation: Procedure to determine heat required or mass changed during phase transitions using Q = mL by solving for the unknown.

concepts.name: Snell's Law (n = sin i / sin r)
concepts.explanation: Relates angles of incidence and refraction; for air-to-medium, the refractive index n equals sin i divided by sin r. General form: n1 sin i = n2 sin r.

concepts.name: Mirror and Lens Formula (1/f = 1/u + 1/v)
concepts.explanation: Relates object distance u, image distance v, and focal length f for spherical mirrors and thin lenses.

concepts.name: Magnification (m = v/u)
concepts.explanation: Linear magnification for thin lenses or spherical mirrors equals image distance over object distance; m also equals image height over object height.

concepts.name: Power of Two Lenses in Contact (P_total = P1 + P2)
concepts.explanation: For thin lenses in contact, the total optical power equals the sum of their individual powers.

concepts.name: Refractive Index and Speed (n = c/v)
concepts.explanation: The absolute refractive index of a medium equals the speed of light in vacuum divided by the speed of light in the medium; relative index between two media equals the ratio of their wave speeds.

concepts.name: Critical Angle Relation (sin C = 1/n)
concepts.explanation: For light passing from a medium of index n into air, the critical angle C satisfies sin C = 1/n; more generally sin C = n2/n1.

concepts.name: Apparent Depth and Refractive Index (n = real depth / apparent depth)
concepts.explanation: For normal viewing from air into a medium, the refractive index equals the ratio of real depth to apparent depth.

concepts.name: Wave Speed Relation (v = fλ)
concepts.explanation: The speed of a wave equals its frequency multiplied by its wavelength.

concepts.name: Doppler Effect for Waves
concepts.explanation: The observed frequency changes due to relative motion of source and observer; for a medium with wave speed v, f' = f (v ± vo)/(v ∓ vs) depending on motion directions.

concepts.name: Fundamental Frequency of a Stretched String (f1 = (1/2L)√(T/μ))
concepts.explanation: The lowest resonant frequency of a string fixed at both ends depends on its length L, tension T, and linear mass density μ.

concepts.name: Resistors in Series
concepts.explanation: Equivalent resistance in series is the sum of resistances: R_eq = R1 + R2 + …

concepts.name: Resistors in Parallel
concepts.explanation: Equivalent resistance in parallel satisfies 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …

concepts.name: Parallel-Plate Capacitor
concepts.explanation: Capacitance of parallel plates given by C = εA/d for uniform dielectric.

concepts.name: Electric Field Strength
concepts.explanation: Force per unit charge, E = F/q; between parallel plates E ≈ V/d.

concepts.name: Joule's Law of Heating (W = I^2 R t)
concepts.explanation: Electrical energy converted to heat in a resistor is proportional to the square of current, resistance, and time.

concepts.name: Electric Power in Circuits (P = VI)
concepts.explanation: Power delivered or consumed in an electrical element equals the product of voltage and current; equivalent forms include P = I^2 R and P = V^2 / R.

concepts.name: Magnetic Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor (F = B I l sinθ)
concepts.explanation: A straight conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force proportional to current, length within the field, field strength, and the sine of the angle between current and field.

concepts.name: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge (F = q v B sinθ)
concepts.explanation: A charge moving through a magnetic field experiences a force proportional to charge, speed, magnetic field strength, and the sine of the angle between velocity and field.

concepts.name: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction (Induced EMF)
concepts.explanation: The induced emf in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the circuit, with direction given by Lenz's law.

concepts.name: Magnetic Flux (Φ = B A cosθ)
concepts.explanation: Magnetic flux through a surface equals the product of magnetic field, area, and the cosine of the angle between field and area normal.

concepts.name: RMS Values of AC Voltage and Current (Vrms, Irms)
concepts.explanation: Root-mean-square values define the DC-equivalent for power in AC circuits; for sinusoidal signals Vrms = Vpeak/√2 and Irms = Ipeak/√2.

concepts.name: Ideal Transformer Turns Ratio
concepts.explanation: In an ideal transformer, the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio (Vp/Vs = Np/Ns) and currents are inversely proportional (Ip/Is = Ns/Np), conserving power.

concepts.name: Wheatstone Bridge for Resistance Measurement
concepts.explanation: A bridge circuit that determines an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of a network to achieve a null detector reading.

concepts.name: Einstein’s Photoelectric Equation
concepts.explanation: Relates photon energy to the metal's work function and the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons: hf = Φ + 1/2 m v_max^2.

concepts.name: Work Function of a Metal
concepts.explanation: The minimum energy required to liberate an electron from a metal surface, appearing as Φ in the photoelectric equation.

concepts.name: Half-life and Decay Constant Relation
concepts.explanation: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is related to the decay constant by T1/2 = ln(2)/λ.
